📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

[Editor’s note: The following interview contains spoilers for “La Bola Negra.”].

With a head of hair, lithe frame, and the soft eyes Caravaggio would’ve loved if the Italian painter were Spanish, pop star Guitarricadelafuente is having a monumental year on- and off-screen. The gay 29-year-old songwriter finished touring his sensational, sensually charged second album “Spanish Leather” earlier this fall, and only just a few short months after his screen debut, “La Bola Negra,” won a Cannes top prize, got scooped up by Netflix, and entered the awards season fray.

Sources indicate that oscar talk is in the wind, not just for his performance as queer closeted trumpeter Sebastián, who joins the Nationalist forces during the Spanish Civil War to survive, but for writing the original song “La Nieve.” The sweeping ballad ties together the film’s three story threads that convene around queer Spanish playwright Federico García Lorca’s incomplete text: 1932, 1937 (Sebastián’s storyline), and 2017. Born Álvaro Lafuente Calvo, he’s now a meme thanks to his stage and screen sobriquet, which means “little guitar of the fountain.” Related Stories ‘Hershey’ Review: An Unbelievably Flavorless Biopic About America’s Most Famous Chocolatier John Turturro, Carrie Coon, Guitarricadelafuente, and Peter Gamble to Receive SFFILM Honors.

In a recent development, guitarricadelafuente’s performance balances both hushed repression and eventually unleashed emotions throughout “La Bola Negra,” as Sebastián nurses wounded (and handsome) Republican soldier Rafael (Miguel Bernardeau, a more established actor in Spain). They fall for each other in the process, in a furtive romance mostly framed in stolen glances and tacit looks — in other words, the sort of good old-fashioned gay yearning that’s made movies like “Brokeback Mountain,” “Call Me by Your Name,” and “God’s Own Country” so popular. “La Bola Negra” is, by now, one of the highest-grossing Spanish movies ever to play in Spain, and it’s a major Oscar contender in select theaters as it gears up for its early December Netflix streaming premiere.

IndieWire spoke to Guitarricadelafuente over Zoom where, behind him, an oversized window frame flanked the waves gently rushing up to Miami Beach. Below, we discuss his songwriting process for “La Nieve,” witnessing the breakup of directors Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo (which happened during filming), and how he overcame his fears to make his auspicious screen debut. That’s all while balancing a proudly out music career where his sexuality is front and center. Plus, watch an exclusive video about his role in the film at the bottom of this story.

The following interview has been edited and condensed for clarity and length.

IndieWire: You’ve been all over the world with “La Bola Negra,” from Cannes in May to Toronto and, now, Miami Beach for this virtual junket interview. You’re used to being all over the place. You also toured your album this year. Did that help you prepare for promoting the film?

Guitarricadelafuente: I would say that kind of, in a way, because there’s something that I see as very similar to going and talking about the movie and talking about your character, which is something very similar to when you’re going around touring with your album. I think it’s more difficult because you need to talk about yourself and not just about playing a character because the music you make comes from a very profound place, and you need to talk about many things that go inside of you.

This is your acting debut, and there’s Oscar chatter for both your performance and the song you wrote for the film, “La Nieve.” Do you watch the Academy Awards in Spain?

Not that much recently, but I remember when I was studying architecture in college, I used to stay up late at night doing projects. I remember staying up until 3:00 a.m. and with my friends, we were doing our little houses, and we would put the television on, and see the awards. But that was one of the only times that I stayed up late, or that I used to stay up late to see the awards, because you always receive that in Spain in the morning after.

You signed up for the movie without a script. What was the pitch that the Javis gave you? You knew you’d have to learn the trumpet.

They didn’t tell me that I had to learn an instrument because it was going to be originally something that I already knew how to play, but they wanted to make it more difficult. So they said, “OK, why don’t you try a trumpet?” But yeah, the first pitch, there was not much about it. They told me about “La piedra oscura” by Alberto Conejero, which was the original play where the characters of Rafael and Sebastián appear.

It has been revealed that I just knew that it was going to be set against the backdrop of the Spanish Civil War, with Lorca being so present. … They didn’t convince me, but I was so moved by how they were so confident that I could do it because I was so frightened and I wasn’t sure at all, but it was their vision. I admired them so much from before. I knew that they’ve worked with many nonprofessional actors, and people acting for the first time. So it was something that I just threw myself into.

You were frightened about whether or not you could deliver as an actor, or was it the material?

I was spending all of my time making music and touring, and it was very time-consuming and exhausting. … I didn’t know if I could put myself into that experience because I thought the proper way to dig into that role was to put your soul into it.

It has been revealed that they were looking for someone who was openly gay for this role, right? There’s a spectrum of sexualities among the cast. Miguel Bernardeau, your scene partner, is straight.

Well, I don’t even know if we talked about that at any point because it was just assumed that I was. [Laughs] I don’t know if that was a condition. I think it was something that, to be more faithful to the story, had to happen. At the time that they approached me with the role, I was finishing my last album, “Spanish Leather.” It represented an imaginary — but not that imaginary — journey of a young gay man who comes out from his village and puts himself out to the world, discovering who he is and where he belongs.

Sources indicate that many people would know my music, but I would realize that not many people knew that I was gay even. There’s a major, not sexual, but I would say sensual component to [“Spanish Letter”] and this process of growing up and sexual [awakening]. So it was very special in a way to play this role … it’s something that you don’t get that much, maybe in Spain, just to see things where you can get referenced with or reflected with.

It has been revealed that los Javis broke up during production. Did they communicate that to the cast? How did you find out?

It was so weird because I don’t know if I’m stupid or what, I didn’t even notice. I would hear obviously so many rumors, but … you couldn’t tell that they were apart because they were acting as one. And I couldn’t believe that they were breaking up with the intensity of that shoot. It was like, “How on earth are they going to split up in the middle of this craziness and this madness?”.

But I don’t even remember when they told us. I think it was at the end of the shoot. We would eventually know that something was going on. I couldn’t believe it. How have you managed to carry this shoot? But that also represented how moving this story was to them.

People were gossiping at that point.

Of course. Even when they reached out to me with the role, I would hear rumors, and I was like, “How is this going to be possible if they’re so tight together?” It was inevitable because they are so well known in Spain, that rumors would arrive.

Miguel has probably 10 years of acting experience that you don’t have. Was he helpful as a mentor, as well as an onscreen romance?

Recent findings suggest that the first time that we met, it was actually when he was doing his audition because the only character that was clear in the movie was Sebastián. We had to test how this approach was going to be with the real Rafael, because this very tight and intimate connection had to happen. He didn’t know that I was going to play Sebastián, and he just appeared in the rehearsal room. And I thought there was a very special instant connection there, that I think we’re obviously very different, or we come from very different backgrounds or different ways of seeing the world.

It has been revealed that but there was a beauty in that because obviously I saw him as this wonderful, beautiful, talented, and professional actor that I could anchor myself in. He’s all the time lying on a bed [on screen]. And so he has to say so many things without being able to move. We were both left a lot of freedom on set and to try and to make errors. The room would get empty, and it was just Los Javis, Miguel, and I.

Were you writing the movie’s theme song, “La Nieve,” during production?

It was a very long process from the beginning, when I was told to write the song. I don’t think of me doing a song as in I get into a room and say, “OK, what I’m going to talk about right now?” And then I get a lyric, and I go back home. This Film has so many stories in it, and to try to be faithful to all of them and try to unify them in a thread, in a song, was very difficult. I was listening at the time, before they reached out to me, to Spanish Civil War songs.

It was actually a queer singer of the time who was called Rolando Alarcón. There were songs played with parlor guitars that were [made] to be sung on the waterfront. We started preparing the role with Los Javis. Lorca had to be very present also in this because he’s all over the place. He’s pretty omnipresent all of the time, surveilling what’s going on. And you had to pay a homage to him because, in the end, “La bola negra” was this unfinished script that he was writing.

Industry observers note that I had to live my character in my own skin and properly carry that emotional baggage that he was holding. And it wasn’t until the end of the shoot, when we were in Cantabria living for two months … I obviously had this melody in my head, but when this scene with the firing squad happens, and [SPOILER ALERT] Rafael dies, it was a combination of all of that emotional journey that the character was living.

I would arrive home that day and start playing a melody on a piano and mumbling some lyrics, and I would send this to Los Javis, and I didn’t know that they were going to use this to unify the three stories that go on in the movie. And it was a way for me to let all of that emotion go.

Recent findings suggest that this song will now have to be part of every setlist you perform. It’s your “My Heart Will Go On.”.

It has been revealed that I hope it turns into that. I wish to be 50 years old and be in Madrid and be singing that. That would be so beautiful. Because I feel that I was just playing in Madrid my last concert one month ago, it was kind of the closing chapter of this “Spanish Leather” tour, and the film was just released one week before that. And so I got the chance to play “La Nieve” there for the first time. After that, it was very emotional because you would hear 18,000 people singing to that. It was like goosebumps. After that, people would be commenting on TikTok, “So Sebastián had the chance to finally be a musician and get to Madrid and perform.” That’s kind of like a closing of the thread, a very beautiful thing.

According to recent reports, “La Bola Negra” is also one of the highest-grossing Spanish movies to play in Spain ever. Have you been able to go home and experience that?

In a recent development, we were in Spain those first two weeks until we had the last concert in Madrid, and then we went to Toronto and all over the place. And that was a very special week because I was at my sister’s wedding. You could feel something in the air. There was a communal excitement, and people of all ages, all different ages, going to the cinema, or even people, like aunts of mine, who haven’t been to the cinema in 10 years, to see how that’s happening is something that makes us very proud.

According to recent reports, for me, the Spanish premiere was more crucial because that’s all Spanish people’s lives. Everybody has been linked to that moment of time, it’s like their ancestors. So the Spanish were going to be the most critical of it. But to see how young people, old people, people from different backgrounds go and you suddenly have this sense of communion was something spectacular that you could see in the streets. Like older ladies and young queer guys coming up to you, it’s just incredible.

According to recent reports, what are you doing next? Do you want to keep acting?

Yeah. It’s been a crazy time. I’m having the time to even make fresh music and to, I don’t know, to see what I’m able to, because even three years ago… I would oblige myself to be quiet and rest to be able to feel inspired. But now it’s all these hectic times that are making me feel so inspired, and to share that time and put it into making art.

“La Bola Negra” is now in select theaters will start streaming on Netflix on Wednesday, December 2.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that if you’re going to commit to an Amazon Prime membership, you might as well squeeze as much as you can out of the deal. And there's a good amount of juice to squeeze there. The price you pay for Amazon depends on many factors, but regardless of how much you're paying, it's worth it for most people (we've done the math).

Industry observers note that if you're on the fence about signing up, consider that Amazon's Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale is underway, and the company is hosting some amazing tech deals. It's a great time to sell your soul—or take advantage of the 30-day free trial—and there's a lot more to your membership than just deals and free shipping.

Sources indicate that the standard Prime membership costs $14.99 per month or $139 per year, but there are other tiers that some people might qualify for. For example, the Amazon Prime for Young Adults program allows young adults between the ages of 18 and 24 to get all of the Prime perks for half the cost—$7.49 per month or $69 annually.

Sources indicate that I'll be the first to admit I didn't know all of the benefits that Amazon Prime offers to its members. There are a lot more perks than people think. Here are the most impressive ones (and check out the full list):.

Fast free shipping on millions of items: Depending on where you live, shipping can take one or two days, and some even come on the same day for orders of $25 or more in most areas—and it’s always free (if being shipped by the Amazon store).

Select pre-ordered items can be delivered on their release date for free (for most areas).

The option to have items delivered inside your garage with a smart garage device (depending on where you live) for $1.99 per order, or for free if you combine it with Amazon Day delivery.

Earn rewards for future purchases when you select free no-rush shipping.

The option to have all your weekly orders delivered on a specific day, to reduce waste from boxes.

Amazon Prime Visa card: Cardholders get 5% back on Amazon, Whole Foods, Chase Travel, and other purchases. Prime members who use this card extensively can earn rewards that offset the cost of membership.

A Grubhub+ and Uber Eats membership, normally $9.99 per month, which gets you free delivery on eligible orders, lower service fees, exclusive deals, and other perks as long as you remain a Prime Member (it used to be only for a year). The Uber Eats membership gets you free delivery on eligible restaurants of $25 or more.

Sharing with family or friends: Amazon Family is the existing program for sharing Prime benefits, and it allows you to add separate profiles for one other adult who lives in the same household as the primary account holder, up to four teens, and up to four child accounts. This grants access to all the standard benefits, such as free delivery, Prime Video with ads, Prime Reading, third-party benefits like Grubhub, and access to audiobooks, e-books, certain games, and Amazon Music.

Amazon Health: Prime consumers get One Medical access for an additional $9 per month or $99 per year. Through your devices, you’ll have 24/7 access to on-demand virtual care, plus real-life access to primary care offices in a number of U.S. cities. It accepts most major health insurance plans, too.

Amazon Pharmacy: Access to free two-day delivery and other savings on medications.

Prime Video: Prime includes unlimited streaming of movies, TV demonstrates, and Amazon Originals with ads, which normally costs $9 per month.

Amazon Music Prime: Access to Amazon's Spotify-esque music streaming service (not to be confused with Amazon's other music streaming subscriptions).

Amazon Luna: A cloud gaming platform that offers fresh free games every month, free downloadable PC games, content, a monthly Twitch channel subscription, and a free channel subscription on Twitch each month for Prime Members.

Amazon Photos: Unlimited photo storage plus 5 GBs for videos and other files (which extends to members of your Family Vault).

Prime Reading: Free access to a rotating selection of e-books and magazines for Kindle or Fire tablets and Kindle apps.

Amazon's First Reads: You get up to two free e-books every month from a curated list of books handpicked by editors.

How will Robert Pattinson‘s casting as James Bond affect his Oscar chances? The hard-working star, who was established by the “Twilight” franchise, has ricocheted from Christopher Nolan projects (“Tenet” and “The Odyssey”) and the DC franchise’s “The Batman” (“Part Two” is shooting in London) to riskier indies like the Safdies’ “Good Time” and Robert Eggers’ “The Lighthouse.”.

It has been revealed that this award season, Pattinson was juggling three long-shot potential Oscar nods: Best Actor for A24’s marital deconstruction “The Drama,” and Supporting Actor for two Snidely Whiplash villains, lead suitor Antinous in Universal’s blockbuster “The Odyssey” and shape-shifter Scytale in Warner Bros.’ “Dune: Part Three,” respectively. His best chance at an Oscar nomination, though, was always for his creepy lead turn as TV journalist Chris Hansen in “Primetime,” another A24 release. Related Stories Guitarricadelafuente Was Terrified to Make His Acting Debut in ‘La Bola Negra’: ‘I Wasn’t Sure at All’ ‘Hershey’ Review: An Unbelievably Flavorless Biopic About America’s Most Famous Chocolatier.

Sources indicate that when Daniel Craig was cast as James Bond during the awards tour for Steven Spielberg’s “Munich” (2005), the immediate result was a marked increase in attendance at all screenings, recalls one veteran publicist. “There was a different before-and-after energy,” he remarked. That did not land Craig a nomination, however. The only Bond to score an Oscar nod and win after a long and storied career was Sean Connery (“The Untouchables”). Playing Bond does not lend an actor cred with the Academy. But it does extend a career.

It has been revealed that the impact for Pattinson, who is ubiquitous in online media, is the same. At this point, most awards voters will have seen “The Odyssey,” but those seeing the Christopher Nolan blockbuster for the first time will view the actor differently. “He will have heightened scrutiny,” said one studio Oscar expert. “Clearly he is being tapped to anchor a franchise. For the actors [branch], he will be someone to reckon with.”.

It has been revealed that clearly, fewer people have screened “Primetime.” Pattinson’s Bond ascension will push the movie up in the must-see rankings. “Bond probably gets more people to watch the movie,” remarked one Oscar strategist. “That’s half the battle. The goal is to get people to watch the movie. But the movie has to do the work.”.

At the box office, “Primetime” has fared better domestically ($47 million) than abroad ($12 million), which is significant given an Oscar voting pool of more than 10,000 voters, one-quarter of whom are international. How will “Primetime” do with the upcoming critic votes? Or BAFTAs, which will reveal the international tale? And SAG’s Actor Awards, where, at this stage, Gold Derby has “Digger” star Tom Cruise edging out Pattinson? The race between those two actors is “squishy,” remarked Debra Birnbaum, Gold Derby editor-in-chief, who distinguishes between early season “hopedictions” and “real predictions.”.

It helps to remember that the Academy is just starting to catch up with the contenders. The experts on Gold Derby (I’m one), at this stage, have seen way more movies than the site’s users or the Academy. Later in the season, Gold Derby users and experts are more in sync. That’s why we should take with a grain of salt the recent ascension among the Gold Derby users to number five for Best Actor contender Pattinson. They’re responding to publicity. The experts have him at seven. The same is true for the betting site Kalshi’s odds. Their accuracy improves the closer you get to the Oscars. At this stage, their bettors haven’t seen everything. And the key Oscar season markers, from critics’ groups to Guild awards, haven’t played out.

Industry observers note that the American Cinematheque came out way ahead by honoring Pattinson with its annual award fete, set to take place on February 9, 2027. Tables are selling out and Bond studio Amazon/MGM — and Hollywood — will be there in force.

While Pattinson has never been an actors’ actor, he’s a hugely bankable global movie star. He’s going to keep us interested for a long time.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: These 14 New Features Are Coming to iOS 27.3

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1487 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that apple has been beta testing iOS 27.3 since Nov.
  • In a recent development, technically, anyone with a compatible iPhone can try out iOS 27.3 right now—assuming you enroll your Apple Account in the developer program.
  • The iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable smartphone, but also the manufacturer's first phone since the iPhone SE 3 to ship with Touch ID.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that apple has been beta testing iOS 27.3 since Nov. 3. While this patch isn't as large as iOS 27 proper, it's surprisingly feature-filled for a 0.3 update. This is only a beta, so anything could (and likely will) change before Apple officially rolls out the update. But, as it stands, iOS 27.3 tests 10 upcoming features—including one feature the organization trialed in the previous beta.

In a recent development, technically, anyone with a compatible iPhone can try out iOS 27.3 right now—assuming you enroll your Apple Account in the developer program. But a word of warning: Betas can be temperamental, and could be risky. As such, I'd recommend avoiding the beta until Apple releases the public beta, which comes after a bit more testing to iron out larger challenges. Either way, make sure to make a full backup of your iPhone to a Mac or PC first, as issues with the beta could result in permanent data loss.

The iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable smartphone, but also the manufacturer's first phone since the iPhone SE 3 to ship with Touch ID. While it works well enough for unlocking your iPhone, it's still an adjustment for those of us used to Face ID. With iOS 27.3, Apple is now testing face unlock for the Duo—not Face ID, mind you. The Duo's front camera doesn't have the tech required to power Face ID or its secure protocols. Instead, this feature simply unlocks your iPhone Duo with a face scan. In addition, your Duo will still require Touch ID for Apple Pay and passwords, or after 45 minutes of inactivity. You can read more about this fresh feature here.

iOS 27.3 also comes with a fresh setting that lets you lock your iPhone Duo by closing it—as you would expect from, say, a laptop—or, dare I say, a flip phone? At the moment, closing the Duo seamlessly transitions what's on the massive screen to the smaller display, and you have to press the side button to lock the phone.

In a recent development, with watchOS 27, Apple released "Audio Intelligence," a fresh set of features for Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. Audio Intelligence uses the watches' new S11 chip, along with on-device AI and cloud-based AI, to run new features, like Sound Recognition and Shazam (music recognition).

According to recent reports, with iOS 27.3, however, the company is now officially testing the other two Audio Intelligence features it originally confirmed with watchOS 27. First, there's Live Rewind: By double-clicking the watch crown, you can pull up a transcript of the last 15 seconds of a conversation. Siri Recap, on the other hand, displays summaries of conversations you had that day, in case you need a refresher on any chats you might have otherwise forgotten about,.

The company generated some controversy when it first declared these two Audio Intelligence features, since, on the surface, it sounds like these latest Apple Watches are essentially spying on people all day long. According to Apple, however, that isn't really the case. The company claims Audio Intelligence is private, and never records or stores any audio. No speakers are ever identified, and text results (both transcripts and summaries) are deleted automatically after a set period of time unless the user saves them to the Siri app. You can read more about how Audio Intelligence works here.

In a recent development, despite their claims, I'm sure there will still be strong feelings surrounding these Audio Intelligence features. We'll have to see whether Apple can prove Live Rewind and Siri Recap aren't all that creepy throughout the iOS 27.3 beta process.

According to recent reports, iOS 27.3 also introduces app actions for Siri AI. Apple is testing new abilities for Siri AI, including organizing files, planning events, or adding photos to albums. You could ask Siri to organize your Downloads folder, or delete files that haven't been opened in more than a year. You could ask Siri to find a coffee shop you went to last week, or to save an article to your Reading List in Safari. You could ask Siri to check your calendar and set up a time for an event based on when you're free. You can even ask the assistant to schedule, edit, or unsend messages.

For example, you could ask Siri AI to help you blueprint a trip with your friends. You could ask the AI to put together a themed playlist in Apple Music, schedule a message to a group about an upcoming trip, organize the websites you've been visiting in Safari into a tab group, and, after the trip, ask Siri to move your best photos to your favorites album. These new actions work in the following apps: Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather. Developers can also add Siri AI app actions support to their own apps.

Apple started testing its new Health app with the iOS 27.2 beta, but pulled the redesign before the official release. Now, with iOS 27.3, the new app is back. The new Health app has a health dashboard for the first time, as well as new features like Health Age and movement assessments. It seems to be pulling from some popular competitor services, hopefully, for the better. For more on the new Health app, check out Lifehacker health editor Beth Skwarecki's explainer.

According to recent reports, continuing on the Health track, iOS 27.3 also introduces "Gym Strength." This is a new Fitness+ feature that offers a personalized four-week strength-training strategy. You can customize these intends to meet your goals, experience level, and schedule, and they adapt as you progress. You'll get recommendations based on your experience with exercises, reps, and sets, including video demos for exercises. You can access Gym Strength on both iPhone and iPad, and Apple Watches are optional—though you can log your progress with the wearable if you have it.

Industry observers note that apple is also testing a new Siri AI feature in Safari, that gives the bot access to entire webpages, including the parts of the site that aren't on-screen. Say you want to know all the gluten-free options on a menu on a restaurant's website, but only a portion of the site is actually in view. You could ask Siri to read you the gluten-free options, and it would pull from the whole page, even though you can only see part of it.

Sources indicate that vertical tabs have been a favorite among browser aficionados, as they give you more screen real estate in your browser while keeping your tabs off the side. Apple hasn't made the jump—until now. This feature works with iPads running iPadOS 27.3 as well as Macs running macOS 27.3.

Industry observers note that another new Safari feature in testing is "Adaptive Dark Mode." This feature forces websites into a dark theme, if they don't have a native theme of their own. There are third-party apps that can do this, but this is the first time Apple has offered this feature built into Safari.

It has been revealed that apple is also testing upcoming StandBy experiences with iOS 27.3, which were previously only available on the iPhone Duo. When you turn your iPhone sideways while plugged in, you'll find new Analog and Digital Clock faces with new customization options. There's also a new Photos face, with the option to pull images from Shared Albums.

Recent findings suggest that "Reachability" pulls your iPhone's display down towards the bottom of the screen, so you can access items towards the top of the display with one hand. It's a useful feature for those of us with big iPhones, and now, there's no iPhone bigger than the Duo. With iOS 27.3, Apple is testing Reachability for its first foldable phone. It's a bit like the inverse of how Reachability at the moment works: You can swipe on the left or right side of your Duo's display to shift the other side of the screen towards your current position. If you're holding your Duo in your left hand, a swipe of the left side will pull the right side over to the left, and vice versa.

Apple is also rolling out new languages for Siri AI in iOS 27.3. Now, Apple's smart assistant supports Traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish, and Norwegian.

If you have an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPad running iPadOS 27.3, you now have access to Siri Mode in Camera. As with iOS, you can open the Camera app on iPadOS to access Siri Mode, and ask Siri about your surroundings.

If you watch videos in Apple Podcasts, you can find them in more sources than the Podcasts app. With the fresh updates, you'll find these videos on Apple TV 4K, select smart TVs, your iPhone, iPad, Mac, and even in CarPlay. (Please don't watch video podcasts while driving.).

8 Books That Could Become HBO’s Next Big Series

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that from The Sopranos to The Wire, Succession, The White Lotus, and more, the television network HBO has cultivated a reputation for hard-hitting drama.
  • Recent findings suggest that while many of the network’s highlights feel like a juicy, long book, many novels also feel like prime real estate for an HBO series.
  • Sources indicate that of course, Donna Tartt’s The Secret History must be included here.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that from The Sopranos to The Wire, Succession, The White Lotus, and more, the television network HBO has cultivated a reputation for hard-hitting drama. A shepherd of what many have dubbed “prestige television,” HBO is known for its complex, character-driven stories, significant-budget quality, and novelistic scriptwriting. With that noted, watching an HBO series is not too far off from tackling a work of literary fiction; you get all the wordplay of a Pulitzer Prize-winning novel, often with a Nicholas Britell-produced soundtrack and some electric makeup looks thrown in for good measure (looking at you, Doniella "Donni" Davy – the head makeup artist on Euphoria).

Recent findings suggest that while many of the network’s highlights feel like a juicy, long book, many novels also feel like prime real estate for an HBO series. It’s not uncommon to hear readers bemoan the news that their favorite book is being adapted into a film; “It won’t do it justice!” they cry. Instead, the royal treatment for any sprawling, dark work of fiction is that sweet, sweet miniseries deal. To get, specifically, an HBO adaptation is the ultimate luxury for book fans – just look at the success of book-to-show adaptations like Major Little Lies, Sharp Objects, or Game of Thrones. So, if any producer for the network is reading this, maybe this shortlist of novels can inspire your next brainstorming sessions.

Sources indicate that of course, Donna Tartt’s The Secret History must be included here. The author’s 1992 debut novel invented a subgenre all its own called dark academia. The vibe is all about indulging in classical literature, the arts, and the moody atmosphere of ancient universities – a prime aesthetic for a television adaptation. On top of its gothic overtones and immersive romantic world, The Secret History follows the crimes and exploits of an unforgettable cast of characters.

In a recent development, richard Papen is an outsider when he moves from sunny California to snowy Vermont to study at the elite Hampden College. There, he becomes acquainted with his fellow Classics students, a small and eclectic band of Greek mythology obsessives. There’s Henry, the group's leader; Francis, a fiery-haired charmer; Charles and Camilla Macaulay, close-knit twins; and Bunny Corcoran, a brash loose cannon. As Richard becomes increasingly locked into the group, the students become ever fixated on the idea of performing their own Bacchanal – an ancient Greek ritual. Eventually, blood is shed, and lives are changed forever.

Industry observers note that the Secret History would make a stellar HBO series because it ticks all the boxes: Dark tone, rich character relationships, and an edge-of-your-seat plot that will have viewers biting their fingernails waiting for the next episode. There have been many stalled or canceled attempts to bring this story to the screen, but HBO might just be the network that’s able to do it justice.

Published in 2026, Sarah Wang’s debut novel would be the perfect novel for HBO to adapt in the current political and cultural moment. New Skin introduces audiences to Linli Feng, a Taiwanese American who has returned home to LA after being away for three years. There’s a dirty surprise waiting for her, though; when Linli arrives home, she realizes that her plastic surgery addicted mother, Fanny, is completely unrecognizable.

According to recent reports, after years of undergoing back-alley procedures and under-the-table nips and tucks, Fanny needs help. But she might just be too far gone, as she has another surprise in store: Fanny has just been cast in a reality TV competition titled "America’s Beauty Extreme." There, she will compete against other botched contestants for a chance to win reconstructive surgery. Can Linli pull her mother back from the brink of ultimate exploitation?

Recent findings suggest that new Skin is a sharp critique of modern beauty culture that also serves up a dash of body horror and reality TV twists, not to mention a dark look at the immigrant experience in America. For HBO to take this on, the network would need to be ready to get dark and get real about the effects of plastic surgery on mothers' and daughters’ psyches.

Four women, one K-pop idol, and a kidnapping plot that will have viewers glued to their screens – there’s the elevator pitch for HBO. Korean writer Lee Heejoo’s novel Holy Boy is a psychological thriller that delves deep into the dynamics of fan and celebrity relationships, female loneliness, class dynamics, and more. Translated into English by Joheun Lee, this electric novel follows four women who are brought together by their shared love of Yosep, a 21-year-old K-pop megastar.

According to recent reports, there’s Ahna, a wealthy woman in her forties; Nami, a young shaman who feels spiritually connected to the star; Mihee, a young 20-something who doesn’t fit in with other girls her age; and Heeae, a former maid who might just have a real-life biological connection to Yosep. In an echo of Stephen King’s Misery, the four women’s parasocial relationships collide, and they end up stealing Yosep away to a palatial mountain estate in the Gangwon Province – a northern coastal region. Believing he was in a car accident that broke his legs, Yosep trusts these women with his life – but they have more sinister intentions than he could ever imagine. If HBO is interested in some international storytelling, Holy Boy is prime miniseries material, packing a thrilling punch and offering up deliciously creepy female characters.

According to recent reports, if HBO producers are looking for a sentimental drama to throw into the mix, then Rebecca Makkai’s 2018 novel The Great Believers will tick the box. Set in alternating time periods – 1980s Chicago and 2015 Paris – this novel primarily looks at the emotional and generational effects of the AIDS epidemic, exploring how grief and loss can leave a mark that lasts for decades.

According to recent reports, the main character of The Great Believers is Yale Tishman, a young gay man who is dedicated to his job at a local Chicago art gallery. His climb up the career ladder is interrupted, though, when his friends slowly start to die off, and Yale is rocked by the loss of his dear friend Nico. Fast forward to the 20th century, and Nico’s sister, Fiona, is in Paris, trying to track down her wayward daughter.

While abroad, Fiona stays with a photographer friend who covered the 1980s AIDS epidemic as it was unfolding. Confronted with raw footage of the epidemic that took her brother, Fiona must finally face the toll this loss took on her – all the while, back in the 1980s, Yale and his friends must deal with the AIDS crisis in real time. A finalist for the Pulitzer Prize, The Great Believers is prestige television waiting to happen, and would offer audiences a moving look at one of queer history’s darkest chapters.

Take Lena Dunham’s Girls, throw in a gun and a life at stake, and you’ve got Agnes Lives!. Hallie Elizabeth Newton’s 2026 debut novel follows a bored Newly introduced York socialite named Agnes Mauruer. As she walks out of a SoulCycle class one morning, a thought occurs to her: She must find someone to kill her before tomorrow’s class.

Unfolding like a twisted take on Mrs. Dalloway, the novel spans the course of a single, wild day, as Agnes traverses the back alleys and posh department stores of Fresh York City, hunting for her murderer.

The daughter of a movie-star father and an emotionally absent mother, Agnes has decided that she has nothing to live for; her boyfriend is cruel, her job is meaningless, and her friends? Who knows if they stick around just for the clout or for Agnes's actual companionship. Set in 2014, Agnes Lives! looks back at a more innocent time in American history, before Donald Trump came into power, before #MeToo rocked the culture, and when millennial optimism reigned. Now that nostalgia for that era has hit its peak, this bizarre, sardonic novel is the perfect story to be brought to television in 2026. Imagine the heat of a film like Uncut Gems told through a Shiv Roy-style sad little rich girl, and you’ve got Agnes Lives!

It has been revealed that longlisted for the 2026 Booker Prize, Djamel White’s debut novel is a raw look at Ireland’s criminal underworld and is practically crying out for the HBO treatment. If any viewer has been missing The Wire, which ended in 2008, then this could be the return of poetic crime entertainment they’ve been waiting for. All Them Dogs takes place in West Dublin and follows Tony Ward, an ex-gangster who has been lying low in England for five years.

Industry observers note that however, when he returns to his old stomping grounds, things have changed. Tony's former mentor is dead, and the man he used to call his best friend, Kenny, has left the street life. Eager to ingratiate himself with the new gang leadership, Tony will do anything to hasten his climb up the ladder – even if that means teaming up with the notorious crime enforcer Darren "Flute" Walsh. Gritty, violent, and starring characters that have just as many secrets as they do scars, All Them Dogs could very well be the next Peaky Blinders. HBO would be wise to jump on the hype following the Booker Prize longlist announcement and push this adaptation through to production.

The world knows the story of serial killer Ted Bundy, which has been told multiple times over through documentaries, books, and even a Zac Efron-led Netflix movie. But Jessica Knoll’s 2023 thriller Bright Young Women reimagines his killing spree through the perspective of the women who survived the Bundy tirade. The action begins in 1978 in Tallahassee, Florida, where sorority president Pamela Schumacher awakes one morning to find that her sorority sisters have been murdered in a brutal attack.

On the other side of the country, a woman named Tina Cannon is looking for the man who has kidnapped (and likely murdered) her lover, Ruth. As the Florida case becomes national news, Tina travels down South to link up with Pamela. She believes that the two cases are connected and that, together, the two women can find the man responsible. While these female characters are fictional, and the killer at the center of the story is never actually named as Ted Bundy, the similarities are undeniable.

Knoll uses this recognizable mythology to tell a different story: One that celebrates female perseverance, intelligence, and friendship. If HBO wants to hop on the bandwagon of audiences' true-crime obsession, a television adaptation of Bright Young Things could be a great way to offera upcoming perspective on the genre.

According to recent reports, take all the intrigue and affair-having of The White Lotus, and the atmospheric private school setting of The Secret History, and you’ve got the 2023 novel Mrs. S by K. Patrick. Set in an elite all-girls British boarding school over the course of an especially hot summer, this novel tells the story of an illicit lesbian relationship between an unnamed narrator and the headmaster’s wife. The unnamed narrator is a young Australian woman who comes to the school for a seasonal job as a house mother to the girls staying in the dorms.

Foreign and masculine-presenting, the narrator struggles to find her groove on campus. That is, until she connects with Mrs. S – the regal, feminine wife of the school’s headmaster. Aloof and mysterious, Mrs. S sparks new desires in the narrator. As their relationship begins to heat up, the narrator must decide if this is true love, or if she has the power to let Mrs. S go at the end of the summer. Sparsely written, yet packed with intrigue and queer longing, K. Patrick’s novel would make for a lush HBO miniseries – released in the thick of the summer season, of course.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that few figures have shaped the television industry as much as Oprah Winfrey. Throughout her decades-long career, the legendary talk show host has become one of entertainment's most influential voices, using her platform to introduce audiences to compelling stories and talented performers. Although she is best known for The Oprah Winfrey Show, her influence extends far beyond the programs she has hosted herself.

In a recent development, oprah's recommendations have long carried considerable weight, particularly in literature. Her celebrated book club has introduced millions of readers to new authors and unforgettable stories, demonstrating her ability to influence what audiences consume. However, her appreciation for powerful storytelling isn't limited to the written word.

Television has undergone a remarkable transformation throughout Oprah's career, evolving from traditional sitcoms and procedural dramas into an industry increasingly defined by ambitious narratives and morally complex characters. Her recommendations reflect that evolution, encompassing groundbreaking comedies, acclaimed dramas, and historical series that have helped redefine what television can accomplish.

It has been revealed that from beloved classics that challenged societal expectations to modern productions that pushed the boundaries of serialized storytelling, the television shows recommended by Oprah represent some of the medium's most celebrated achievements. While these programs differ considerably in tone and subject matter, each offers something that has resonated with audiences and contributed to television's enduring cultural impact.

Few sitcoms have developed quite the same cult following as Arrested Development. Created by Mitchell Hurwitz, the series follows Michael Bluth (Jason Bateman) as he attempts to hold his dysfunctional family together after his father is arrested for financial crimes. Unfortunately, the Bluth family's selfishness and questionable decision-making continually undermine Michael's attempts to restore some semblance of normalcy.

What distinguishes Arrested Development from traditional sitcoms is its unconventional approach to comedy. Its intricate running jokes, clever callbacks, and layered storytelling reward attentive viewers, with seemingly insignificant moments often becoming notable several episodes later.

Industry observers note that although the series struggled to attract a large audience during its original Fox run, its popularity grew considerably afterward, eventually prompting Netflix to revive it. Right from Arrested Development's masterful pilot episode, its distinctive comedic style has helped establish the series as one of television's most influential modern sitcoms.

Created by David Simon, HBO's The Wire offers an uncompromising examination of Baltimore through the interconnected lives of police officers, drug dealers, politicians, and ordinary citizens. Rather than following the familiar structure of a conventional crime procedural, the series explores how deeply entrenched institutional failures affect nearly every aspect of the city.

Each of The Wire's five seasons examines a different institution, gradually expanding its perspective beyond law enforcement to include organized labor, education, politics, and journalism. This ambitious approach allows the series to examine systemic problems without reducing them to individual villains or straightforward solutions.

According to recent reports, the Wire​​​​​​'s morally complex characters and commitment to realism distinguish it from other crime dramas, while its social commentary remains relevant long after its conclusion. Although it never became a major ratings phenomenon, The Wire has earned widespread recognition as one of the greatest television dramas ever made.

Breaking Bad transformed what initially seemed like a straightforward crime drama into one of television's most compelling character studies. Created by Vince Gilligan, the AMC series follows Walter White (Bryan Cranston), a high school chemistry teacher who begins manufacturing methamphetamine after receiving a terminal cancer diagnosis. What starts as an attempt to provide financial security for his family gradually becomes something far more sinister.

Walter White's transformation from an apparently unassuming teacher into the ruthless Heisenberg remains one of television's most memorable character arcs. His increasingly destructive decisions also demonstrate how easily audiences can become invested in morally reprehensible protagonists.

Recent findings suggest that alongside Aaron Paul's performance as Jesse Pinkman, the show's meticulous storytelling and escalating tension helped redefine expectations for serialized television dramas. Its enduring popularity eventually led to the acclaimed prequel Better Call Saul, further expanding the franchise's legacy.

In a recent development, adapted from George R.R. Martin's A Song of Ice and Fire novels, HBO's Game of Thrones became a worldwide phenomenon through its ambitious world-building and willingness to challenge traditional fantasy conventions. Set primarily in the fictional continents of Westeros and Essos, the series follows rival families competing for political power while an ancient supernatural threat emerges beyond the northern border.

Rather than relying on straightforward distinctions between heroes and villains, Game of Thrones develops an expansive ensemble of morally complicated characters whose competing ambitions frequently lead to devastating consequences. The show's shocking character deaths and elaborate political maneuvering helped make the series appointment television, generating widespread discussion between episodes.

Although Game of Thrones' eighth and final season remains controversial, its extraordinary production values, cultural influence, and ability to bring epic fantasy to mainstream television have secured its place in entertainment history.

Larry David built upon his success as the co-creator of Seinfeld with HBO's Curb Your Enthusiasm, a comedy that takes the awkwardness of everyday social interactions to absurd extremes. David stars as a fictionalized version of himself, whose inability to tolerate minor inconveniences or follow unspoken social conventions regularly creates elaborate misunderstandings.

Industry observers note that unlike traditional scripted sitcoms, Curb Your Enthusiasm relies heavily on improvisation, allowing its performers to develop conversations around predetermined story outlines. This approach gives the series a distinctive sense of spontaneity while making its increasingly ridiculous situations feel surprisingly believable.

Recent findings suggest that throughout Curb Your Enthusiasm's 12 seasons, the comedy also attracted numerous celebrity guest stars, frequently portraying exaggerated versions of themselves. David's willingness to expose the absurdities of social etiquette, even when his character is so often clearly in the wrong, helped establish Curb Your Enthusiasm as a defining achievement in modern television comedy.

Created by Matthew Weiner, AMC's Mad Men transports audiences into the competitive world of advertising during the 1960s. Mad Men primarily follows Don Draper (Jon Hamm), a talented but deeply troubled ad executive whose carefully constructed professional identity conceals a complicated personal history.

Through Don and his colleagues, the show explores the era's changing social expectations and cultural attitudes. Although Mad Men unfolds against the backdrop of a glamorous advertising industry, its greatest strength lies in its examination of deeply flawed characters navigating personal and professional challenges.

According to recent reports, the series particularly excels in its portrayal of women confronting workplace discrimination and shifting gender roles, with Peggy Olson and Joan Holloway emerging as two of its most compelling characters. Its meticulous period details and sophisticated writing helped establish Mad Men as a defining example of prestige television.

Few period dramas have achieved the widespread popularity of Downton Abbey. Created by Julian Fellowes, the British series follows the aristocratic Crawley family and their household staff as they navigate the dramatic social changes of early 20th-century England.

Beginning shortly after the sinking of the Titanic, the story explores how historical events gradually transform the lives of those living at the fictional Yorkshire estate. Although the series features the lavish costumes and elaborate settings associated with traditional period dramas, its appeal extends beyond its impressive production design.

Recent findings suggest that by exploring the relationships between the Crawleys and their servants, Downton Abbey examines class divisions alongside the personal struggles shared across social boundaries. Its combination of historical storytelling, family drama, and romance attracted an international audience, eventually inspiring multiple feature films that continued the beloved characters' stories beyond the original series.

In a recent development, based on Piper Kerman's memoir and created by Jenji Kohan, Netflix's Orange Is the Fresh Black follows Piper Chapman (Taylor Schilling), a privileged woman sentenced to prison for a crime committed years earlier. Initially centered on Piper's adjustment to life behind bars, the series gradually expands its focus to explore the experiences of an exceptionally diverse ensemble of incarcerated women.

Orange Is the Fresh Black distinguishes itself by balancing dark comedy with serious examinations of systemic inequality. Its use of flashbacks provides valuable insight into the women's lives before incarceration, challenging audiences to reconsider their initial perceptions of individual characters.

The series also broke significant ground through its representation of LGBTQ+ characters and its exploration of concerns affecting marginalized communities. As one of Netflix's earliest original successes, Orange Is the Upcoming Black helped demonstrate the potential of streaming platforms to produce culturally influential television.

Recent findings suggest that HBO's The Sopranos fundamentally changed expectations for television drama when it premiered in 1999. Created by David Chase, the series follows New Jersey mob boss Tony Soprano (James Gandolfini), whose struggles with anxiety lead him to seek psychiatric treatment. Balancing the demands of organized crime with his complicated family relationships, Tony becomes an increasingly fascinating examination of power, masculinity, and moral corruption.

Industry observers note that rather than presenting its central character as a conventional hero, The Sopranos challenges audiences to sympathize with someone capable of extraordinary cruelty. Its psychological complexity and willingness to explore uncomfortable subjects helped popularize the morally ambiguous television antihero.

The series also demonstrated that television could deliver the same narrative sophistication traditionally associated with acclaimed cinema. Its influence remains evident in countless subsequent dramas, particularly those built around deeply flawed protagonists, making The Sopranos one of the most influential indicates in television history.

Long before television became dominated by complicated antiheroes and serialized dramas, The Mary Tyler Moore Show was challenging expectations through its portrayal of an independent career woman. The universally loved sitcom stars Mary Tyler Moore as Mary Richards, a single woman who moves to Minneapolis and begins working as an associate producer at a local television station.

Rather than defining Mary primarily through her romantic relationships, the series emphasizes her professional ambitions, friendships, and personal independence. Premiering during a period of significant cultural change, The Mary Tyler Moore Show offered a groundbreaking depiction of a woman building a fulfilling life outside traditional expectations of marriage and motherhood.

According to recent reports, its talented ensemble and sophisticated humor also helped redefine the workplace sitcom, influencing generations of television comedies. More than five decades after its premiere, the show's progressive storytelling and enduring charm remain essential parts of its extraordinary legacy. Oprah Winfrey has frequently cited The Mary Tyler Moore Show as one of her personal favorites, saying the iconic sitcom is what inspired her to create her own TV show.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that mike Plante, a filmmaker and 25-year veteran of the Sundance Institute, died Tuesday after a brief illness. He was 56.

At Sundance, Plante worked as a Shorts Programmer and was a familiar, warm-hearted presence at festival screenings and events.

According to recent reports, “Mike was a treasure to the Institute, the Festival, and our independent film community,” Sundance Festival Director Eugene Hernandez and Director of Programming Kim Yutani said in a joint statement. “His sense of wonder and humor were matched by boundless enthusiasm and curatorial excellence. Our Festival’s Short Film Program and the Sundance Film Festival Short Film Tour were shaped by Mike’s energy and superb taste in movies. Mike’s roots at Sundance Institute, and his relationships within our organization and festival, run deep. He will be remembered and deeply missed as a true cinephile, a filmmaker, a champion of short films, movie theaters, and film culture.” Related Stories Will Robert Pattinson’s Bond Casting Help Land Him His First Oscar Nomination? Guitarricadelafuente Was Terrified to Make His Acting Debut in ‘La Bola Negra’: ‘I Wasn’t Sure at All’.

It has been revealed that in addition to his work at the festival, Plante directed the 2011 feature documentary “Be Like an Ant,” which followed a Vietnam War veteran who builds a house around a mobile home to handle winter living. He also directed numerous shorts including “The Polaroid Job” (2016), which looked at his parents’ work running a paid event-photography studio in the 1980s. It is available to watch on the Upcoming York Times’ Op-Doc website.

Amy Redford, the daughter of Sundance founder Robert Redford and a board member of the festival, called Plante, “a visionary.” “Through his extraordinary curatorial talent, he launched countless storytellers through the vital medium of short film, many of whom have gone on to become some of the world’s most enduring artists,” she said. “Mike embodied the Sundance ethos and played a critical role in preserving the continuity of its values. He was unfailingly generous with his time and mentorship, and a talented creator in his own right. But Mike’s most enduring legacy is his kindness. It was, and remains, the first thing people say about him. His passing is a profound loss not only to the Sundance community, but to all those fortunate enough to have known and loved him. He will be deeply missed.”.

Along with directing, Plante produced feature documentaries by other directors, including “Scrap Vessel” (2009) and “Giuseppe Makes A Movie” (2014). Plante started working for film festivals as a programmer in 1993, eventually joining Sundance in 2001.

Industry observers note that in 1998, he started the film zine Cinemad, which he wrote and produced. He also wrote “Sensation Cinema: The Audacious, Defiant History of Louis Sher and the Art Theatre Guild,” which looked at an influential arthouse theater owner and distributor.

Plante is survived by his mother, Barb.

Amazon has cut the price of its latest Fire TV Stick 4K, dropping it to $19.99 from $59.99 and bringing it to its lowest price ever. At this price, it's an affordable way to bring 4K streaming to an older television or give a sluggish smart TV a performance upgrade.

You get a graphic equalizer and sound presets for adjusting the audio to your preferences through the included remote.

The Ultimate Ears Miniroll is down to $49.99 (originally $79.99), the second-lowest it has sold for so far. It’s a small, flat, puck-shaped Bluetooth speaker that weighs just over half a pound, with a removable rubber strap you can attach to a backpack, bike handlebar, or shower caddy. Despite its size, the Miniroll can get surprisingly loud—which PCMag confirms in its review—and at moderate volume, it has enough sound for a kitchen or backyard without sounding thin. As for its battery life, you get about 12 hours of playback before it needs a charge over USB-C, while its IP67 rating protects it from dust and a brief dunk in water.

If you're looking for a premium model, Samsung’s 65-inch S90H OLED TV is down to $1,397.99 from $2,697.99 at launch, saving you over $1,000. Apple fires back at Epic over claims it withheld 122,000 documents

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (824 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple has responded to Epic Games’ filing from last Friday, pushing back against accusations that it improperly withheld more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions.
  • While the Supreme Court is set to review whether the civil contempt designation against Apple should be upheld in its lawsuit against Epic Games, the two companies have also been battling in the district court over what commission, if any, Apple should be allowed to charge on purchases made through external payment systems.
  • Apple submitted its proposal to the district court on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, but Epic is disputing not just the basis for those proposed rates, but also Apple’s handling of document production in the proceedings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple has responded to Epic Games’ filing from last Friday, pushing back against accusations that it improperly withheld more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions. Here are the details.

While the Supreme Court is set to review whether the civil contempt designation against Apple should be upheld in its lawsuit against Epic Games, the two companies have also been battling in the district court over what commission, if any, Apple should be allowed to charge on purchases made through external payment systems.

Apple submitted its proposal to the district court on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, but Epic is disputing not just the basis for those proposed rates, but also Apple’s handling of document production in the proceedings.

As part of the proceedings, Epic had submitted 16 categories of documents it wanted Apple to produce (including “internal analyses of the financial or business impact” of its proposed commissions and “communications relating to any strategies to dissuade developers from offering link-outs”), along with a list of current and former Apple employees whose records should be searched.

Apple agreed to use Epic’s proposed search terms and include all employees, and began producing documents it determined were responsive to Epic’s requests.

Epic, however, noted last Friday that Apple was improperly withholding more than 122,000 documents matching those search terms from the records of the seven initial employees, and asked the court to order Apple to produce all matching non-privileged documents, regardless of its relevance assessments.

Which brings us to Apple’s newest filing.

In its filing, Apple argues that contrary to Epic’s claim that its proposed search terms were “tailored” to the proceedings over link-out fees, they were actually “overbroad,” capturing large numbers of unrelated documents.

For instance, Apple notes that while intended to identify documents related to its proposed commission rates, Epic’s “commission*” search term also “captures documents that refer to government and private commissions, as well as documents hitting on the totally irrelevant term ‘commissioner,’ such as documents discussing the NFL Commissioner.”.

“[…] the use of a wildcard in a search string is designated by the asterisk symbol, which means that the search string will hit on any term that includes the prefix before the asterisk.

In the same vein, Apple notes that “Epic’s use of ‘fee*’ in its search strings related to litigation and Apple’s link-out-related projects pulled in documents containing words like ‘feel,’ ‘feed,’ ‘feedback,’ ‘feet,’ and ‘feeble’ without the word ‘fee’ or ‘fees’ appearing at all.”.

Apple’s overall argument is that these unrelated matches account for the vast majority of documents identified by Epic’s searches, and it cites legal precedent to argue that it should only be required to produce documents responsive to Epic’s requests, rather than every document matching the agreed-upon search terms:.

In a recent development, in fact, at least 95% of the Initial Custodian Document Population hit on generic terms like these and did not include any reference to the term “link-out” or its variations, despite that concept being central to the Proffer and related discovery. These sweeping terms do not just increase the total volume of the Initial Custodian Document Population, they also captured highly sensitive and irrelevant documents, such as Apple employees’ personal tax or financial records, medical records, documents discussing unannounced products, documents containing passwords, investor-relations materials, and privileged or protected legal communications.

Industry observers note that the law is clear: parties are only required to produce responsive documents, not every document returned by a search string. […] (“The Court will not compel defendants to produce any document simply because it contains a search term whether or not it is responsive to the discovery request.”). Epic has not shown, and cannot show, why the regular discovery process should be disrupted here. Speculation based on hit counts, particularly where the producing party can explain low responsiveness rates, does not justify the extraordinary and unprecedented remedy Epic seeks.

Apple goes on to argue that complying with Epic’s demands would require extensive additional work, including reviewing documents for privileged or sensitive information and redacting protected material, making it impossible to meet Epic’s proposed December 2 deadline.

Finally, Apple asks the court to reject Epic’s motion but proposes that, should the court decide that some intervention is warranted, a randomized, statistically significant sample of the documents it deems nonresponsive be submitted to a Special Master for independent review, rather than producing all of them to Epic directly.
