#85574. Breaking: Movie Theaters in 2026: Filmmakers and Exhibitors on What’s Good, What’s Bad, and What’s Changing

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 23m • 📚 Deep Dive (4647 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Indiewire ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Movie Theaters in 2026: Filmmakers and Exhibitors on What’s Good, What’s Bad, and What’s Changing

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4647 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Indiewire

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In 1948, movie studios held a monopoly in entertainment, owning the means of producing and distributing films, and the theaters themselves.
  • Sources indicate that 70 years later, movie studios again faced the possibility of giving up on exhibition.
  • “COVID allowed people to acknowledge their inner recluse,” Tim League, the co-founder and former CEO of Alamo Drafthouse, told IndieWire.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In 1948, movie studios held a monopoly in entertainment, owning the means of producing and distributing films, and the theaters themselves. The 1948 Paramount Decrees (named after the studio that pioneered the vertical integration) required studios to give up one of the three options. They decided to give up exhibition. The choice was easy: With low margins on ticket sales and the need to constantly bring audiences in, who wanted to run a movie theater?

Sources indicate that 70 years later, movie studios again faced the possibility of giving up on exhibition. The rise of streaming was mentioned to bring about the end of theaters as we know them. But the COVID-19 pandemic brought exhibition to its closest brink of extinction yet. Related Stories Mike Plante, Sundance Film Festival Shorts Programmer, Dies at 56 Will Robert Pattinson’s Bond Casting Help Land Him His First Oscar Nomination?

“COVID allowed people to acknowledge their inner recluse,” Tim League, the co-founder and former CEO of Alamo Drafthouse, told IndieWire.

Sources indicate that after the global pandemic, lockdown protocols forced movie theaters to close for months. The luxury theater chain Arclight shuttered all its locations within weeks. Locations closed at a variety of companies, including Alamo Drafthouse. Some theaters survived off of private rentals. Even as theaters slowly reopened, COVID protocols required leaving some seats empty, meaning not all tickets could be sold.

“I think there was no right move,” League added. “We laid most of our people off. We spent a lot of energy trying to build up a TVOD streaming platform which didn’t entirely work for a lot of reasons… And so we went through bankruptcy, and it was rough. We just ran out of money.”.

In a recent development, “There really was no strategy,” remarked Greg Laemmle, owner of the California-based independent theater chain Laemmle Theatres. Since Los Angeles did not allow private rentals, the tech giant stayed afloat via concessions, pop-up events, and some virtual cinema opportunities. “It was all just trying to understand how we can maintain contact.”.

Exhibition became such an unappetizing business that many of those who jumped on board the irony-fueled GameStop stock inflation of 2021 also bought shares of AMC Theatres, bringing the firm to an all-time high in valuation.

But years later, the theater market is experiencing a rebirth. Driven by new theater operators and new kinds of theatrical experiences, the contemporary exhibition landscape looks very different from 10 years ago.

Sources indicate that theater operators paint a picture of an industry that is no longer weathering a storm. Instead, they reveal the trends driving theaters to thrive and the issues with the model that won’t seem to die.

According to recent reports, the first high-profile artist-led theater acquisition was Quentin Tarantino’s purchase of the Latest Beverly Cinema in Los Angeles. The director had previously helped fund his childhood theater to keep it afloat before buying the cinema outright and taking over as programmer in 2014. The purchase of the 300-seat New Beverly was partly fueled by Tarantino’s desire to preserve what the digital era sought to make extinct: celluloid projection. Since the director’s acquisition, the theater proudly boasts that it screens only on film, usually 35mm.

Tarantino declined to comment on this story.

Sources indicate that A few years later, COVID-19 brought a newly introduced threat to movie theaters. A similar mission-driven attitude took hold in a new crop of directors and artists: to protect not just how movies are screened, but to ensure audiences can still see them in communal spaces.

Independent film director Kevin Smith bought his hometown theater in Atlantic Highlands, Newly introduced Jersey, in 2024. The Atlantic Twin Cinema was a five-screen multiplex Smith grew up going to, housed in a building over 100 years old. But over time, nearby multiplexes threatened to drive the theater out of business. When Smith’s friend Ernie O’Donnell told him the theater would be torn down to build condos, he resolved to help save it.

“Anything I ever learned about myself I never learned in a classroom, and I certainly didn’t learn it sitting in a church,” Smith told IndieWire. “But mostly everything I know about myself I learned sitting in the darkness of that theater, looking up at the great white mirror and seeing life reflected back at me.”.

Industry observers note that smith invested $450,000 and partnered with several friends to buy the theater, rebranding it as Smodcastle Cinemas. While he mostly lives in Los Angeles, Smith travels to Jersey every month to work on the theater.

Smith described how the finances of owning a theater in a small town may not always reflect larger box office trends. “Avatar: The Way of Water” opened in 2024 and eventually grossed over $2 billion, making it one of the most successful films in history. But at Smodcastle Cinemas, they only sold 12 tickets opening weekend.

At Smodcastle, the theater has leaned into what Smith calls “The business of Kevin Smith.” This includes Q&As of his films featuring Smith and his collaborators like Justin Long for a “Tusk” screening, and Tracy Morgan for the 15th anniversary of “Cop Out.” The theater started a film festival to help showcase local New Jersey cinema. Smith was working on selling a reality show about the theater’s day-to-day operations, similar to the seven-season run of “Comic Book Men” filmed inside the comic shop he owns, but said progress has stalled.

“I love calling up Ernie and being like, ‘How many seats [have we sold] so far?’ And he’ll be like ‘120 out of 230,’ and I’m like, ‘All right man, I gotta put 90 more asses in seats. Let me see if I can jump on a radio show… go over to Manhattan and jump on “Good Day New York” and try to get the word out,’” Smith explained. “It’s fun, but it is definitely fucking work. I have a feeling Quentin don’t work nearly as fucking hard at his theater.”.

Smith elaborated on the work it takes to keep the theater running, “We all got together and saved the theater, man. But it was the worst financial fucking decision I ever made,” Smith said. “Owning a movie theater in the 21st-century post-COVID [world], it’s a dicey proposition at best… We became a nonprofit theater because the movie theater’s never going into fucking profit.”.

In a recent development, the nonprofit model has become an increasingly popular option for keeping theaters alive. In 2012, Los Angeles video rental store Vidiots transitioned to a nonprofit to stay afloat, recasting its mission around film preservation, protection, and education. The organization later received heavy support from Megan Ellison’s Annapurna Pictures, which kept the company running for two years after it shuttered its store in 2017.

Recent findings suggest that “If you go across the country, you’re seeing a real boom in nonprofit or community-supported movie theaters,” noted Laemmle. He highlighted the Tasveer Film Center in Seattle, which reopened the former Ark Lodge Cinemas in 2025 due to support from a local nonprofit that had run a South Asian film festival.

“Why not form a community organization that augments ticket sales with other sources of revenue, or that can take advantage of their not-for-profit status and do the enhanced kind of programming that you can’t do at a for-profit business?” said Laemmle.

According to recent reports, the high costs of running a movie theater are also evident in one of the latest major theater purchases by an artist. Director Jason Reitman led a group of 30 filmmakers — including Christopher Nolan, Guillermo del Toro, Steven Spielberg, and Chloé Zhao — to purchase the historic Village Theater in Westwood, Los Angeles, in 2024. Since rebranding as Directors Village, the theater has partnered with the film nonprofit American Cinematheque, which will handle its programming.

According to recent reports, the $12 million acquisition in 2024 rescued the historic theater after its lease with its former owner expired. The filmmakers will pour an additional $25 million into renovating the theater, which was open for programming in summer 2026 but closed in October and will reopen in 2027. The project required an alleged six-figure minimum buy-in from the artists involved.

Jason Reitman declined to comment through a representative, citing that it is too early to discuss plans for the theater’s renovation. American Cinematheque did not respond to requests for comment.

Jason Reitman and Co. also looked into purchasing the adjacent Bruin Theater but were ultimately deterred by the extensive cost of renovations, as previously reported by IndieWire.

The list of artists owning theaters is only growing. Kristen Stewart purchased the historic Highland Theatre in Los Angeles in February 2026 and plans to restore the space into a hub for the L.A. film community. Tarantino bought a second LA theater, the Vista, in 2021. Martin Scorsese, Ethan Hawke, and Frances McDormand joined the advisory board of the Upper West Side Cinema Center to turn the former Metro Theater on Broadway in Fresh York City into a five-screen arthouse theater, funded by New York City grants and donors like the Kate Capshaw and Steven Spielberg Hearthland Foundation.

Industry observers note that the trend highlights a fresh form of altruism by creatives seeking to keep theaters alive. But even if the business isn’t financially valuable, there is an argument for artists to be seen as patrons of their craft. “As more and more movie theaters start closing down, every filmmaker is from somewhere, and every filmmaker has their hometown theater,” said Smith. “And if you have a degree of success where you’ve got some side hustle loot and whatnot, what a great way to spend your money.”.

Industry observers note that in 2019, the Department of Justice marked the Paramount Decrees for termination, citing changes in the studio system structure and film market that rendered the law obsolete. In August 2020, while most theaters in the United States were shuttered, the Department of Justice ended the decree.

In November 2019, Netflix announced it would lease Latest York City’s historic Paris Theater, three months after a notice of closure was posted. In May 2020, the streamer bought the closed Egyptian Theatre in Hollywood to be co-programmed between the studio and its previous operator, American Cinematheque. In October 2021, Netflix also announced it would take over the lease of the Bay Theater in the Pacific Palisades.

In a recent development, these acquisitions had a touch of irony considering Netflix made a name for itself by rejecting theatrical exhibition. The streamer did not abide by the then-standard 90-day exhibition window before making its films available on the service. The Academy Awards require week-long theatrical runs to make films eligible for awards. Major chains like AMC Theatres and Regal Cinemas refused to show Netflix films (and still do on occasion; Regal and Cinemark recently unveiled they will not screen “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” due to the shortened theatrical window). But just as it became legal for Netflix to enter the theater market, it did. By becoming an exhibitor, it no longer needed major theaters to show its films.

“Netflix needs screens in the L.A. and New York market,” said James Huntsman, the co-founder of distribution company Blue Fox Entertainment Group, which purchased two former iPic theaters in June 2026. “I don’t care if you are Netflix, it’s really hard to get a screen in both of those two markets… So if you’re Netflix and you have six movies that are coming out between October and December and they all need qualifying runs of seven days, full runs in both markets, now you start seeing why they’re interested in screens.”.

Industry observers note that amazon Studios opened The Culver Theater — the former Culver City Arclight location, which shuttered in March 2020 after the organization went bankrupt due to closures from the COVID-19 pandemic — in December 2022. The theater screens a mix of latest releases, repertory screenings, and hosts premieres for Amazon MGM Studios’ television reveals and movies.

Sources indicate that in October 2026, Paramount Pictures revealed it took over the lease for the Bay Theater, which has been closed since the 2025 Palisades fires. The upcoming theater, opened in November 2026 and operated by The Lot, similarly offers first-run theatrical releases from all studios, along with dine-in food.

According to recent reports, “We’ll see if it really develops into anything more than just a novelty for them,” said Laemmle about studios purchasing individual theaters. “[They’re] one-offs and just being able to want to say that they’ve got something. But I don’t sense there’s going to be a more prolonged investment, but if it happens, it’d be great.”.

The most high-profile studio entrance into the movie theater market was Sony Pictures Entertainment’s acquisition of theater chain Alamo Drafthouse in 2024. Founded by Karrie and Tim League in 1997, the company made its name as an offbeat theater option with dine-in service and strict rules against talking and phone use in its theaters.

“I think we came to it from people who loved movies but didn’t really love our options with chain theaters that we had around,” noted Tim League. “We were always looking at how we can build this and build a community around sharing movies we love.”.

Alamo Drafthouse began talks with Sony Pictures Entertainment in late 2023 before completing the sale in 2024.

“It was kind of essential to find a upcoming partner as soon as we ran out of money,” remarked League, who has since stepped back from daily operations at the company and remains involved as Strategic Advisor.

“Why it was appealing for us as a firm with our board prior to deciding that Sony was the right acquirer for us is partly because of what that also meant in terms of resources that Sony could offer… Not only in terms of Sony [being] a very major, well-capitalized company but reputationally, very financially stable, [and] very well respected in the space,” said Michael Kustermann, CEO of Alamo Drafthouse and head of Sony Pictures Experiences.

Recent findings suggest that sony is not involved with day-to-day operations of Alamo Drafthouse. But the parent tech giant’s ownership is evident in occasional special programming, such as airing the Season 4 finale of “Breaking Bad,” which Sony’s TV division produced, in Alamo theaters in September 2026 to celebrate protagonist Walter White’s birthday.

But the largest initiative made possible by Sony’s ownership was the July 2026 announcement that Alamo Drafthouse would purchase the historic Cinerama Dome theater in Hollywood and the attached 14-screen multiplex.

Sources indicate that “This has been the white whale for Alamo for a long time,” noted Kustermann. He explained Alamo was interested in the location before the Sony deal but didn’t have the financial means to acquire a new flagship location. But after a couple of years of interest and conversations that did not progress, Alamo reached back out after the Sony deal and began serious talks in 2025.

Industry observers note that the company plans to operate the Cinerama Dome screen unlike traditional Alamo theaters. Dine-in service will not be offered. Kustermann said that the renovations will be minimal, aiming to keep a similar seat count. The iconic curved screen that defined Cinerama projection will remain, and reprints of films screened in Cinerama such as “It’s a Mad, Mad, Mad, Mad World” will be part of the programming slate.

Renovations to the multiplex will include adding one or two 70mm projectors, karaoke rooms, an updated bar, and an aesthetic redesign inspired by the theater’s 1960s decor.

Blue Fox Entertainment was founded in 2015. The North American distribution and film sales company distributes over a dozen films a year across a variety of genres.“Exhibition is where all the glamour is, right?” remarked Huntsman. “Distribution is very labor-intensive; you’re supplying content to a theater, to a platform, to DVD. It’s very back office, administrative.”.

Sources indicate that “I only got into distribution as a way to get into exhibition,” Huntsman explained, adding that Blue Fox Entertainment bought its two theaters to combine the organization’s passion for film and enter a new market. “I make no qualms. I’m in the money business, but I’m using movie theaters and film distribution and film sales to do that.”.

It has been revealed that when the dine-in theater chain iPic went bankrupt in 2026, Blue Fox bid on six of the 12 available locations and ultimately purchased the Westwood, Los Angeles, and Upcoming York City theaters. The dine-in service was removed, but each location has a full-service restaurant attached that does not require a cinema ticket.

By rebranding as The Cinemas, Huntsman aims to turn the theaters into viable assets that can make money beyond box office revenue. “I have private events, I have two restaurants at these locations, I do advertisements around the exterior. So if you put all that together, it’s not a bad business. If it was just a standalone straight movie theater, it’s a tough market.”.

The economics of why so many fresh independent theaters are popping up can be traced to a basic reality of the business, according to Laemmle: the simplicity in bringing a theater back to life. “You don’t need to pay anything to acquire inventory. It’s not like opening a bodega where you’ve got to fill it with stuff. You get a film, you promise to pay a percentage of the box office to the studio, and suddenly you’re in business.”.

In a recent development, ticket split rates can vary per title. The rate can be anywhere from 30% for repertory screenings to over 60% for a blockbuster Disney release. Some studios send a range of split rates that can be negotiated; others (like Disney) set a non-negotiable rate.

Sources indicate that A film’s success can also affect how much a theater owner makes per ticket sale. Speaking to this summer’s releases, Huntsman said that the underperformance of films like “Supergirl” and “Moana” meant he received a larger portion of the box office. But for big hits like “Toy Story 5,” theaters get a smaller piece of the action.

Studios can also control exhibition through clean policies: the practice that if a theater licenses a certain film, it must be on screen when the theater is open. These policies can be especially detrimental to single-screen theaters in rural areas, effectively limiting the variety of films a community can show.

Industry observers note that at Smodcastle, Smith planned special programming with Vulgathon, a marathon of all the films in his View Askew universe from “Clerks” to “Clerks III” in order. But while ticket sales were tracking to sell out all 900 seats across five screens, Disney stated that if the theater did not leave a screen open for the second weekend of “Deadpool and Wolverine,” the studio would not send them the film to screen for its opening weekend.

“So we had to leave one screen open, for fucking ‘Deadpool’ and shit, that did not sell out,” Smith said.

Advertising revenue also dropped dramatically post-COVID, according to Laemmle. He estimates that the tech giant currently makes 25% of its pre-pandemic revenue through theater advertising. “Ad agencies had a budget that they allocated for in-theater advertising in the pre-pandemic world. All of a sudden, movie theaters were closed so they just took those same ad dollars and moved them somewhere else…That was a significant source of contribution to the bottom line that’s really gone.”.

Loss of advertising revenue forces theaters to find new revenue streams. For some major chains like AMC and Regal, that includes pay-for-play trailer programming: where studios can pay to put trailers for their upcoming releases in front of new titles. This also incentivizes longer trailer blocks that can run up to 30 minutes.

In a recent development, other major sources of revenue for theaters are concessions, which can offer high margins for cheap snacks like popcorn and pre-packaged candy. Beer and wine sales have also been a major boost of revenue for Laemmle Theatres.

Recent findings suggest that the other option: Lean into alternative programming that may not incur as high ticket splits. The Cinemas has been experimenting with testing various repertory titles across different genres to figure out what titles will draw people back into theaters. Their upcoming lineup for November and December 2026 includes “Boyz in the Hood,” “When Harry Met Sally,” and “The Lord of the Rings” trilogy.

In a recent development, for Huntsman, the need for theaters to diversify revenue reflects the current model for how studios release films. “When I grew up seeing movies in theaters primarily in the ‘80s, there were like three studio releases every week…There was always the rom-com, the horror film, the action film, the indie film…Now it’s ‘Fast and the Furious’ comes out, and nobody releases anything for three weeks.” Huntsman added, “So in terms of profitability, [that’s] part of why we’re making the theater a destination.”.

According to recent reports, rising labor, rent, and electric bills over the last few years have made it harder for theaters to improve their margins. In a search for more profits, theater operators have taken on upcoming initiatives to upgrade the technologies and amenities associated with theater-going to bring in crowds looking for a more premium experience, with varying degrees of success.

For Alamo Drafthouse, the Sony-owned tech giant received complaints from longtime fans in 2026 after introducing mobile ordering to its theaters, replacing the original pen-and-paper method that involved more engagement with servers. Instead, guests scan QR codes to place orders that are sent directly to the kitchen.

This move drew ire from the Alamo community, who saw it as hypocritical to the company’s prominent No Phones policy. The company’s subreddit became flooded with users saying they wouldn’t be returning to the theater amid the changes. Actor Elijah Wood, an Austin local who frequently appeared at events put on by the chain, criticized the new system, calling it “truly awful” in a post on X.

The company described the QR code ordering system as part of a larger plan to ensure long-term stability and keep innovating the experience, citing past changes like introducing reserved seating and ending its adults-only policy.

An Alamo spokesperson mentioned that the organization has not laid off any staff due to introducing QR codes and that it allows servers to handle more tabs. They added the core of the decision was to protect wages and jobs for the company’s staff working 12 months a year, but that QR codes will allow them to hire fewer seasonal staffers.

Tim League declined to comment on the QR code system.

While Alamo Drafthouse pioneered the dine-in model for theaters, League’s newest business venture is to bring exhibition into the luxury space. He launched Metro Private Cinema in 2025, a 20-screen theater in Upcoming York City’s Chelsea neighborhood that specializes in small, private theater experiences with fine-dining menus to accompany the films.

Industry observers note that theaters range from four to 20 seats. Bookings start at four hours, and food packages are added to the price. Guests can choose between new releases, special holiday-themed programming, or a specific movie, plus a la carte food.

According to recent reports, “Since the dawn of cinema, it has been being tightly packed into a large room with a bunch of strangers,” remarked League. “So what if we kind of flip that around, and it’s you’re surrounded by friends. And how does that change the experience?”.

Pricing for the experience can vary. Example packages on the website list costs starting around $200 per person. When asked about introducing a luxury price point into the theater market, League explains that costs align with the high prices commonplace in the city. “Our meals are $115 for a 13-course meal, which is very much in line with New York pricing.” League added, “We have built a more higher-end, expensive model, but I think what we’re offering is not ridiculous.”.

If companies are not expanding the price-point of concessions, the other option is to expand the theatrical viewing experience itself. Sony Pictures Entertainment launched Cosm, a 364-seat immersive theater with an 87-foot curved screen, in 2024. Tickets are roughly $50, with some including themed food options. And massive Las Vegas entertainment complex The Sphere received over $400 million in revenue from sales of its multisensory AI-edited run of “The Wizard of Oz.”.

In a recent development, in recent years, audiences have shown growing interest in premium theater presentations. Major studio blockbusters are expected to have exclusive IMAX runs. Films like “Sinners” and “The Odyssey” have driven a rise in interest in IMAX 70mm screenings, letting audiences see movies in the format directors intended.

Recent findings suggest that CJ 4DPlex, the developer of premium screening formats ScreenX and 4DX theaters, reported a 26% increase in revenue in the first half of 2026 compared to 2025. Their technology includes 270-degree panoramic presentations or immersive 4DX theaters with moving seats and water effects. Ticket surcharges can range from $3 to $7 for ScreenX showings and up to $10 for 4DX tickets, compared to a traditional 2D ticket.

But the desire to jump into premium formats is not universal. Laemmle mentioned his theaters have no aims to offer advanced presentations. “We’re not necessarily engaged in the large format with the higher ticket price because we believe that movie-going should be something that’s done regularly…Moviegoing historically was the cheapest form of out-of-home entertainment, and we believe it should stay that way.”.

Industry observers note that the movie theater industry has always existed on a wire’s edge. Owners and monopolies have come and gone. Projection trends like Cinerama and Vistavision had their moments before becoming obsolete. Television, VHS, DVDs, and streaming have all carried the threat of being the final innovation that would put theatergoing in the past forever.

“The death of our industry has been predicted since the ‘50s with every new turn,” remarked League. “I just think there’s [now] pressure not to lose sight of the fragility of being an awesome third space.”.

2026 is at the moment on track to have the best box office performance globally since 2019, with the year expected to end with $35.7 billion in global ticket sales.

According to recent reports, for Huntsman, the increase is corollary to the output the studios offer: that the box office success of “The Odyssey” and “Spider-Man: Brand Latest Day” is more tied to quality than any other metric. “Anyone that states, ‘Oh, movie theaters are back,” they didn’t go anywhere. There just weren’t any good movies playing.”.

At Laemmle Theatres, the biggest draws of the year have been indie success stories, with films like “You Can See Everything,” “NAZA,” and “Filipiñana” bringing the theater some of its largest ticket sales.

It has been revealed that speaking with a variety of theater operators, the common thread in running a successful theater wasn’t what was on the screen. The key was understanding each theater’s audience. For Laemmle Theatres, it’s typically older people who go to the movies often and have a wide variety of tastes. At Metro Cinema, it’s Newly introduced Yorkers with the funds to splurge on an elevated experience for special occasions. And at Smodcastle, it’s Kevin Smith fans looking for programming only Kevin Smith can provide.

According to recent reports, the full scale of how COVID-19 changed culture has yet to be fully realized. But the renewed investment in owning and innovating movie theaters speaks to a broader desire to safeguard community spaces where people can exist between work and home. The theater industry’s revenue streams are more diversified than they’ve been in years. The allure of owning a movie theater isn’t just about making money; public goodwill has added intangible rewards for exhibitors for keeping theaters alive.

Or as Smith noted, “It’s good for the heart, good for the soul, good for the optics, good for the brand.”.

It has been revealed that given the success Prime Video has enjoyed with Fallout and HBO with The Last of Us, it's hardly surprising that Hollywood has been looking to get its hands on some of the biggest properties in the video game industry, although arguably the biggest of them all has remained frustratingly out of reach. Rockstar Games has just released Grand Theft Auto VI after a 13-year wait between installments, and given how much money Rockstar makes from its games alone, you can understand why the company hasn't felt a particular need to get involved with Hollywood. However, anyone who's spent the last few years watching Taylor Sheridan's Yellowstone spin-offs will probably be quite interested in which of Rockstar's franchises the company is reportedly more willing to entertain offers for.

According to a new report from Lesley Goldberg at The Ankler, Rockstar Games is reportedly open to bringing Red Dead Redemption to either film or television, despite continuing to reject approaches from Hollywood to adapt Grand Theft Auto. And given the popularity of the Western franchise, which hasn't had a new installment since 2018, getting the rights to adapt the games isn't going to come cheap. An agent who works with writers in the video game industry told Goldberg:.

“At one point, they were throwing around a purchase price of more than $100 million minimum for licensing rights.”.

That's $100 million just to get the rights, before anybody has even saddled up a horse. For comparison, as Goldberg notes, Amazon spent $250 million acquiring the global television rights to The Lord of the Rings in 2017. We're only speculating when we say the deal to secure the rights is entirely dependent on whether or not Gavin can be located.

According to recent reports, the show that claimed the most of your answers is the world you were built for. If two tied, both are shown — you're complicated enough to straddle two Sheridan universes.

Industry observers note that you are a Dutton — or you might as well be. You understand that some things are worth protecting at any cost, and that the modern world's indifference to history, to land, to legacy, is not something you're willing to accept quietly. You lead from the front, you carry your family's weight without complaint, and when someone threatens what's yours, you don't escalate — you finish it. You're not cruel. But you are absolute. In Yellowstone's world, that combination of ferocity and loyalty doesn't make you a villain. It makes you the only thing standing between everything that matters and everyone who wants to take it.

Industry observers note that you thrive in the chaos of high-stakes negotiation, where the money is enormous, the margins are thin, and the wrong word in the wrong room can cost everyone everything. You're a fixer — the person called when a situation is already on fire and needs someone with the nerve to walk into it. West Texas oil country rewards exactly what you are: sharp, adaptable, unsentimental, and absolutely clear-eyed about what people want and what they'll do to get it. You're not naive enough to think this world is fair. You're smart enough to be the one deciding who it's fair to.

You are a Dwight Manfredi — someone who has served their time, paid their dues, and arrived somewhere unexpected with nothing but their reputation and their wits. You adapt without losing yourself. You build loyalty through respect rather than fear, though you're not above reminding people that the two aren't mutually exclusive. Tulsa King is for people who are still standing when everyone assumed they'd be finished — who find, in an unfamiliar place, that they're more capable than the world gave them credit for. You don't need a throne. You build one, wherever you happen to land.

You carry the weight of a system that is broken by design, and you do it anyway — because someone has to, and because you're the only one positioned to do it without the whole thing collapsing. Mike McLusky's world is for people who are comfortable operating where there are no good options, only less catastrophic ones. You speak every language: law enforcement, criminal, political, human. That fluency makes you invaluable and it makes you a target. You've made your peace with both. Mayor of Kingstown belongs to people who understand that keeping the peace is not the same as being at peace — and who do the job regardless.

Recent findings suggest that anyone who's played Red Dead Redemption 2 will know that, for all the time we spent robbing trains and riding around the countryside, it was the relationship between Arthur Morgan (Roger Clark) and Dutch van der Linde (Benjamin Byron Davis) that made the game such a compelling experience. Watching Arthur gradually come to terms with the fact that the man he'd looked up to for much of his life wasn't necessarily the man he thought he was would lend itself particularly well to a long-form television adaptation. And of course, it would naturally lead into a second season following John Marston (Rob Wiethoff), the protagonist of the original Red Dead Redemption.

The success of 1883 and 1923 has also demonstrated that there's an appetite for Westerns on television that extend beyond the modern-day setting of Yellowstone, although there's no indication at this stage that Sheridan, or indeed any particular filmmaker or studio, is involved.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thanksgiving weekend is one of the busiest of the entire year for movie theaters. Each year, several big movies are released in and around the holiday, all vying for top spot at the worldwide box office. This year is no different, with several titles releasing from Wednesday to Friday. Audiences looking to see a movie over the long weekend will certainly have plenty to choose from, even more so than other years.

Last year, for example, Disney had a huge animated release in the form of Zootopia 2. The sequel, which was in development for nine years before finally debuting in theaters, ended up making a huge amount of money at the box office ($1.8 billion worldwide, to be precise). The fact that it was released around the Thanksgiving holiday in the United States certainly helped a great deal financially, as many are off from work and school.

Disney looks set to continue their trend of releasing an animated movie for Thanksgiving this year. This time, it’s Disney's Hexed, an original film that the studio hopes will gain enough of a following to develop sequels and spinoffs. The movie, which has a star-studded cast that includes Hailee Steinfeld and Walton Goggins, is projected to perform better than other original Disney animated releases from the last few years.

Recent findings suggest that there are a lot more Thanksgiving movies beyond Disney, too. There are comedies, dramas, sequels, and some Christmas movies as well. Not only that, but there are plenty of streaming services debuting new movies this week, too, giving audiences a chance to watch new releases from the comfort of their own home.

In a recent development, one of the sequels being released this Thanksgiving is Focker-in-Law. This is the fourth film in the comedy franchise that began with Meet the Parents in 2000. Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro have starred in every installment, and are set to do so again when Focker-in-Law debuts in theaters. They’re also joined by Owen Wilson, Teri Polo, Skyler Gisondo, and Ariana Grande (the latter two are newcomers to the franchise).

Industry observers note that focker-in-Law follows the next generation of the Fockers, as a newly introduced member hopes to join the family. This time, it’s Ariana Grande’s character who is engaged to the son of Ben Stiller's Greg Focker, Skyler Gisonodo's Henry Focker. Mirroring the plot of the first movie in regards to the dynamic between Stiller and DeNiro, Greg has reservations about his son's fiancé.

Recent findings suggest that the aforementioned Disney's Hexed is another movie that will release on November 25. Hexed's star-studded cast includes Steinfeld and Goggins, and also features Rashida Jones, Jodie Foster, Stephen Fry, Tracey Ullman, and Dan Stevens. The story follows a young girl named Billie Doe, played by Steinfeld, who enters the world of Hexe, which is the home of witches.

Recent findings suggest that another sequel releasing over Thanksgiving is The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth. From Netflix, the movie directed by David Fincher and written by Quentin Tarantino, and is a sequel to the latter’s Once Upon a Time in Hollywood. Here, it’s Brad Pitt who takes center stage, with Cliff Booth serving as the primary protagonist in the new adventure(s), leaving behind Leonardo diCaprio's character.

Recent findings suggest that the new movie follows Cliff Booth eight years after the events of Once Upon a Time in Hollywood. Rick Dalton has now moved to Australia to shoot a television series, so Booth is operating on his own in the film business. The movie demonstrates his many adventures around Hollywood, including helping a famous television star get out of a bad situation.

From Angel Studios, the biographical film Hershey will also release on the same day as Focker-in-Law, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, and more. Hershey, which stars Finn Wittrock as Milton S. Hershey (the founder of the chocolate empire), tells the story of its title character as he builds the tech giant alongside his wife, Kitty.

Recent findings suggest that hershey will cap another excellent year for Angel Studios. The studio has experienced some modest successes this year, thanks to releases like Drummer Boy and Young Washington.

It has been revealed that christmas is coming early with the release of Bitter Christmas, which also comes out on November 25. A Spanish language film, this project stars Bárbara Lennie and Leonardo Sbaraglia, and they’re joined by Patrick Criado, Victoria Luengo, Milena Smit, Aitana Sánchez-Gijón, and Quim Gutiérrez.

In a recent development, the story is set in two time periods: 2004 (in Madrid, Spain) and 2026 (also in Madrid). The modern-day portion follows a screenwriter working on a script also called Bitter Christmas, whereas the former focuses on a filmmaker undergoing a personal crisis over the holiday season.

One film releasing in a limited capacity this Thanksgiving is All of a Sudden. From Neon, All of a Sudden is a Japanese French production that tells the story of a quick-forming friendship between a playwright and a nurse. The playwright is suffering from stage four cancer and has only a few weeks to live, which is expected to bring a heartbreaking element to their close relationship.

According to recent reports, another limited theatrical release this Thanksgiving is In Waves. An animated production, In Waves is a romantic drama that tells the story of a teenager named AJ, who develops a relationship with a surfer named Kristen. It chronicles their growing bond, showing them navigating life and all its ups and downs (including a sudden illness for Kristen).

According to recent reports, also releasing on November 27 is the movie 14th. From director Ava DuVernay, 14th is a documentary that highlights the history of the Fourteenth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution. The documentary also highlights ongoing battles in Washington related to the amendment, and features interviews with key political figures like Stacey Abrams and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.

Also debutiing during the week of Thanksgiving is Clashing Through the Snow. A holiday romantic comedy in the same vein as a classic Hallmark Christmas movie, Clashing Through the Snow follows two rival editors who are stranded at an airport during a snowstorm, leading to an unlikely love story.

Fitting in nicely with the upcoming college and NFL football slate for Thanksgiving weekend is The Mosquito Bowl. Directed by Peter Berg, The Mosquito Bowl is an adaptation of the nonfiction book by Buzz Bissinger. The story focuses on four college football players who enlist to join the Marines after the tragedy at Pearl Harbor in 1941. The group go on to play a football game on Christmas Eve before flying to Japan to fight in battle.

Cleaning our homes is never going to make anyone’s list of favorite activities, but with the right technology, the task can be made almost effortless.

Whether you’re looking for an affordable robot vacuum for a small apartment or the ultimate flagship model capable of coping with the challenges of a large home, pet hair, and more, there’s a Roborock model for you – and with Black Friday savings of up to $1,650, there’s never been a better time to buy.

Roborock’s 2026 flagship model offers the ultimate in truly intelligent cleaning thanks to a combination of raw cleaning power and a market-leading combination of smart features.

It has been revealed that the benefits begin with a combination of raw power, reach, and fully automated self-cleaning. The Saros 20 delivers 36,000 Pa suction power with a dual anti-tangle system, ensuring no hassle with even the toughest of pet hairs, while a FlexiArm system ensures true edge-to-edge cleaning. The fully automated dock takes care of emptying the dust as well as washing and drying the mops.

It has been revealed that adaptiLift Chassis 3.0 enables the Saros 20 to move freely around the most largest and most complex of homes. A combination of an advanced vision system, adaptive algorithms, and a mechanical system comprising a main wheel, auxiliary wheel, and climbing arm mean that the device can cope with most thresholds between rooms. ‘Friends’ Gave Its Winning Formula an Unexpected Change in Just 22 Minutes

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As one of the most beloved sitcoms of all time, Friends was known for depicting a specific group of friends in New York City as they navigated their 20s and 30s.
  • Recent findings suggest that often, some of the most beloved episodes of the series are remembered for their antics, hijinks, and celebrity cameos; there’s one that is often underappreciated: Season 7’s “The One Where Chandler Doesn’t Like Dogs.” In this episode, the gang's all together for another annual feast.
  • In a recent development, it's time to journey back to 2000 for Season 7's eighth episode.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As one of the most beloved sitcoms of all time, Friends was known for depicting a specific group of friends in New York City as they navigated their 20s and 30s. Though it was merely a fantasy to live a life like Monica, Rachel, Joey, Chandler, Ross, and Phoebe, we aspired to have friends like them. Their friendship was something of a chosen family, as they would tend to celebrate Thanksgiving as a bunch; thus, the series was known for its Thanksgiving episodes.

Recent findings suggest that often, some of the most beloved episodes of the series are remembered for their antics, hijinks, and celebrity cameos; there’s one that is often underappreciated: Season 7’s “The One Where Chandler Doesn’t Like Dogs.” In this episode, the gang's all together for another annual feast. There is a baseline festive tone, but the episode also reflects a transition. This simple holiday episode captures a softer side of the series, reflecting its evolving tone. As the characters aged and reached pivotal points in their lives, the series increasingly balanced hilarious incidents with subtle life moments. The ensemble sitcom found a rhythm with a slower pace and softer beat, shifting the blueprint into a comforting blanket.

In a recent development, it's time to journey back to 2000 for Season 7's eighth episode. The plot of the episode sees Rachel (Jennifer Aniston) overjoyed that her cute, adorable assistant Tag (Eddie Cahill) has joined the gang for Thanksgiving dinner, but things don’t go according to proposal, causing their chance at a relationship to hit a snag. Ross (David Schwimmer) becomes obsessed with naming all 50 states before dinner, but initially falls four short. Meanwhile, Phoebe (Lisa Kudrow) is discovered hiding a cute dog named Clunkers in the apartment. The discovery forces Chandler (Matthew Perry) to admit his fear of dogs. If you removed the opening line about Thanksgiving, it could have been just any other day.

In a recent development, for the Thanksgiving episode, there wasn't a lot of fanfare around the holiday. The decorations were sparse. The attire was casual. And the meal, though prepared exceptionally well by Monica (Courteney Cox), was a chance for everyone to eat as one. It was a chosen family gathering. Compared to many other episodes that came before, "The One Where Chandler Doesn't Like Dogs" had a much slower pace. In fact, it was like sitting on the couch after a massive Thanksgiving feast when you're stuffed: it was relaxed. Though it might be a bit jarring to imagine, pretend the studio laughter is whisked away, and the scenes are presented as if they were the modern friend-hangout hit, Adults. There is a universe in which these slice-of-life moments could be presented in that manner, something impossible in many of the other scenarios Friends presented prior.

Sources indicate that friends was a show about 20-somethings living their best lives in NYC. When their 30s crept in, our friends became vulnerable as they embarked on internal reflection. Tag showing up is a big shock for Rachel, but his arrival is due to the fact that he broke up with his girlfriend. So, when he's not in the room, she asks Monica and Phoebe when it's an appropriate amount of time to make a move. Phoebe claims a month, Monica says three to four, but Joey, listening in from the background, chimes in with a half hour. The punch line is present, as well as the arrival of Joey's (Matt LeBlanc) iconic "moo point" line, but this is a genuine question that marks a shift in Rachel.

She has had a thing for her hot assistant, but couldn't pursue it. Now, presented with the opportunity, their conversation reveals shared uncertainty about finding love. His worries about the future resonate with her own. She wants what Monica and Chandler have. Of course, Joey nearly ruins it all, forcing Rachel to confront her feelings. In the end, her admission becomes the pair’s beginning, as Tag seals the night with a kiss.

Chandler, the king of snark, admits he hates dogs, which becomes a shocking confession for everyone. Scared by the inability to know what they are thinking, Chandler's revelation serves as a comedic element in the episode. Even when he tries to joke that either the dog goes or he goes, his reaction is met with silence as they all want the cute dog to stick around. But peel back a layer, and his shocked reaction is authentic. It gives the audience a moment to see his wall crack. He begins to show his vulnerability, once masked by wit. It's a sign of growing up. In the most Joey and Chandler fashion, they have a heart-to-heart in which Chandler has to set aside his fear to make Monica happy. His willingness to bring Clunkers back demonstrates that Chandler can put her feelings before his discomfort.

Through all the real-life vulnerabilities of Chandler and Rachel, Ross is secluded in his own world. He becomes obsessed with chasing a goal. His fixation on naming the 50 states exposes a side of him that has strayed from years of Ross and Rachel, allowing her to move on (for now). Perhaps his biggest moment of letting go of the old Ross was when he accepted help from Joey, who previously believed there were 56 states. For someone who always attempts to be the most intellectual person in the room, he gives himself momentary grace that he's not perfect. For some of us, it takes menial tasks like this to realize we're not made of steel. As Rachel wins the boy and Chandler faces his fear, Ross finally, in the closing scene, wakes up Chandler believing he has won the game, naming the fiftieth state, Delaware, only to be reminded he has Nevada twice.

The later seasons become a show about 30-somethings growing into the individuals they’d become. The comedy was still present, but the focus was on the comfort of accepting the next stage of life. There was more focus on what it means to settle down than on "live your best life." You could see this shift especially in how some of the Thanksgiving episodes were presented. Even when Brad Pitt dropped by to reminisce about the past, the episode had a more mature aura as it recognized that the past was growing more distant.

As someone revisiting the series years later, I see Friends differently now. I understand why the Thanksgiving episodes shifted. Friends was always going to need to grow up. Our gang of six was always going to take the next steps in life, so the series did the same. As they found those moments, the show softened and became warm and comforting. The laughs and gags are still there, but it is also shaped by the reality of life.

Friends is available to stream on HBO Max in the U.S.

Latest Update: 'Wifi Motion Sensing' Can Track Everything You Do Through Your Router

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (820 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A simple wifi feature could let ISPs track your location and movement patterns within your home.
  • In a recent development, while the technology isn’t universally implemented just yet and is typically opt-in only (smart home consumers might want the movement tracking feature for lights and heating), it presents quite a few privacy risks.
  • Sources indicate that wifi routers rely on radio signals to connect wirelessly to your devices and appliances.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A simple wifi feature could let ISPs track your location and movement patterns within your home. "Wifi motion sensing" turns your ISP’s router into a motion detector, letting providers know exactly how many people are in the house, where they are situated, individual movement patterns, and, in some cases, even body shapes that could approximate a person’s identity.

In a recent development, while the technology isn’t universally implemented just yet and is typically opt-in only (smart home consumers might want the movement tracking feature for lights and heating), it presents quite a few privacy risks. So here’s how wifi routers sense motion, what they can do with it, who has access to the data, and how you can disable it.

Sources indicate that wifi routers rely on radio signals to connect wirelessly to your devices and appliances. Those same radio signals are also absorbed and reflected by the human body as they travel in all directions from the router. With the right software, ISPs can track how those wifi signals travel around your room, which can be studied to detect presence and sense motion patterns.

As long as your ISP’s router model supports this feature natively, it doesn’t require any additional hardware to be installed in your home. For example, Xfinity’s version of the feature pairs your router with five other connected appliances in your room to create oval-shaped sensing zones that can track your presence and movement within those spaces.

It isn’t a newly introduced feature, either—companies like Cognitive Systems and Origin Wireless that supply networking hardware to ISPs have been offering wifi motion sensing for years now, while early research prototypes from the MIT date back at least as far as 2015. In 2025, IEEE updated its Wi-Fi 802.11 standard to include motion sensing and lay out the architectural guidelines for it, which makes it likely that even more routers will now ship with the feature.

In its current consumer form, wifi motion sensing can help you control smart home apparatus like lights or thermostats, get pet safety notifications on your phone, set up a fall alert system for elderly people, and trigger appliances remotely based on human presence. But enabling it carries risks.

Most providers, including Cognitive Systems, claim that the technology isn’t sensitive to identity and can’t be used to track specific individuals. But even if true, that’s more likely to be a product decision rather than a technical limitation. Karlsruhe Institute researchers have shown that even ordinary wifi signals can identify individuals with a 99.5% accuracy.

Also worth noting: ISPs’ legal wording suggests that they may disclose the collected and stored motion data at any time to law enforcement, government agencies, regulators, and courts in response to subpoenas or during an emergency. ISPs may also retain your motion data in the cloud long-term in case they are required to facilitate a subpoena in the future.

Sources indicate that as far as major ISPs are concerned, Xfinity (Comcast) is the only broadband provider that right now offers this feature across its commercial routers on the XB7, XB8, XB9, XB10, MXB1, and XER10 gateways. It’s opted out by default, but in case you or a family member already switched it on, you can disable it again by navigating to Home > WiFi Motion on the Xfinity app, click on the gear icon on the live view page, and tap Remove WiFi Motion.

Verizon Fios customers also had access to a Home Awareness feature on their routers that could be toggled on or off using the MyFios app, but that’s since been discontinued. In an official disclosure published shortly after the discontinuation, Verizon notified customers that it has deleted all associated movement logs from this service and no longer retains any motion data from owners.

But there are other regional ISPs that offer it, too. For example, Breezeline (Atlantic Broadband) offers a feature called Motion within its Plume-powered application that alerts customers when movement is detected in their homes, among its other features. MidCo, a telecom company in the Upper Midwest, has a feature called Sense which can be toggled on or off using the MidCo Wi-Fi app. Plume, ADT-owned Origin Wireless, and Airties—all of whom supply technology to ISPs—have also been marketing motion sensing to customers for the last few years.

Sources indicate that if you’re unsure if your wifi router or ISP has motion sensing features or opts you in by default, look for a feature called “Sense,” “Motion,” or equivalent in your broadband’s mobile app. Exact steps differ greatly from one ISP to another, so it’s best not to assume that they will all opt you out by default, or that they collect the same types of data. With the 802.11bf enhancement to IEEE standards in 2025, this technology will be accessible to even more router manufacturers, so expect adoption to grow among internet providers as well.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Writers Guild of America, East said that a number of MS NOW hosts — including Rachel Maddow, Jen Psaki, Chris Hayes and Nicolle Wallace — have signed on to a letter of solidarity urging the network to adopt a new contract that expands representation and boosts annual and minimum wage increases to keep pace with inflation.

The network, meanwhile, claims that talks have progressed and have been “constructive,” while stating that it supports employees’ right to organize. But it has contended that proposed wage increases would be out of line with what other employees across the company and at other networks have received. Related Stories News Joe Rogan's The Most Trusted Name In Media For Dudes - Especially Dudes With Daddy Issues News Skydance Buyouts Impact CBS Stations; Local Chicago Anchor Among Those Departing.

In a recent development, the WGAE represents about 300 members, and, per the union, is looking for recognition of 50 additional employees in digital, audio and longform, newsgathering, planning and the DC bureau. Watch on Deadline.

Recent findings suggest that the current contract expires on Dec. 3.

Sources indicate that “As hosts and guests of MS NOW programs, we stand in solidarity with the MS NOW Union as they fight for a contract that addresses inflation, AI protections, and retirement security. As one of the most trusted names in news, we are proud of our programming and the MS NOW producers that make it possible,” the letter stated.

Industry observers note that “We’re disappointed that Versant Media’s decision makers expect unit members to work extra hours creating latest digital content, without treating it as extra work or paying for it. On top of that, we are disappointed that Versant Media will not agree to the Union’s demands for annual and minimum wage increases that keep pace with inflation,” the letter added.

Other on-air figures who signed the letter include Ali Velshi, Amy McGrath, Alicia Menendez, Jacob Soboroff, David Noriega, Jillian Frankel, Ayman Mohyeldin, Katie Phang, Christine Jansing, Symone Sanders Townsend, Antonia Hylton, Jonathan Capehart and Michael Steele.

Industry observers note that rebecca Kutler, the president of MS NOW, wrote in a memo to employees, “Let me be clear: we support our employees’ right to organize, to be represented, and to advocate for themselves. That has never been in question, nor should it be.”.

She noted that the WGAE had reached agreement with other labor unions including IATSE and the DGA, and that they have already reached tentative agreements on a number of concerns with the WGAE and have “shown a willingness to find common ground where differences remain.”.

“We offer the highest starting salaries among our peers, having raised entry-level salaries significantly over the last five years, and the starting point for each role’s salary range is typically higher than our broadcast and cable news competitors,” she wrote.

In a recent development, she also cited the network’s hiring for more than 200 positions over the past year, as other newsrooms cut back. MS NOW has been building its newsgathering operation since the split from Comcast meant that NBC News was no longer a sister network.

The first contract for the MS NOW Union [previously MSNBC] was reached in 2023 and included a 3% pay increase for every year of the agreement’s duration. It also included “vital improvements to policies regarding extra pay for additional work, overnight work, and out-of-title work,” per the WGAE.

According to the network, they have offered guaranteed 3% salary increases, enhanced pay for filling in at an upgraded position, and a 33% increase in the night shift allowance per shift for exempt employees, crediting on-call time as time worked, as well as AI-related protections, among other proposals.

Per the network, WGAE is seeking 5% annual wage increases over the next two years and a 4.5% increase in the third year, as well as a 4% increase in salary minimums at signing and another 4.5% increase in 2029.

Kutler wrote that the network’s audience growth “does not insulate us from the financial pressures reshaping our industry. It takes a realistic understanding of these market pressures for us to continue our success.”.

The letters from the WGAE and Kutler are below:.

In a recent development, as hosts and guests of MS NOW programs, we stand in solidarity with the MS NOW Union as they fight for a contract that addresses inflation, AI protections, and retirement security. As one of the most trusted names in news, we are proud of our programming and the MS NOW producers that make it possible.We’re disappointed that Versant Media’s decision makers expect unit members to work extra hours creating newly introduced digital content, without treating it as extra work or paying for it. On top of that, we are disappointed that Versant Media will not agree to the Union’s demands for annual and minimum wage increases that keep pace with inflation.We are calling on the Company to agree to a quick and fair process to recognize all employees’ rightful place in the MS NOW Union without division or delay. Additionally, we call on the Company to agree to a contract that will protect wages, benefits, and security at work.

Recent findings suggest that team,As we continue to negotiate with the Writers Guild of America East, I’d like to give you an update about where we stand.For those unfamiliar with this process, the WGAE represents a group of our editorial employees in a collective bargaining unit that negotiates their compensation and other terms of employment. We reached an initial agreement with this union in 2023, and now that contract is set to expire on Dec. 3.Let me be clear: we support our employees’ right to organize, to be represented, and to advocate for themselves. That has never been in question, nor should it be. In the past year, we have successfully reached new collective bargaining agreements with other labor organizations, including two International Alliance of Theatrical Stage Employees locals and the Directors Guild of America, and have approached these negotiations with the same mindset. We have already reached tentative agreements with WGAE on numerous complications throughout this process and shown a willingness to find common ground where differences remain. We have made meaningful proposals to increase compensation, address workload concerns, expand opportunities for growth and advancement, and provide protections against AI, among many other offerings.We offer the highest starting salaries among our peers, having raised entry-level salaries significantly over the last five years, and the starting point for each role’s salary range is typically higher than our broadcast and cable news competitors. We are a workforce that is embracing new technologies and creating opportunities for employees to broaden their skill sets and advance their careers. Our goal is to ensure our employees will grow alongside our business and the broader industry. These commitments are part of the reason we have a tech giant-wide attrition rate well below national averages. Plus, while many other news organizations are cutting back their newsrooms and trimming roles, we have filled more than 200 in the past year at MS NOW and continue recruiting for dozens of open positions.We are enormously proud of MS NOW’s performance; our strong audience metrics are a testament to the work you do every day. But this success does not insulate us from the financial pressures reshaping our industry. It takes a realistic understanding of these market pressures for us to continue our success. We must weigh every financial commitment against our ability to invest in journalism, develop new programming, hire journalists, cover the 2028 presidential campaign, and build out platforms that will carry MS NOW into the future, including our direct-to-consumer offering.We will continue to compensate our employees fairly and competitively, while protecting our long-term growth. Those responsibilities are not mutually exclusive, but they require thoughtful decisions.As we approach the final weeks of these negotiations, let’s stay focused on what unites us: our shared commitment to the journalism we produce, the audiences who count on us, and the future of MS NOW. I am optimistic that together we will reach a fair and responsible agreement that reflects the respect we have for our colleagues and the work we do together.If you have any questions, please don’t hesitate to reach out to me, Greg, Madeleine, Scott, Marcus, or anyone on our leadership team. Our doors are always open.Rebecca.

#85557. Tech Report: 10 'Find Hub' Hacks Every Android User Should Know

Tech Report: 10 'Find Hub' Hacks Every Android User Should Know

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1292 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Google's Find Hub app isn't just for tracking your lost smartphone.
  • This month, Google finally added Left Behind notifications to Android trackers—but you have to enable the feature manually.
  • There’s a hidden feature in the Find Hub app that helps you keep track of things without actually using a Bluetooth tracker.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google's Find Hub app isn't just for tracking your lost smartphone. Over the past year, Google has consistently added features to manage your belongings, share your location with loved ones, and locate lost devices. Find Hub can now notify you when you've left your device or your tracker behind. Plus, you can use Gemini to remember where you left items, even without a tracker attached. Behind the scenes, there are even more hidden settings and features to help track your devices and make it easier to retrieve them in case they are stolen or misplaced. If you use Find Hub, you need to know about these 10 hacks.

This month, Google finally added Left Behind notifications to Android trackers—but you have to enable the feature manually. AirTags customers should be familiar with this feature already. When you leave your tracker or device behind, and exit the location range, you’ll receive a notification that you left without your item. You need to enable this feature on a per-device basis. Go to Find Hub and select a device. Tap the settings gear icon next to the device's name, and enable Notify when left behind. While you’re here, go to Add location to add familiar locations where you don’t want to get a notification (like your home or workspace). Otherwise, Find Hub may spam you with left behind alerts.

There’s a hidden feature in the Find Hub app that helps you keep track of things without actually using a Bluetooth tracker. You can simply ask Gemini to remember where you put things, and it will show up in the Find Hub app. To use it, pull up Gemini and say something like, “Remember in Find Hub that the passport is in the downstairs wardrobe,” or “I’ve kept the spare car keys behind the garage door.”.

In a recent development, you can then ask Gemini, “Where did I keep my passport?” and it will tell you. If you change the location of an item, just ask Gemini to patch it for you. When you go to the Remembered tab, you’ll see the location of all remembered items. You can also add items manually here using the Add button.

Some Android smartphones can remain findable for several hours after they've been switched off or their batteries have run out. If you’re using a supported device (like the latest Pixel series smartphone), you can use a hardware feature to track the location using Google’s mesh network, relying on nearby devices (similar to how Android tags work).

To make sure this feature is enabled, go to Find Hub, and tap Find your offline devices. Here, make sure that either With network in busy places only or With network everywhere is selected.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re using a tracker in your car, luggage, or on your keys, you might want to share location access with your spouse or family members. Find Hub has a feature called "Share Ownership" that lets you share the tracker details with up to 10 people. Only the location of your tracker is shared, not your personal device.

Sources indicate that to set it up, go to Find Hub, and choose the tracker or accessory that you want to share. Tap the Share Ownership button and follow the on-screen instructions to share the invite link via a messaging app or using Quick Share. Once the recipient taps Accept, you’ll get a notification. Go to the device settings in Find Hub and tap the Confirm button to enable location sharing.

Recent findings suggest that you can quickly share your live location with your friends or loved ones using Google Messages. Open a conversation, tap the Attachment icon, and choose Real-time location. Set the duration and tap Send.

If you don’t like using the Messages app, you can do so directly from Find Hub. Go to the People tab at the bottom of the screen, and tap the Plus icon. Choose the duration and select a contact to share the location with, then tap the Get Link button to copy the link. You can then share it via any messaging app of your choice.

You might have a Find Hub tracker in your luggage to help keep tabs on your bags. But you don't have to be the only one privy to its location. If your airline loses that luggage, you can temporarily share its location with your airline to help you retrieve it. This is an official feature, too: Google partnered with multiple airlines to make this data sharing easier. From the Find Hub, choose your tracker. Tap the Share Item Location button, and then tap Share Item Location again. Copy the generated web link and share it with your airline using the app or support page. The link will automatically expire in seven days, so you don't have to worry about your airline continuing to monitor your luggage's location long after your flight.

Find Hub uses a mesh network of supported Android devices to securely locate your lost device or tag. But by default, it waits until multiple Android devices detect the location of the lost device. This works well if you've lost the device in crowded areas, but it can increase your wait time if you lose it somewhere remote. Luckily, there is a hidden setting that triggers location sharing even if a single device reports its location. Go to Settings > Google > All services > Find Hub > Find your offline devices and select With network everywhere instead of With network in busy places only.

If you’ve lost your smartphone, you don’t need to rush to a computer or a website to track it. Borrow someone’s Android smartphone and head into their Find Hub. Tap Sign in as guest and sign in with your Google account associated with your device, then find and select your device in the account. If requested, enter the PIN that you’ve previously set up. You can now track the device’s location, get directions to the device, or play a sound to help track the device if it’s nearby. If the device is truly lost, you can use the Mark as Lost feature to remotely lock your device.

Sources indicate that map-based tracking is helpful in getting to the general vicinity of your lost device. But your smartphone or tracker is hidden; finding it may require precision tracking. Many newer trackers like the Pixel Tag come with an ultra-wideband chip that helps you find the exact location of the tracker, given you are nearby. This also works on Pixel smartphones (Pixel 8 Pro series and above) and Samsung Galaxy devices (S21 and above, Plus and Ultra models only).

Industry observers note that when using this feature, make sure you have Bluetooth enabled on your smartphone, then open Find Hub. Choose your tracker, and tap Find Nearby. Follow the on-screen instructions to locate the nearby device. You can also tap Play Sound to make the location process easier.

In a recent development, if you think your Android smartphone is lost or stolen, don’t rush to erase all data. While a remote factory reset is great for protecting your data, it also removes the device from your account. It’s best to try to get the device back. Two-factor authentication (or a passkey) on your Google account, along with a biometric lock on your smartphone, will protect the data itself.

It has been revealed that go to the Find Hub website, or use Find Hub on someone else’s phone in guest mode. Choose your device, and instead of Factory Reset, choose Mark as Lost. Here, you’ll see an option to enter a message. Type an alternative contact number, and a message to help recover the device.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I've read more than 30 books in the past year, all of them on an e-reader with a screen roughly the size of a credit card. If you think that sounds untenable, I say: Don't knock it 'til you've tried it. Once you're immersed in a book, you'll find the size doesn't matter, and the convenience of being able to slip it into any pocket and forget it's there means you need never be without it.

Right now, the Xteink X4 Pro, the best tiny e-reader I've tried so far—and Lifehacker's pick for the 2026 E-Reader Gift of the Year—is on its best sale yet for Black Friday: When ordered directly from Xteink, you'll save 15% off the usual $99 price, bringing it down to $84. This is the cheapest e-reader with a light and a touchscreen that you can buy right now, and it's well worth the money.

Sources indicate that the X4 Pro is the newest and best e-reader from Xteink, the Chinese tech startup that turned the e-reading world upside down last year with the launch of the original X4 pocket e-reader. While the X4 Pro is the same size as the basic X4 Classic, it adds two major upgrades—a temperature-adjustable front light and a touchscreen—plus a faster processor and more memory. As a result, it costs a bit more, but you can pick one at a $15 discount right now. (Even at full retail, the X4 Pro is $50 cheaper than the entry-level Kindle after its recent price increase—and even considering the Kindle's current Black Friday discount).

Meanwhile, if you're a reader who prioritizes the crispest text over conveniences like a front light, the 4.3-inch Xteink X4 Classic and the smaller 3.7-inch Xteink X3 are about $30 less during Amazon's own Black Friday sale.

As much as I love them, these minuscule e-readers aren't for everyone. Some may indeed find the screen too small (though if you've ever read a book on a phone, the experience is similar). Then there's the fact that they can't load your existing libraries of Kindle books; you'll need to source copies of e-books lacking Digital Rights Management (DRM) software. But if you can jump those hurdles, you might just discover it's the weirdest, most lovable piece of tech you've used in years.

Having spent two seasons married into the Dutton family in 1923, Michelle Randolph has become an even bigger star as the daughter of Billy Bob Thornton's Tommy Norris in Landman, and Taylor Sheridan isn't the only one who's been keeping Randolph busy over the last couple of years. Having ventured into the world of horror earlier this year with Scream 7, Randolph has now turned her attention to a considerably lighter genre, teaming up with one of the stars of The Summer I Turned Pretty for a Christmas movie. And it seems audiences haven't even waited until Thanksgiving to get into the festive spirit.

Having debuted on Prime Video on November 23, Clashing Through the Snow has already become the No. 1 movie on the streaming service worldwide, according to FlixPatrol's November 24 rankings. The movie is also sitting at No. 2 in the United States, while its success internationally has seen it overtake several installments of The Hunger Games franchise.

It has been revealed that think of Planes, Trains and Automobiles with a little more sexual tension. Or maybe the same amount, actually? We read the movie in a certain way. Randolph and Christopher Briney play rival publishing editors Hannah Hendricks and Ryan Mitchell, who find themselves sharing a rental car after a snowstorm puts an end to their plans to fly to Fresh York. Neither can really afford not to make it to Manhattan, given that their jobs are on the line and both have meetings with authors whose books could save their respective careers. For two people who make a living editing books, they're remarkably oblivious to the sort of story they've found themselves in.

Directed by Carlson Young (Upgraded), the movie features Randolph (Landman) as Hannah Hendricks, Briney (The Summer I Turned Pretty) as Ryan Mitchell, Lukas Gage (The White Lotus) as Teddy, Andrew Schulz (The Thicket) as Walter, Julia Fox (Uncut Gems) as Bianca Hart, and Paris Hilton (House of Wax) as Herself.

Meanwhile, Randolph is already back at work on the third season of Landman, having recently filmed scenes as Ainsley Norris alongside members of Texas Christian University's cheerleading squad. Paramount+ has yet to announce a premiere date for the third season.

Clashing Through the Snow is streaming now on Prime Video. Stay tuned to Collider for all the latest news and updates on the biggest and best movies and shows heading to your favorite streaming platforms soon.

Sources indicate that in the rugged terrain of West Texas, a team of landmen work to secure oil and gas leases, acting as intermediaries between landowners and energy corporations. The narrative centers on a driven landman whose ambitions in the energy sector lead him into complex negotiations and moral quandaries. The show explores the intense competition and the far-reaching consequences of the landmen's deals, highlighting the intersection of personal ambition and the broader effects on the community and the natural world.

💡 Key Takeaways
