📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1031 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

12 Things to Do on Christmas If You Don’t Celebrate

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1031 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that in a way, the Christmas season is more fun if you don’t celebrate it.
  • You can’t go wrong with some moo shu pork and a trip to the multiplex.
  • In a recent development, if Chinese food isn’t your thing, look at restaurants serving any non-European cuisine—Greek places, Japanese places, and Mediterranean places are usually open, as are plenty of Italian restaurants and steakhouses.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that in a way, the Christmas season is more fun if you don’t celebrate it. You get to enjoy all the brightly colored lights your neighbors put up, but you don’t have to put up your own. You don’t have to do any duty-shopping. There's no pressure. But Christmas Day itself leaves you in a mostly shuttered world that feels like there’s nothing going on. Fortunately, there are options to make Dec. 25 a fun day off, regardless of your observances.

You can’t go wrong with some moo shu pork and a trip to the multiplex. Chinese restaurants and movie theaters traditionally stay open on Christmas Day for those who don't celebrate, and they’re often filled with fellow Christmas refugees. Check Google for the hours of your local Chinese restaurant and give them a call to make a reservation. If you’re more adventurous and you’re in a city large enough to have a Chinatown (or a whatever-town), just head straight there on Christmas and see what happens—that’s how the best days usually start.

In a recent development, if Chinese food isn’t your thing, look at restaurants serving any non-European cuisine—Greek places, Japanese places, and Mediterranean places are usually open, as are plenty of Italian restaurants and steakhouses. Just make sure you check first. Lots of chain restaurants are open on Christmas Day too, including Applebee's, McDonald’s, Benihana, and more. You can even get Christmas breakfast at your local IHOP. But not every location of every outlet follows the same hours.

As for movies, most chain multiplex theaters are open on Dec. 25, and theaters are usually pretty full. The movies attract both people who don't celebrate Christmas and people who do, but want to get away from their families for a couple hours, so make sure and reserve a seat beforehand. Consider hitting up an out-of-the-way spot or that theater with the table service and cushy recliners to make it feel like more of an occasion.

Most people going to the movies on Christmas Day aren’t there for Christmas movies, so interesting “secular” movies are often slated for release on the 25th. This year's Christmas is unusually packed with interesting upcoming movies, including family flick Jumani: Open World, a Robert Eggers horror movie called Werwulf, and the crowd pleasing football story Mr. Irrelevant, so you have serious options.

Chinese restaurants and movie theaters aren’t the only establishments open on Christmas. Here are some other options:.

Go skiing or snowboarding: Most mountains are open on Christmas, and the lift lines are blissfully empty. There's no better way of celebrating a winter-based holiday than on a wide-open mountain.

Visit a skating rink: Speaking of winter sports, ice skating rinks are generally open on Christmas too.

In a recent development, pretend to be a tourist: Tourist attractions are often open on Christmas, especially in larger cities. This includes places like Madame Tussaud’s and Ripley’s Believe It or Not, as well as ziplines and Segway tours—so do that touristy thing you’ve never done before.

Get a room: If you’ve got some spare cash and have nothing better to do, get a room at a hotel. Hotels don’t usually close on Christmas, and they typically offer plenty of amenities, so take advantage of the pool at the Holiday Inn or the spa at the Four Seasons, depending on your lifestyle.

In a recent development, hiking and biking: Hiking trails and parks are open on Christmas if you want to get outdoors. If you’re into biking, hit the trails or hit the streets: Traffic is minimal on Christmas, so it’s a great time to put in some serious roadwork.

Volunteer: Not having anything to do on Christmas isn’t the biggest life problem, especially compared to people who have nowhere to go and nothing to eat. So use Christmas to help people and actually deliver on that whole “good will towards men” thing. Check your local Craigslist for volunteering opportunities.

Sources indicate that use Christmas as a catch-up day: This is strictly for type-A people, but if everyone is out of town and no one is going to call you, why not spend the day catching up on neglected chores or personal projects? You can spend at least part of your day knocking a few things off your to-do list and the rest of the time relaxing. That way you’ll get a break and still feel accomplished.

Just sleep all day: Type-B personalities like me see a day free of obligations and other people as a golden opportunity to do as little as is humanly possible, a day to fully commit to sloth.

Sources indicate that spend time with friends and family at home: Not celebrating Christmas doesn’t mean you can’t spend the day with family and/or friends. Get together with your loved ones, play games, watch a movie, cook together, talk, or whatever else you all enjoy. You don’t have to go out to have fun, so don’t rule out staying in with people you care about.

Shopping: This is at the bottom of the list because it’s iffy. Drug stores and convenience stores like 711 are usually open on the 25th. Grocery chains like Kroger’s and Trader Joe’s usually aren’t. Your local shopping mall or retail district might be open, but probably won't be, so check ahead.

Because so many places are closed on Christmas Day, you should plan ahead (unless you like spontaneity and are OK with the possibility of disappointment) by:.

Making a list of the places you want to go.

Calling nearby locations to confirm they’ll be open, as not every chain follows corporate holiday hour recommendations.

Making reservations at any restaurant(s) you blueprint to visit.

Putting together a basic timeline of the day, accounting for travel time, so you don’t lose any reservations, miss a movie, or arrive after the store closes.

Industry observers note that the most important advice here is to do something intentional on Christmas, even if it's sleeping in, so the day doesn't feel depressing or empty. So hit the slopes, suck down some dim sum, or keep your couch from floating away, but be sure you make Christmas your own.

You can never be too cautious when it comes to your online privacy. Between websites tracking your activity, advertisers collecting browsing data, and the ever-present risks of using public wifi, having an extra layer of protection is always a good idea.

Proton VPN has built a reputation around privacy and security and offers fully encrypted connections that help protect your internet traffic. This is especially important when you’re browsing on public wifi networks. The VPN service offers access to well over 20,000 servers across 149 countries, giving you plenty of options for choosing a connection location. This can come in handy if you want to access region-specific content while traveling or just want to get around geographical restrictions.

The Plus blueprint is particularly appealing if you plan to stream content from other parts of the world, as it offers higher speeds, supports streaming services, and lets you connect as many as 10 devices simultaneously.

According to recent reports, one of Proton VPN’s biggest draws is its focus on privacy. Based out of Switzerland, Proton operates under Swiss privacy laws. Additionally, the apps are open-source and independently audited, which adds another level of transparency to the service. Finally, you can expect to find quality-of-life additions like a kill switch, which cuts your internet connection if the VPN drops unexpectedly. This is critical to ensuring that your real IP address doesn’t get exposed on the internet.

10 Hidden Controls Every 'GTA 6' Player Should Know

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (830 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that you can have a ton of fun in GTA 6 even if you only follow the core gameplay loop of running around, stealing cars, and completing missions and side quests.
  • Industry observers note that if you just want to sit back and relax as your character drives around Leonida in GTA 6, you should try the auto-drive mode.
  • Sources indicate that your character is going to commit a lot of crimes in GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that you can have a ton of fun in GTA 6 even if you only follow the core gameplay loop of running around, stealing cars, and completing missions and side quests. However, if you take a minute to learn a few hidden controls, I think you'll enjoy the game even more. These are fairly simple controls that let you hide from the cops, trash talk other drivers, or flip the bird when you're feeling like annoying NPCs. These are 10 of the best hidden GTA 6 controls that'll help you unlock an entirely new side of the game.

Industry observers note that if you just want to sit back and relax as your character drives around Leonida in GTA 6, you should try the auto-drive mode. It's a relaxing way to enjoy the streets without having to worry about following traffic rules. To enable it, you need to get in a vehicle and add a waypoint on the map. This serves as your character's destination, so if you want a longer drive, be sure to drop the waypoint far, far away. Next, hold the down arrow on the D-Pad, and press the Option button. This enables cinematic mode. Then, hold the Circle button to enable auto-drive.

Sources indicate that your character is going to commit a lot of crimes in GTA 6. When this happens, you attract heat, and soon enough, cops will begin chasing you. Switching cars is a great way to reduce the amount of attention you get from law enforcement, but you can still be identified by your face or clothing. Until you can reach a safe spot to swap outfits, maintain a low profile by ducking while driving. Hold the Circle button while driving to duck.

EA's Road Rash was among the first racing games I played as a child, and I remember how much fun it was to kick your rivals while speeding through the game's various courses. You can have a taste of that in GTA 6 too. Press the Square button while you're riding a bike, and your character will kick anyone who's near you. If you do this in a car, it opens the door, and hits people around the car. To annoy other drivers, press R3, and your character will direct some trash talk towards NPCs.

Recent findings suggest that hold Circle to lean back against walls, or to sit on the beach. To rest on a ledge, you can hold L3. This lets you take a moment to soak in beautiful views in the game, or lounge around as you listen to NPC conversations. Paying attention to those conversations can lead to some fun side quests, and sometimes give you a tip or two for quick money or other rewards.

Sources indicate that if you really want to rile people up in GTA 6, you can flip the bird. This works only when your character is unarmed. Hold L2, focus on a person, then press R1. Actions have consequences in GTA 6, so be prepared to fight NPCs when you do this.

It has been revealed that when you're being chased by cops, enemies, or angry NPCs, you can use a quick shortcut to look back without turning the camera around. Just hold R3 to look behind you.

According to recent reports, while driving, press Circle to toggle headlights (and switch to high beams). This is particularly useful when you're offroading at night. You can also hold left arrow on the D-Pad, and move the right stick up to access other vehicle controls like hazard lights, opening or closing windows, etc., in case you want to add to the realism.

It has been revealed that stealing emergency vehicles in GTA 6 is risky, but the reward is totally worth it. Not only do you find stashes of weapons, gear, and money in some of these vehicles, but you also have access to sirens that help you clear traffic off your path. If you steal an ambulance or a cop car, hold L3, and move the left stick up to go through different siren tones. Press L3 and the left stick up to enable the siren.

GTA 6 is a third-person game, but it has a first-person mode that partially works. It is useful for looking at smaller objects around your character, such as posters, small signs, or to look for clues in and around a house. (Yes, I am talking about Mandy's creepy house and bad vibes.) Hold L2 + hit R3 to switch to first-person mode. Sadly, you can't move when you do this, but you can look around. Try it in Mandy's property to observe a few nasty surprises.

When you sprint towards a car, press the X button to slide across the hood. This is much faster and smoother than running around parked cars or jumping over them. It also looks cool, which is reason enough to try this feature.

Advances in sensing, manufacturing, computational resources, and data-driven methods are enabling upcoming approaches to electromagnetic sensing, non-destructive evaluation, and advanced materials processing. This webinar will demonstrate how the COMSOL Multiphysics software supports predictive modeling by coupling electromagnetic fields with thermal, chemical, mechanical, and transport phenomena across multiple length and time scales.The first application we will show focuses on eddy-current thermometry for reconstructing three-dimensional temperature fields in metal plates. Temperature-dependent electrical conductivity alters induced currents and magnetic fields, enabling volumetric thermal inference. COMSOL simulations of defects and laser-induced transient heating will support validation of reconstruction algorithms. Multifrequency excitation will be investigated to improve depth discrimination through frequency-dependent penetration depths and sensitivities.The second application examines microwave-enabled volumetric additive manufacturing of ceramic components. A high-power microwave beamforming array delivers localized energy into three-dimensional volumes, enabling processing of opaque, particle-laden resins. Coupled COMSOL models of electromagnetic propagation, microwave absorption, heat transfer, and ceramic sintering kinetics are used to predict temperature evolution, reaction progression, spatial resolution, and processing scalability. Future extensions will incorporate pulsed excitation, fluid flow, resin viscosity, convection, shrinkage, and solid mechanics.Together, these examples demonstrate how the COMSOL software can integrate multiphysics modeling with sensing, manufacturing, and data inversion. This webinar will present two applications of coupled electromagnetic and thermal modeling in COMSOL Multiphysics: eddy-current thermometry in metal plates and microwave-assisted processing of ceramic-loaded resins. By connecting simulation with practical engineering systems, COMSOL-based modeling can accelerate technology development, reduce experimental iteration, and support reliable scale-up of next-generation electromagnetic technologies. According to recent reports, 9to5Mac is supported by Sony: Score Sony’s ULT Field 1 Bluetooth speaker for 51% off. Powerful bass, room-filling sound, up to 12 hours of battery life, IP67 durability, stereo pairing support, and much more.

As my colleague Ryan explained, Apple will likely release iOS 27.3 to all iPhone users sometime in December. Typically, Apple would release its x.2 software updates in December, but this year is different because iOS 27.1 was exclusive to iPhone Duo. That means that, in terms of the timeline, iOS 27.3 is essentially the equivalent of iOS 27.2.

Here’s when Apple has released its December updates in recent years:.

So with that in mind, we expect iOS 27.3 to be released sometime during the first half of December.

It has been revealed that the redesigned Health app is back in iOS 27.3. This was first available during testing of iOS 27.2, but did not ship as part of that final update.

In a recent development, the redesigned Health app is split into three tabs: Insights, Longevity, and Browse. The app features an all-new design that dynamically adapts based on your data, including Apple Intelligence. The Longevity tab includes a new Health age feature that uses Apple Watch data to show how your metrics track relative to your actual age.

For Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 people, it also offers easy access to view your Readiness score every morning.

For Apple Fitness+, iOS 27.3 adds a new Gym Strength feature. This creates progressive, four-week prepares based on your strength goals, experience, schedule, and available equipment.

As you complete each week of workouts, the following week adapts based on the reps and weights you logged.

For iPhone Duo customers, iOS 27.3 adds Reachability support. This setting shifts the interface on the outer display to the right or left, making it easier to reach the far corners. It’s designed to make iPhone Duo easier to use with one hand, despite the wider outer display. You activate it by swiping right on the right edge of the screen or left on the left edge.

Reachability for iPhone Duo is on by default. You can turn it off in Settings > Accessibility > Touch > Reachability.

Sources indicate that iOS 27.3 also brings a new face unlock feature to iPhone Duo. This is not full-fledged Face ID. Instead, Apple is using the front-facing camera on the iPhone Duo’s outer display to recognize you, then unlock the device. It doesn’t work for things like Apple Pay and passwords.

iOS 27.3 also tweaks the iPhone Duo’s software keyboard by making the keys slightly narrower and the font slightly smaller.

Industry observers note that finally, iOS 27.3 includes a upcoming option in the Settings app to have your iPhone Duo lock when closed. Once enabled, your iPhone Duo will lock when you fold it, rather than transition content from the inner display to the outer display.

Industry observers note that when it debuted, the iPhone Duo included a more robust version of StandBy with latest clock faces and expanded customization options. iOS 27.3 brings the iPhone Duo’s StandBy experience to all iPhone models.

This includes the redesigned Analog and Digital Clock faces, as well as additional customization options for colors and complications. The enhancement also adds support for Shared Albums to the Photos face.

According to recent reports, iOS 27.3 brings several key Siri AI updates. First, the update expands Siri AI with many latest capabilities across Apple apps. Apple explains:.

We started rolling out these new capabilities across many Apple apps, including Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather, so consumers can do things like find a coffee shop they visited last week or archive files that haven’t been opened in over a year.

There are many more actions available now as examples for you to reference. To see what you can do in each app, just ask Siri AI.

It has been revealed that with iOS 27.3, Apple is also starting to test upcoming ways for developers to create Siri AI integrations for the first time. This is described as an “early Developer Preview.” Apple explains:.

Today’s preview allows any app to bring its content and actions directly into Siri AI by using App Intents, making it easier for all apps to tap into Siri AI’s newest capabilities, including personal context understanding, onscreen awareness, natural language, and more. So people can just ask for help in their own words, and Siri AI carries out any custom action you’ve built, from checking a delivery to booking a reservation to placing an order.

While this is being tested as part of iOS 27.3, Apple indicates it will start shipping to customers in a few months.

iOS 27.3 also expands Siri AI to new languages, including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.

Sources indicate that you can unlock higher usage limits with an eligible iCloud+ initiative, starting at $2.99 per month. If you hit your usage limit, basic Siri requests will still work. That includes things like setting timers and alarms.

iOS 27.3 brings the original set of Apple Intelligence features to China for the first time. This does not include Siri AI or other iOS 27 updates, but it does include the following features:.

iOS 27.3 is a major revision to Safari. First, the update adds support for a latest vertical tabs design layout on iPhone Duo’s inner display. If you choose this option, your Safari tabs will be arranged vertically along the left-hand side of Safari, rather than along the top. Vertical tabs are also available on Mac and iPad with macOS 27.3 and iPadOS 27.3.

iOS 27.3 also adds a new Adaptive Dark Mode feature. This feature can automatically apply Dark Mode to websites that don’t natively support it. You can choose to have Adaptive Dark Mode automatically kick in or use it on a site-by-site basis.

For Apple Music consumers, iOS 27.3 adds a latest “Selfie Sing” feature that lets users record a video of themselves while singing karaoke. To use this feature, start playing a song and go to the lyrics view. Then tap the new camera button that appears on the right-hand side of the lyrics.

The revision also refines the design of viewing lyrics while your iPhone is in landscape mode.

There are two key changes to the Apple TV app in iOS 27.3. First, the revision introduces video podcasts in the TV app. You can now watch your favorite video podcasts in the TV app, and sync your playback progress between the TV app and the Podcasts app.

It has been revealed that second, iOS 27.3 adds vertical video to the TV app. The app now includes a newly introduced “Explore Clip Collections” section where you can browse clips from Apple TV content in a TikTok-style design.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NBC is closely tracking a Thanksgiving storm expected to bring high winds and heavy rain to Latest York City and much of the Eastern U.S.

It has been revealed that the network’s coverage of the 100th edition of the annual Macy’s Thanksgiving Day parade will air on NBC and stream on Peacock from 8:30 a.m. to noon ET. The parade remains a major draw, with last year’s pulling in 34.3 million viewers across NBC and Peacock, its biggest combined audience on record.

It has been revealed that tyler Roys, a senior meteorologist with AccuWeather, remarked in an interview with Deadline that the second half of the parade seems to be at the most risk of being disrupted. He said the winds will be “near criteria” for grounding balloons – a signature feature of the Upcoming York City event, along with marching bands and floats. “They have some decisions to make over the next 48 hours,” Roys added.

RELATED: Deadline’s Guide To 2026 Holiday Specials, TV Programming Plus Where To Watch Classic Christmas Movies Watch on Deadline.

In a recent development, NBC’s affiliate in New York expects it to be “a close call” whether wind speeds on the Midtown Manhattan streets are below city-mandated guidelines. Rules require balloons to be grounded in sustained winds of 24 miles per hour or if gusts are higher than 35 mph.

The Nor’easter, a classic storm pattern, is expected to take shape late Wednesday and into Thursday morning, gathering strength as it grinds toward the Atlantic Ocean later in the holiday. Sustained winds are expected to be 12-25 miles an hour with gusts of 20 to 30 mph, increasing over the course of the day. AccuWeather is expecting one to two inches of rain to fall on Fresh York, making this likely to be one of the wettest Thanksgiving in the city’s history.

In honor of NBC’s broadcasting centennial, the parade is set to have 100 large balloons. The “All-Star Broadway Thanksgiving Day Celebration” will feature numerous indicates in a 10-minute medley. The balloons have only been grounded once before, in 1971, due to a similar mix of rain and wind.

According to recent reports, about 3 million people typically watch the parade live, with the Manhattan skyscrapers creating a wind tunnel that can intensift the impact of the weather. In 1997, a wind-blown Cat in the Hat balloon clipped a light pole, sending it tumbling to the street below. The accident injured four spectators, one seriously, and cost the city a steep payout to settle a lawsuit.

Sources indicate that “Our team is closely monitoring the weather forecast with our city and agency partners, and as always, the safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority,” NBC mentioned in a statement provided to Deadline. “Decisions regarding balloon flight will be made on parade morning based on weather conditions and established safety protocols.”.

NBCUniversal’s ad sales teams have been promoting the 100th anniversary for many months, and the division noted Monday it had established a revenue record for the parade. The firm’s full inventory of holiday programming, including the parade as well as a Thanksgiving Eve special, Christmas in Rockefeller Center and seasonal editions of Today and The Tonight Show, posted a 30% revenue gain over last year. The company said 50 upcoming advertisers have also joined the fold.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Los Angeles County judge has rejected Backstreet Boys singer Nick Carter’s bid to dismiss a sexual battery claim brought by singer and actress Melissa Schuman.

In a new ruling obtained by Rolling Stone, the judge said the claim could proceed under a California law that took effect Jan. 1, opening a two-year revival window for otherwise time-barred claims of adult sexual abuse against individual perpetrators. Unlike the law in effect when Schuman first sued Carter, the new statute allows lawsuits against individuals without requiring plaintiffs to establish a cover-up or name a business as a defendant.

“The individual claim against defendant Carter for sexual battery is proper irrespective of the existence of a cover-up. Defendants cannot prevail on summary adjudication merely by attacking the cover-up allegations,” Los Angeles County Superior Court Judge Lisa K. Sepe-Wiesenfeld wrote in her ruling issued Monday. “There is a conflict in the evidence presented as to whether a sexual assault of plaintiff occurred. Accordingly, a triable concern of material fact is present as to the first cause of action [for sexual battery].”.

Attempts to reach Carter’s lawyers were not immediately successful on Tuesday. Schuman’s attorneys, Guinness Costello and Jamie Majerus, praised the judge’s decision.

“[The] ruling moves Ms. Schuman one step closer to justice. Mr. Carter asked the court to throw out her case against him without a trial, and the court declined,” the lawyers noted. “Ms. Schuman first came forward in 2017 and has waited nearly a decade to put her case in front of a jury. In May, she will finally have her day in court and the opportunity to seek the justice she deserves.”.

Industry observers note that carter had sought to dismiss Schuman’s sexual battery claim by challenging the purported cover-up alleged in her lawsuit. He argued in filings that her “entire complaint would be time-barred except for her cover-up claim” and that there was “no viable sexual battery claim against Carter individually” without the claim of an “underlying cover-up.” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

In a declaration, Carter mentioned, “At no point in time have I ever offered, solicited and/or secured a non-disclosure agreement, a confidentiality agreement, a payoff, a settlement and/or otherwise participated in silencing an alleged victim of sexual assault.”.

In a recent development, at a Nov. 6 hearing, Carter’s lawyer, Dale Hayes Jr., argued that Schuman’s “only evidence” of a cover-up came from Shannon Ruth, who alleges Carter sexually assaulted her on tour bus outside the Tacoma Dome in Washington after a show on February 25, 2001. Ruth claims Carter told her the incident was their “special secret” and that she would go to jail if she reported it to police. Hayes argued to the judge that Ruth’s testimony was “heavily contradicted” by 13 other witnesses who testified that Carter had no opportunity to encounter Ruth the night of the alleged assault. Carter maintains he never met Ruth.

After taking two weeks to consider the arguments, Judge Sepe-Wiesenfeld ruled in Schuman’s favor, allowing the sexual battery claim to proceed. A trial is set for May 10, 2027.

Sources indicate that schuman first sued Carter in April 2023, alleging he raped her at his Santa Monica apartment in 2003, when she was 18, and he was 23. The former member of the pop group Dream alleges Carter gave her a sedative-laced cocktail and performed oral sex on her over her protests before raping her. The two had been cast as co-stars in the 2004 made-for-TV horror film The Hollow.

Carter, 46, previously tried to dismiss the lawsuit, arguing that the dispute belonged in Nevada, where he was already suing Schuman and two other women who accused him of rape, alleging they conspired to defame and extort him. The judge rejected the request. In July 2024, he filed a $2.5 million cross-complaint against Schuman in California, maintaining that the two had consensual sex. 📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you use Signal, it's likely you care at least a little bit about keeping your communication private so only you and those you're chatting with can see your message threads.
  • In a recent blog post, Signal president Meredith Whitaker outlined the potential threat AI assistants like Siri and Gemini pose to the platform's promise of privacy.
  • Sources indicate that signal has already blocked screenshot capabilities for Microsoft's Recall AI, which by default was able to take and store screen grabs of Signal messages on Windows 11.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you use Signal, it's likely you care at least a little bit about keeping your communication private so only you and those you're chatting with can see your message threads. Signal's end-to-end encryption keeps prying eyes out, but if you use agentic AI on your device, your chats may not be as locked down as you think.

In a recent blog post, Signal president Meredith Whitaker outlined the potential threat AI assistants like Siri and Gemini pose to the platform's promise of privacy. Systems-level capabilities like Gemini Intelligence (on Android) and Siri AI's Onscreen Awareness (on iOS and macOS) scan your screen and may be able to capture data from Signal conversations in the process, which can then be used to perform tasks. Not only does this potentially expose your information, but that of other conversation participants as well. Whitaker notes that this leaves privacy protections outside of Signal's control because the platform cannot easily restrict AI access to the app.

Sources indicate that signal has already blocked screenshot capabilities for Microsoft's Recall AI, which by default was able to take and store screen grabs of Signal messages on Windows 11. While Signal cannot guarantee that AI won't have access to your data, there are a few protections now available for those on iOS and Android as well.

The main workaround in Signal for now is to restrict screenshots and screen recordings inside the app, though this does not prevent AI agents from potentially grabbing content from other parts of your device. According to Signal's support documents, these protections will now be enabled by default on iOS 27 and Android with the latest versions of the Signal app.

It has been revealed that people on iOS 27 can confirm or manually disable screenshot protection via Settings > Privacy > Block Siri AI. The compromise with this setting is that it also blocks you from taking screenshots of Signal conversations in the app and App Switcher, though you can disable it temporarily for 10 minutes if needed. On Android, Signal automatically engages the "Screen security" setting when it detects an AI agent attempting to access the screen. This, too, blocks screenshots inside the app and can be disabled via Settings > Privacy > App security > Screen security. Signal cannot block screenshots on macOS 27. However, users can add Signal to their Excluded Apps list via System Settings > Siri, which at least limits proactive access to conversations by Siri AI.

Two Budget Smartwatches That Make Perfect Gifts

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1478 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, if you or someone on your shopping list wants a upcoming smartwatch, you have plenty of options to choose from.
  • According to recent reports, luckily, you do have options.
  • Industry observers note that contrary to what you might expect, Amazfit has no ties to Amazon—other than that you can buy these watches from the latter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, if you or someone on your shopping list wants a upcoming smartwatch, you have plenty of options to choose from. The problem is, a lot of them can be quite pricey. Apple's cheapest smartwatch, the SE 3, starts at $249, and its other selections only skyrocket from there. On the flip side, the risk in picking a smartwatch that's too inexpensive is that the manufacturer likely made a series of sacrifices to get the price that low. At a certain point, the tradeoff just isn't worth it.

According to recent reports, luckily, you do have options. There are two smartwatches on the market that aren't just cheaper than the competition, they're not even in the same ballpark. And while you shouldn't expect the same capabilities as you would on flagship wearables, these devices are perfectly usable, both as fitness trackers and smartwatches—all while spending well below $100 a pop. CNET put both smartwatches through their paces to make these determinations, so you know whichever model you get, you won't be picking up a wearable paperweight.

Industry observers note that contrary to what you might expect, Amazfit has no ties to Amazon—other than that you can buy these watches from the latter. Amazfit is its own manufacturer, and produces a wide selection of smartwatch options. The Bip 6 happens to be the company's latest budget smartwatch, with an MSRP of just $79.99. In most cases, a price that low would be a red flag for a smartwatch, but not in the Bip 6's case.

The Amazfit Bip 6 holds its own against other flagship smartwatches. That's true on a surface level: This watch looks your average smartwatch, rather than a cheap imitation. In fact, at first glance, I'd bet most people would assume the Bip 6 is actually an Apple Watch. It has a rounded square design with a large 1.97-inch display with a resolution of 390 by 450 pixels (though there's no Always-On display). This isn't a cheap display, either: Amazfit put an AMOLED screen on the watch, which looks great indoors—though CNET Labs struggled to see the screen in direct sunlight.

Where the Bip 6 really shines, however, is with fitness tracking. This watch supports GPS, which makes tracking outdoor runs possible without a smartphone. CNET Labs found that it takes about 10 seconds to find a GPS signal, but once it connects, you're set. While running, the Bip 6 reliably tracks your heart rate. CNET Labs compared its sensor to the Polar chest strap HR monitor and found it on par, though, like other smartwatches, the Bip 6 is slower at detecting heart rate spikes. You'll get data like cadence and stride while tracking runs, and strength training and muscle groups while working out indoors. For example, CNET Labs found that it correctly identified arm muscle exercises while testing the watch during a pilates session.

According to recent reports, you also get some health and wellness features, too. The Bip 6 can measure heart rate variations, body temperature changes, sleep stages, and even your breathing quality. Its One Tap Measuring mode supports a single reading for heart rate, SpO2 (blood oxygen saturation), stress, and breathing rate, and it supports cycle tracking—though CNET specifies it can't track skin temperature like other smartwatches and health trackers. There's an optional subscription that provides AI coaching tools and looks out for health conditions like sleep apnea and insomnia. While health and wellness tracking is solid, note that CNET Labs found Amazfit's app, Zepp, to be confusing, since it simply displays your data without much context or explanation.

In a recent development, for an $80 smartwatch, the Bip 6 has an excellent battery life. CNET Labs found that the watch could be pushed to its limits—multiple workouts using GPS, heart rate tracking, keeping the display on during workouts—and still run for eight days before needing a charge. In fact, reviewer Vanessa Hand Orellana speculates you could push the Bip 6 to Amazfit's two-week battery life claim by limiting some of the most intensive settings and features. The only downside here is that there is no fast charging, so it will take about two hours to get back to 100%. But if you're only charging the watch once every week or two, that isn't much of a burden. There's also no charger in the box, so you'll need to use a separate USB-C cable.

Industry observers note that as a smartwatch, the Bip 6 can be a mixed bag. CNET found that the UI was clunky and sluggish, and the OS requires some user intervention before it's as usable as a standard Apple Watch or Galaxy Watch. While the watch has a voice assistant, Flow, CNET found it to be borderline unusable. However, CNET claims Android customers can reply to texts with a keyboard or dictation without needing the assistant. iPhone users can't do the same by default, but by downloading a third-party app, they can jerry-rig the watch to send and receive texts.

Based on CNET Labs' testing, the Amazfit Bip 6 is one of the best budget smartwatches you can buy. For $80, you get a reliable workout tracker that looks like most standard watches on the market. And while you're making some sacrifices at this price point, they're largely worth it for $80.

Recent findings suggest that while the Amazfit is a good choice for both iPhone and Android users, the Galaxy Fit 3 might be the best choice for Samsung users. This isn't an option for iPhone users, and while it works with all Android devices, you get some Samsung-specific perks if you have a Galaxy phone.

The Galaxy Fit 3 is even cheaper than the Amazfit Bip 6: This watch is only $60, which makes it among the cheapest smartwatches you can buy. Now, this doesn't look like your average smartwatch. Samsung opted for a fitness tracker-like design, with a long 1.6-inch (40mm) AMOLED display. But for a fitness tracker/smartwatch hybrid, it's a solid look.

According to recent reports, in CNET's testing, one of the Galaxy Fit 3's biggest strengths is its battery life—though it pales in comparison to the Bip 6. When pushed to its limits, the Fit 3 can run three days in between charges, though Samsung claims you can get it up to 13 days with the right settings. While the Amazfit has it beat, the Fit 3 might sound like a dream compared to other smartwatches, even from Samsung. Unlike the Bip 6, the Fit 3 supports fast charging. You can fill the watch up completely in just over an hour.

Recent findings suggest that CNET did find that the "smart" elements of this wearable were a bit lacking, however. The Fit 3 doesn't support voice dictation or mobile payments like other watches do, and unless you have a Galaxy phone, you won't be able to access the camera remote or sync your alarms. And while the Amazfit Bip 6's "Flow" is hardly reliable, the Fit 3 doesn't have an assistant at all. You can see incoming calls and decline (but not answer) them, and you can send prewritten responses to text messages, but not initiate them. Still, CNET found that Samsung added the essentials: You have an alarm, calculator, weather app, camera remote, and, of course, the Samsung Health app. (What kind of health tracker would this be without it?).

Industry observers note that CNET found that the Fit 3 is a reliable fitness tracker, particularly for $60. You can track over 100 different workouts, and the watch automatically logs exercises like runs, walks, rowing, and elliptical sessions—if you enable auto-tracking, that is. It also supports swimming with its IP68 water resistance rating. CNET Labs found that the heart rate tracking was "generally accurate" when compared to the Polar chest strap, though its slower with registering heart rate spikes. Interestingly, the heart rate tracker was a bit delayed in testing, but once CNET reviewed the data in the health app, the data had corrected to be largely accurate. You also get high and low heart rate alerts, though no ECG app. (The $249 Apple Watch SE 3 also omits this feature.).

Industry observers note that in CNET's testing, the sleep tracker on the Fit 3 was useful, if not entirely accurate. The watch can detect your sleep stages and look out for snoring using your Galaxy phone's mic. Like other health trackers, you get a sleep score, but CNET found it a bit inaccurate, since it rated a six and a half hour sleep session "Excellent" (91/100).

In a recent development, still, the Fit 3 is really the only other smartwatch option at this price point that people should seriously consider. Until another organization drops a product around this MSRP, you have two solid choices in the Amazfit Bip 6 and Galaxy Fit 3.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it’s been almost five years since Canton, Massachusetts resident Karen Read found the body of her police-officer boyfriend John O’Keefe unresponsive in the snow in the early hours of Jan. 29, 2022. Since that day, the circumstances around O’Keefe’s death and the subsequent investigation have turned Read into one of the most divisive murder defendants in the nation. Now, a new docuseries is tackling the internet-famous case and the behind-the-scenes details people don’t know.

In a recent development, directed by Danielle Johnson Cutts and released Nov. 23, The Trials of Karen Read charts Read’s journey from unknown Canton resident to a true-crime mainstay. The fervor around Read’s trial was complicated by social media accounts alleging a police conspiracy was using Read as a scapegoat. The series’ biggest revelations focus less on chasing down the minute details of Read’s defense and more on building out a picture of O’Keefe that his family and friends say was lost in the fervor of Read’s case.

It has been revealed that “The intention was always to make a well-rounded series, and we wanted to try and tell this story from multiple firsthand perspectives,” Johnson Cutts told Netflix’s Tudum. She added that O’Keefe’s friends and family only spoke to “center John [in the story] and remind what has now become a global audience of their pain: [the fact] that they have lost a father figure, a brother, and a son. And that has very, very much been lost in the melee of the trials of Karen Read.”.

According to recent reports, it was supposed to be a routine night. On Jan. 28, 2022, Read and O’Keefe met friends at Canton’s Waterfall Bar and Grille and the group decided to keep the hangout going at the home of Brian Albert, a fellow police officer. Read has maintained that she was driving under the influence and has a shoddy memory of the night. She told police she dropped O’Keefe off at the house and returned in the early hours when she realized he hadn’t made it home, where she found him unresponsive in a snowbank. Police have a different theory: They believe Read backed up into O’Keefe with her car and then left him to freeze to death. She was arrested and charged with second-degree murder, manslaughter while operating under the influence of alcohol, and leaving the scene of personal injury and death. Read’s first trial, which started on April 16, 2024, ended with a mistrial. And at her second trial, which began on April 1, 2025, a jury acquitted Read of all charges except drunk driving, leaving her a free woman. “Johnny was the strong one and the pillar of strength,” O’Keefe’s brother, Paul O’Keefe, says in the documentary. “You want someone to be held accountable for taking a loved one from you. We just want justice for our loss.”.

Read and her representatives declined to participate in the three-part docuseries, but it does include  interviews from O’Keefe’s friends, family, and investigators involved in the case. It also shows some never-before-seen footage, including police cameras, O’Keefe’s home videos, and unreleased audio from an interview Read did in 2023 with Boston Magazine.

According to recent reports, “At the end of the day this was about John O’Keefe. And his death has become an absolute circus,” Jen McCabe, Albert’s sister-in-law, states in the docuseries. “People have profited off it and people have used it to destroy so many lives and the victim and his family, they lost. People should remember John and the amazing guy he was. Not Karen Read.”.

Here are four things we learned from The Trials of Karen Read.

Read and O’Keefe dated briefly in 2004 but reconnected after the Covid-19 pandemic. When they started dating exclusively in 2020, Canton residents and close friends of O’Keefe say that the two seemed very happy with each other. O’Keefe was the legal guardian of his niece and nephew, Kayley and Patrick Furbush, and they promptly welcomed Read into the fold. In her interview with Boston Magazine, Read mentioned she didn’t want to replace their deceased parents but wanted to be as helpful as possible — often staying over for days on end or making sure she was at recitals and sporting events with O’Keefe. Industry observers note that “She treated me like a friend,” Kayley, now about 18, states in the documentary. “She’s funny. She was always laughing or making us laugh. She meshed really well with me and my brother. I definitely thought Karen was going to be someone I could talk to and relate with the way my friends got to with their moms. That was exciting.”.

In a recent development, in the docuseries, O’Keefe’s friends say Read promptly fit into the group. “She was super nice. She was friendly. She was funny. She was outgoing,” McCabe says. “I loved her. I think John loved having a companion and someone to go out and have a good time with.”.

Sources indicate that mcCabe, who was friends with both O’Keefe and Read, was with Read when she discovered O’Keefe’s body, and says the scene was immediately chaotic. But even after police left, O’Keefe’s family and friends had unanswered questions about how exactly he died. When police arrested Read on Feb. 1, their theory was that Read had accidentally hit O’Keefe with her car and was so drunk she didn’t notice. But further investigations, including a data pull from her car, revealed her back up cameras and sensors were completely functional, making an accidental strike unlikely.

Sources indicate that read’s case promptly caught the attention of online true-crime enthusiasts. One of the most prominent YouTubers who first posted about the case was Aidan Kearney, known as Turtleboy on YouTube. Kearney posted dozens of videos claiming Read was being set up by the Canton Police Department; popularizing alternative theories about O’Keefe’s death, including the possibility of a fight inside Albert’s home or a dog attack. (Kearney did not participate in the documentary). He often showed up to homes of O’Keefe’s friends, or confronted them in public places like sporting events. He also hosted several “Free Karen Read” rallies and protests, one of which involved marching protestors by the homes of Albert and McCabe. He was especially focused on Colin Albert, a teen who he believed might have fought with O’Keefe and accidentally killed him.

According to recent reports, in the docuseries, Albert speaks out in a rare public interview and states Kearney’s video sent waves of targeted harassment towards him, both online and in person. “I am not the kid that these people were making me out as,” he says. “I am scared every single day about somebody coming up to me, whether they try to attack me, whether they try to do something horrible. I’m scared every day of my life for that.”.

During Read’s first trial, her defense team uncovered multiple text messages from.

Massachusetts State Police Trooper Michael Proctor, the lead investigator on her case, in which he referred to Read as a “bitch,” and a “wack job cunt,” adding “hopefully she kills herself.” This eroded trust in his investigation, and Proctor was fired in 2025 after months of suspension. On Nov. 10, Massachusetts State Police and Read settled a civil lawsuit alleging police misconduct during her arrest and trial. The suit claimed the department had “an embedded culture of bigotry, misogyny, systemic failures” and cited Proctor’s text messages.

Industry observers note that “I feel like I let down the O’Keefe family. I feel like I let down my family. I let down the state police, the DA’s office,” Proctor indicates in the docuseries, a rare look into his feelings on the public misstep. “I just feel like I let down so many people.”.

It has been revealed that two jurors for Read’s second trial, identified only by their first names in the docuseries, say that Read’s case was so substantial that the jurors couldn’t avoid news about it before the trial. Many of the people on the jury were aware of Read’s case before they heard any testimony and several were familiar with the internet theories of a police coverup or conspiracy.

In a recent development, “I don’t know if it was possible to find a jury that was a completely blank slate,” Jason, a juror, indicates in the series. It has been revealed that while the jury was torn on whether actual police corruption occurred, both jurors say that there were too many holes in the evidence and available testimony to prove that Read was guilty beyond a reasonable doubt. It’s a defining characteristic that not only determined Read’s fate but has continued to dog her case.

Industry observers note that “I really did think, most likely, that she did it,” Janet, the other juror, says. “But I think by our legal system’s standards, she’s not guilty because there were so many different possibilities. He could’ve gone into the house, he could’ve gotten beaten up, he could’ve got hit by a plow. It’s almost like ‘doubt, doubt, doubt’ kinda hanging out there. Three Reasons Not to Use ‘Buy Now, Pay Later’ During Black Friday

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1112 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, gone are the days of needing to wait until after Thanksgiving to shop some seriously substantial Black Friday sales.
  • While BNPL plans can allow you to pay for purchases in installments without interest, they come with a cost that can easily outweigh any substantial discounts.
  • According to recent reports, to be clear, Amazon doesn't have its own buy now, pay later program, and the company is not uniquely misleading on this front.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, gone are the days of needing to wait until after Thanksgiving to shop some seriously substantial Black Friday sales. As you're adding item after item to your cart during the sale, you might be tempted by offers for an "affordable monthly payment system." Also known as "buy now, pay later" (BNPL), the pitch is a tempting one: Buy what you need now, and pay later, "on your own timeline." But as convenient as it sounds, you should think twice before using buy now, pay later options, whether during Black Friday, Cyber Monday, or at any other time.

While BNPL plans can allow you to pay for purchases in installments without interest, they come with a cost that can easily outweigh any substantial discounts. Let's take a look at the hidden costs of BNPL, and why you're better off paying upfront for all your Black Friday purchases.

According to recent reports, to be clear, Amazon doesn't have its own buy now, pay later program, and the company is not uniquely misleading on this front. The process is straightforward: you choose your items, select Affirm (a third-party lender) at checkout, complete a quick application, and receive an instant decision on your loan terms. Individual transactions initiated through Affirm are limited to $25,000, with a daily maximum of $100,000 across multiple purchases—but of course, your Black Friday splurge will be nowhere near that big, right? (Right?!).

According to recent reports, the main draw of these programs is the ability to "pay at your own pace." If you are required to pay a down payment, that is due at the time of the transaction. From there, your first monthly payment is usually due one month after your purchase is processed. Each following payment will be due one month later, on the same day of the month.

Sources indicate that you can choose your own timeline, usually spanning 3, 6, 12, or 24 months, depending on the purchase amount and your creditworthiness. Unlike traditional credit cards, Affirm demonstrates you the exact payment amount and total cost upfront, and claims no hidden fees or compound interest.

You need a separate Affirm account in addition to your Amazon Prime membership. The application process requires basic information, including your name, mobile phone number, date of birth, and the last four digits of your Social Security number. Affirm performs a soft credit check initially, which doesn't impact your credit score, though they may conduct a hard inquiry for some loans.

BNPL looks are helpful if you really need to finance something major, but whenever possible, it’s best to avoid taking on debt for everyday expenses.

Industry observers note that the ease of this sort of financing can make expensive purchases feel more affordable than they actually are. When you can buy a $1,000 tablet for "just $67 per month," it's easy to lose sight of the total cost, as well as your overall financial picture. In turn, this makes it all too easy to overspend on items you might not have purchased otherwise. You're better off taking a breath, stepping away from your shopping cart, and setting alerts to be notified when a product hits a price you can stomach, at a time you can afford it.

Despite what you may have heard in the past, BNPL providers may report to credit bureaus, meaning your BNPL purchases can in fact affect your credit score. For instance, all Affirm payments (including on-time, late, and missed payments) are now reported to the credit bureau Experian. So if you miss payments or default on the installment proposal, it will cause damage to your credit score—making it even harder to get approved for mortgages, auto loans, credit cards, and other financing down the road.

Still, not all BNPL providers report to credit bureaus or use the same type of credit check, so it’s crucial to understand the specific terms and practices of any service you’re considering.

When you use a credit card, you get valuable purchase protections like extended warranty coverage, price protection, and the ability to dispute fraudulent charges. BNPL prepares generally don't come with these safeguards. This means you're on the hook if something goes wrong with your BNPL purchase and the retailer doesn't make things right. The smarter move is to only buy what you can afford during a sale, no matter how tempting those deals may seem.

Although installment plans are helpful if you really need to finance something major, it’s best to avoid taking on debt for everyday expenses. Better to wait for a good price for something you truly need and can afford to pay for right now.

If there's a significant-ticket item on sale for Black Friday but it's still out of your budget, consider these two questions before you turn to BNPL through Affirm:.

Is this really an essential purchase? BNPL should really only be used on completely necessary purchases that you can’t afford right now, but can afford in six weeks. On that note...

Will I be able to pay this off within six weeks? When a bigger payment gets broken down into smaller installments, you might find yourself overspending in the long run, because it "feels" like you can afford it. Stay on top of how much you’re actually spending—especially if you're considering multiple BNPL purchases—and how it will impact your overall budget going forward.

For more information about deals and discounts, keep an eye on all of Lifehacker's Black Friday coverage.

Sources indicate that in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

It has been revealed that follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

In a recent development, the best thing you can do is compare the prices with other retailers that have Black Friday sales. If that seems like too much work, you can just follow our Black Friday coverage (we're already doing all the searching and vetting for you). Some other tips are making sure you're not being sold an older or cheaper version and always reading reviews.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ted Sarandos has never hid his love for Old Hollywood, and now the Netflix co-CEO has a 55-acre and 98-year old piece of Tinseltown property.

After months of negotiations, speculation and reporting by Deadline that things were moving ahead, Netflix has bought the iconic Radford Studio Center in Studio City. The anticipated auction of the property today proved a bit of a non-event as Goldman Sachs-led lenders pulled the lot back and sold it directly to the streamer.

Netflix paid $380 million for Radford.

Industry observers note that A CBS hub over the decades and once dubbed Republic Studios decades ago, Radford has “22 stages, 210,000 square feet of office space and 172,737 square feet of support space,” according to its specs. Watch on Deadline.

As part of today’s purchase, with paperwork being filed as we speak, Netflix also paid the pricey ULA transfer tax that goes with the acquisition, I hear.

In a recent development, with 1,000 Netflix employees let go last month, execs such as Content chief Bela Bajaria ousted last month, dissent among the ranks, and the stock still struggling, the optics around such a big outlay of cash might not look so good. But this is Hollywood, where perception is reality and the Sarandos and Greg Peters-led streamer is leaning into a narrative of being good industry citizens in today’s purchase to give some gloss to the whole thing.

“There’s still a long way to go, but we are hopeful that with the partnership of the State of California and the City of Los Angeles, this will be the start of a meaningful new investment in California’s film industry,” Netflix stated today of the purchase and the future it envisions for Radford as a production hub in what has been some very tough times for the home of Hollywood the past five years.

With facilities in various states of readiness in New Mexico, plus tax credits-rich New York and New Jersey, the streamer Tuesday went full Randy Newman about L.A.

“This city is home to us,” they exclaimed. “We’re excited to keep investing here and finding more ways to entertain the world, while supporting the writers, builders, electricians, drivers, designers, and talent who make L.A., California, and the entertainment industry so special.”.

To the over 50,000 industry workers who have seen their jobs disappear since 2020 that can’t help but sound like hope. The statement (see the full missive below) also can’t help but remind some of the threats to leave L.A. that Skydance was leaking like crazy in its ultimately successful effort to seal the $111 billion merger of Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery earlier this summer.

Netflix plans extensive renovations at the 1928-opened Radford, especially being that previous owner Hackman Capital Partners, who bought the lot off what was then ViacomCBS for $1.85 billion in 2021, never finished their own upgrades before losing the property to creditors. To that, Netflix has engaged real estate and infrastructure organization ZVantage and gear group Cinelease to shepard the literal and figurative re-branding of the sprawling joint.

In a recent development, having said that, nothing’s gonna change for a while at either Netflix’s Sunset Blvd-leased HQ or for the current renters at the former CBS hub. Sticking to their current leases, the streamer plans to stay at the Hollywood locations until around late 2031. As for those already at Radford, a source close to the situation tells me that “business will continue as usual on the lot in the near term, including for productions that are currently filming on the lot.”.

Business as usual, in an ever-changing business — and Ted finally got his lot.

Read the full statement from Netflix on the purchase Of Radford Studio Center here:.

According to recent reports, unless you work in entertainment or live in Los Angeles, you may not have heard of Radford Studio Center. But you’ve probably seen something that was made there.Opened in 1928, at the end of the silent film era, Radford has been home to a long list of classic indicates — from Gunsmoke and Gilligan’s Island to The Mary Tyler Moore Show, Seinfeld, and That ‘70s Show, among many, many others.Today, we’re proud to share that Netflix is purchasing Radford to build on that history and strengthen our investment in Los Angeles and California.Netflix was founded in California, and we opened our first office in L.A. more than two decades ago. Since then, many of our shows like early favorites Grace and Frankie and GLOW have filmed in L.A., as have more recent series and films like Nobody Wants This, The Lincoln Lawyer, The Rip and The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth. This year alone, more than 45 of our shows and movies are confirmed to film across L.A.We’ve also engaged ZVantage, Zello’s entertainment advisory division, to support the transition and next chapter of the iconic lot through its operating platform, Backlot Studio Services. As part of the engagement, Cinelease will serve as a production equipment provider at the studio, further enhancing the infrastructure and services available to the production community. Working together, our goal is to maintain operational continuity, retain the existing studio team and strengthen Radford’s position as a premier production destination.There’s still a long way to go, but we are hopeful that with the partnership of the State of California and the City of Los Angeles, this will be the start of a meaningful upcoming investment in California’s film industry.This city is home to us. We’re excited to keep investing here and finding more ways to entertain the world, while supporting the writers, builders, electricians, drivers, designers, and talent who make L.A., California, and the entertainment industry so special.

Despite the fact that it’s still showing in theaters, You Can See Everything is available to stream at home; the film is available to rent for $19.99 or buy for $24.99 on PVOD platforms like Amazon, Apple TV, and Fandango at Home.

Recent findings suggest that distributor A24 has not yet unveiled a Blu-ray or subscription streaming release. The film will eventually land on HBO Max because of A24’s pay-1 deal with the streaming service.

In a recent development, you Can See Everything, directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, ups the ante on Fielder’s brand of intimate, awkward interactions. In the film, he spends over a month living with Elizabeth Holmes and her partner, Billy Evans, just before Holmes heads to prison for financial crimes related to her failed biotech organization, Theranos. The documentary also marks a major year for Oppenheim, who helmed this year’s acclaimed Robert Pattinson-starring Primetime.

In a recent development, you Can See Everything features a surprisingly significant appearance by Amanda Seyfried, who played Holmes in the Hulu series The Dropout. The series was one of a number of films and books about Holmes, whose case became one of the most notorious financial crimes of the 21st century. Yet somehow, You Can See Everything managed to frame the story in an entirely fresh light, in part thanks to Seyfried’s appearance.

Sources indicate that in an extensive interview with Rolling Stone, Seyfried discussed her eagerness to be a part of the film with Fielder and Oppenheim. “When you needed me, I came because of how invested you were, and how I felt like we were all on the same page at a point,” she said to the co-directors. “We were like a band. We were like a team. It felt like part of the team. And when I felt part of the team, it made me want to go even further. It’s not necessarily about being safe, but about doing something different.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that “It just works” is one of the phrases most commonly associated with Apple. Interestingly, it appears to have been coined by the organization’s customers and then used by reviewers before it was later picked up by Steve Jobs.

Of course, it’s now commonly used ironically when Apple products don’t do what they are supposed to (Apple Home, I’m looking at you), but I do think that it’s absolutely the right philosophy and goal – most of the time ….

Industry observers note that macworld referenced an Apple brochure from 1996 entitled “Why do people prefer Macintosh?” This is a collection of testimonials from customers, a number of whom use the “it just works” phrasing. It was subsequently used by a number of reviewers. The earliest example I can find of Steve Jobs adopting it was in 1999, when discussing the rollout of FireWire to the Mac in the PowerMac G3.

It’s hot-pluggable. You don’t have to turn your computer off to connect and disconnect peripherals, you can just plug them right in. Again, the drivers are dynamically loaded. There are no terminators and there are no switches. It just works.

(If you have a link to any earlier example, please do let me know in the comments.).

In a recent development, I’m a big fan of the philosophy. Most of the time, owners should just be able to get on with the tasks they want to execute without having to worry about the technology. The tech that makes it all possible should sit there quietly in the background.

However, there are cases where I think Apple takes this approach a little too far, and where tech-savvy consumers at least would like a little more transparency and control.

AirPods firmware updates are a good example. Back in September, there was quite a significant update in the form of custom EQ. It’s a rather basic version, but still a feature many had wanted for a long time. Instead of being able to manually trigger the update, users had to wait until it “just worked.”.

According to recent reports, apple’s support document has a how-to guide that is essentially an outline of the conditions required to permit an enhancement, and an instruction to simply wait until it happens. Which you will only know by repeatedly checking.

In a recent development, make sure your AirPods are connected via Bluetooth to your iPhone, iPad or Mac. Connect your charging case to a power source. Put your AirPods in their charging case and close the lid. Keep the lid of the charging case closed, and keep your AirPods in Bluetooth range of your iPhone, iPad or Mac. Wait at least 30 minutes for the firmware to be updated. Check the firmware version again.

Recent findings suggest that another example, and one I’ve complained about before, is that there is no way to manually trigger an iCloud document sync, nor any progress indicator when it does finally happen. In the best of cases, it takes seconds; in the worst, many hours. And again, the only way to find out is to repeatedly check.

It’s the same story when shooting a video on your iPhone. Will it still be there an hour later, available to instantly edit and view? Maybe, or maybe it will have been offloaded to the cloud, requiring it to be downloaded before you can do anything with it – while a video you shot months earlier is still stored locally on the device! You can, of course, switch off optimization altogether, but if you choose to use it, you get no control over it. I want a setting that allows me to do things like specify local retention of all photos and videos taken within the past fortnight.

According to recent reports, will that video be available in the Mac Photos app when you check half an hour later? Maybe, maybe not. You can click the Sync Now button as many times as you like, and it will apparently have no effect, claiming it’s up to date despite the video being entirely absent. It will be there when it’s there.

Once it is in the Photos app on your Mac, it’s a similar story when exporting it to a folder. You can drag and drop the video into the folder, and this time you are manually triggering the transfer (yay!), but there will be absolutely no visual indication that it is in progress. No grayed-out icon, no progress bar, nothing. So far as the user interface is concerned, it appears that your drag and drop had no effect – until the video file finally appears.

It has been revealed that I think with all of these things and more, Apple needs to offer options. Yes, most non-tech users may be perfectly happy to just wait until things happen, but there ought to be a standard way to trigger things that right now happen in their own sweet time, as well as progress indicators and confirmation that a process is complete.

Sources indicate that is this an ecosystem-wide improvement you’d like to see? Please share your thoughts in the comments and add any frustrating examples of your own.

  • If you’re on the fence about signing up for (or renewing) your Prime membership, here’s how to judge whether or not the benefits outweigh the $139 cost.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Friday isn't until Nov. 27, but Amazon's early Black Friday sales have been ramping up for several days. For frequent Amazon shoppers, Prime can quickly pay for itself—mostly thanks to the free shipping perk. But how does the math shake out if you aren't regularly ordering from Amazon? Is it worth signing up if you only shop during major sales?

Millions of Amazon Prime users currently pay $14.99 per month or $139 per year for their memberships—though other plans cost less if you qualify. For example, the Amazon Prime Student program allows young adults between the ages of 18 and 24 to get all of the Prime perks for half the cost—$7.49 per month or $69 annually.

If you’re on the fence about signing up for (or renewing) your Prime membership, here’s how to judge whether or not the benefits outweigh the $139 cost.

Here are the main perks of Amazon Prime that make it worth the cost for so many owners.

Free two-day shipping on millions of items: This is the main draw of Prime. If you shop frequently on Amazon and want quick free delivery, the shipping perks alone may make Prime worthwhile. Prime members also get free same-day delivery on over 3 million items in eligible areas. The ultra-fast (and morally suspect) shipping usually costs $9.99 per order for non-members, though you can choose lower-cost or free shipping options if you're willing to place larger orders and wait longer to receive them.

It has been revealed that access to Prime Video: Prime includes unlimited streaming of movies, TV shows, and Amazon Originals. If you ask me, the content library isn’t as robust as Netflix or Hulu, but this is still an added value.

Other Prime benefits: You also get Amazon Music for streaming songs, Prime Reading for ebooks, magazines, and audiobooks; Prime gaming, free photo storage, and occasional exclusive discounts/deals.

Amazon Prime Rewards Visa card: Cardholders get 5% back on Amazon/Whole Foods purchases. Prime members who use this card extensively can earn rewards that offset the annual fee.

Number of people: Prime benefits can be shared with other members of your household. The more users, the more value per person.

Let's say you don't care about Prime Video, Amazon Music, or free e-books, and just want to know if you'll save money you would otherwise be spending on shipping.

Sources indicate that for non-Prime members, Amazon requires a minimum order of $35 to qualify for free shipping on eligible items. The average shipping costs for non-members aren't publicly listed, and can vary by item and shipping speed, typically ranging from $5 to $10.

Industry observers note that for our purposes, I messed around on my non-shared, non-Prime Amazon account to find an average shipping cost of around $6 per order (assuming the order total fell below the $35 threshold, of course). Of course, shipping costs will vary depending on the item and how rapidly you want it, but let’s compare the cost to the appeal of Prime’s two-day shipping option. So, we have the cost of individual online orders (around six bucks) compared to the free delivery that comes with an $139 annual fee. This means the costs you’d save on shipping alone make Prime worth the cost as long as you place more than two dozen orders in a year.

In other words: The $139 annual fee pays for itself as long as you order from Amazon Prime at least twice a month.

In a recent development, of course, this conclusion is strictly in terms of shipping costs. How it stacks up ethically is between you and the person in the mirror.

And then there's this key caveat: You can still get free shipping from Amazon without a Prime membership, provided your order has $35 or more of eligible items. However, this won't grant you Prime shipping speed—your order will typically take five to eight days to be delivered. But you can place fewer, larger orders and wait a little longer, and still never pay for shipping.

According to recent reports, also worth considering is how much of that membership cost you'll be able to recoup via exclusive Prime Day offers. During the sale, some items will be heavily discounted only for Prime members—but whether the Prime Day price is really a "deal" will vary greatly based on the item you're buying. Some of those "big discounts" aren't any greater than what the item typically sells for. The Prime Day price can even be higher than other sale prices throughout the year. That's why it's crucial to make sure what you're ordering is something you planned to buy anyway—and that the sale price is actually a true bargain—before you order.

Recent findings suggest that the cost of a Prime membership is a solid value for anyone using Amazon 23 times per year or more—especially if you're also watching shows on Prime Video or purchasing something that is deeply discounted for Prime Day. But if you only shop on Amazon a few times a year and don't take advantage of Prime Day offers or the other benefits, then that $139 annual fee isn't necessarily paying for itself.

Sources indicate that yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.
