If You Loved 'Cupertino,' There's One Movie You Need to Watch Next

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1034 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that cupertino is one of those TV shows that arrived just when we all needed it.
  • Just like Cupertino, The Social Network arrived at precisely the right moment in history—just when everyone was beginning to wonder if the social media revolution kicked off by Facebook and Mark Zuckerberg was actually a good idea or not.
  • At its core, The Social Network is a legal drama—the framing narrative involves dual lawsuits brought against Zuckerberg and the depositions he is giving, which prompt flashbacks to the formation and success of Facebook in the early 2000s.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that cupertino is one of those TV shows that arrived just when we all needed it. In this economy, a story about two lawyers who get shafted by the “move fast and break things” culture of Silicon Valley and decide to use their legal chops to fight back was almost destined to be a hit, and the great performances by Mike Colter and Rachel Keller sealed the deal. If you love the sharp legal wrangling and tech-focused storylines and want a movie that perfectly complements the show, it’s time to watch (or re-watch) Aaron Sorkin and David Fincher’s 2010 masterpiece, The Social Network.

Just like Cupertino, The Social Network arrived at precisely the right moment in history—just when everyone was beginning to wonder if the social media revolution kicked off by Facebook and Mark Zuckerberg was actually a good idea or not. While it might seem hard to imagine, there was a time when Facebook was the social media platform—everyone was on it, and it dominated the conversation like nothing else. And the outsized wealth and influence Zuckerberg accrued as a result were just starting to make people a little uneasy.

At its core, The Social Network is a legal drama—the framing narrative involves dual lawsuits brought against Zuckerberg and the depositions he is giving, which prompt flashbacks to the formation and success of Facebook in the early 2000s. Like Cupertino, the story is soaked in the “apologize later” culture of tech startups, and traces the ruthlessness and cold genius of Zuckerberg as he cements his control over the platform, ices out former partners, and generally behaves like a sociopathic genius (Jesse Eisenberg’s performance as Zuckerberg is coldly compelling).

The film doesn’t have any kind of clear-cut ending where the good guys win, but there’s a certain satisfaction in the way Sorkin’s script and Eisenberg’s performance strip away the glamour of Zuckerberg’s money and success, reducing him in many ways to an aggrieved loner who translated his rage into a brilliant idea, and then has to isolate himself from everyone in order to maintain his control over it. The Zuckerberg depicted in the film is a lonely, bitter dude, and it’s as much of a happy ending as you’ll get. It’s a fascinating story of legal maneuvering and bickering lawyers against a backdrop of one of the foundational social media moments that shaped modern culture, and fans of the show will dig it. Stream The Social Network on Pluto or rent it on Prime Video.

Still craving legal drama, tech-sector skulduggery, or more David-versus-Goliath courtroom fireworks? Here are a few more movies that fans of Cupertino will love.

It’s set nowhere near Silicon Valley, but Michael Clayton is a real barn-burner of a paranoid legal thriller. George Clooney plays the title role, a “fixer” for a substantial-money law firm. When his mentor and friend, Arthur Edens (Tom Wilkinson), suffers a mental breakdown while working on a case involving a toxic weedkiller produced by one of the firm’s clients and becomes a security threat, he’s assassinated, and Clayton is forced to reckon with his role in the world and how much injustice he’s willing to tolerate in exchange for money. It’s tense, smart, and has a wonderfully satisfying conclusion that fans of legal dramas where the good guys are willing to sacrifice (and win) will cheer. Rent Michael Clayton on Prime Video.

Based on real events, Dark Waters will appeal to anyone who likes to see smart lawyers take on enormous corporations in a search for the truth. A successful corporate lawyer, Robert Bilott (Mark Ruffalo), looks into a series of bizarre cattle deaths in rural West Virginia and stumbles onto evidence that the DuPont corporation has been dumping illegal, unregulated chemicals into the groundwater. Bilott’s years-long effort to hold DuPont responsible for the health impact on the community nearly costs him everything, but his determination to make the system work is ultimately the kind of inspiring legal story fans of Cupertino will appreciate. Rent Dark Waters on Prime Video.

If you just want the simple pleasures of a thrilling legal procedural, you can’t do much better than A Civil Action. John Travolta (at the height of his comeback) plays attorney Jan Schlichtmann, who takes on a class action lawsuit against two huge corporations because he thinks the case will be lucrative and relatively straightforward. As the case saps his resources and brings his firm to the brink of collapse, however, Schlichtmann slowly realizes that he’s fighting for more than just a massive payday. Fair warning: This isn’t a feel-good movie in many ways, but it definitely brings those David-versus-Goliath vibes that Cupertino trades in. Rent A Civil Action on Prime Video.

Sources indicate that the true story behind the effort to license the video game Tetris from the Soviet-era Russian government doesn’t have the same stakes as many of the stories in Cupertino, and it’s certainly no longer timely. But the globe-trotting legal maze that Henk Rogers (Taron Egerton) must navigate to secure the rights, which seem to keep twisting and slipping from his grasp as various political and corporate interests weigh in, is just as fun and fascinating as the legal battles on the show. Tetris may no longer be a novel sensation in the gaming world, but it’s fascinating to see how something so baked into modern pop culture achieved that status. Stream Tetris on Apple TV or rent it on Prime Video.

If your favorite part of Cupertino is its exploration of the way tech companies impact our lives, and the way decisions made in obscure corporate offices can have enormous consequences, BlackBerry will be a favorite. Based on true events, it tells the story of how Research in Motion (RIM) created what was, for a time, the most dominant phone in the world—and how the company lost everything when its leaders took their eye off the ball and let personal obsessions and grudges impede their work. With a cast that includes Jay Baruchel and Glenn Howerton, this story of Silicon Valley hubris is right on target for Cupertino fans. Stream Blackberry on Netflix, Kanopy, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

Signal now blocks screenshots on iPhone to stop Siri AI from seeing chats

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, popular secure messaging app Signal has rolled out a latest update that automatically disables screenshots for the sake of blocking Siri AI from reading your chats. Here are the details.

Signal’s latest app patch on iPhone disables a key system feature: taking screenshots.

As Signal told Reuters, that’s because Apple doesn’t currently provide better tools for iOS developers to safeguard app content from Siri AI and third-party AI agents.

By default, owners who update and try to take a screenshot will see a message that says: “Screenshot prevented by ‘Block Siri AI’ setting.”.

Fortunately, there’s an easy workaround. Customers who want to re-enable screenshots can do so by visiting Signal’s privacy settings and turning off the new toggle that’s labeled ‘Block Siri AI.’.

Here’s 9to5Mac’s own Arin Waichulis:.

Signal now blocks in-app screenshots on iPhone to keep Siri AI from reading chatsIt’s a upcoming toggle in settings that’s on by default, but can be turned offNo equivalent for its Mac app pic.twitter.com/ImsinqMNPq.

Here’s exactly what that toggle does, per the in-app settings:.

Industry observers note that prevent Siri AI from scanning Signal content. This will also block you from taking screenshots in the app and App Switcher.

It’s good to see that owners can manually disable the upcoming privacy setting if they want. But Signal’s decision to block screenshots does raise notable questions about the potential gap in privacy tools for iOS developers.

In a recent development, apple already lets you block Siri AI from accessing whichever apps you manually exclude, and that became even easier in iOS 27.2. But rather than directing users to that system option, Signal seems to believe it needed to take action itself with this patch.

What do you think of Signal’s latest move? Let us know in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the Broadway League and IATSE Local One of theater workers have reached a tentative deal to avoid a strike that could have disrupted the lucrative holiday season. The agreement is pending ratification by union members.

In a joint statement from the League and the union, the two sides confirmed “they have reached a tentative agreement, pending ratification by the bargaining unit. The respective parties will inform their members of the details of this agreement in the coming days.”.

The union remarked details of the tentative agreement will be provided to Local One members ahead of the Local’s December membership meeting, when members will decide whether to ratify the agreement. That meeting is scheduled for December 20. Related Stories News 'Inter Alia' Starring Rosamund Pike Sells Out; 'Hamilton' With Christopher Jackson Tops $3M - Broadway Box Office News Steven Hack Dies: Actor On 'American Horror Story', 'Ratched', 'Marvel's Agent Carter', 'General Hospital'; Original Cast Member Of Broadway's 'Cats' Was 68.

It has been revealed that local One represents thousands of theater workers who build, install, maintain and operate Broadway’s productions systems including staging and scenery, lighting, sound, video and special effects. Watch on Deadline.

The union’s previous agreement with the League expired July 26, with negotiations underway since September. During that period, both sides agreed to narrow initial demands to focus on wage increases and benefits. Just recently Local One members authorized a strike if negotiations broke down.

In a recent development, separate negotiations between the League, the trade organization representing producers and theater owners, and the Theatrical Wardrobe Union IATSE Local 764 are ongoing. The local has authorized a strike if a deal isn’t reached.

It has been revealed that in its announcement about today’s deal, IATSE added, “Local 764 members have been bargaining with The Broadway League since June, and their previous agreement expired July 26. The League canceled bargaining sessions scheduled for November 18 and 19, and Local 764 has called on the League and Broadway producers to immediately set latest dates and return to the table.

“Among the major unresolved challenges are wages and a longstanding gender pay gap affecting Broadway wardrobe workers. Wardrobe work on Broadway has historically been performed predominantly by women and paid at significantly lower rates than stagehand classifications historically held predominantly by men. Although recent negotiations have narrowed that gap, Local 764 department heads today must work nearly 45 percent longer to earn pay comparable to workers in similar department-head roles.”.

Local 764 members, according to the union, are seeking an agreement “that continues progress toward pay equity and does not widen that longstanding disparity.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Are you ready for a rude reminder about the fragility of time? December is nearly here. Impossibly, we’re already heading into the final stretch of 2026, though at least the best streaming services are helping to soothe that calendar shock with a fresh slate of upcoming movies and TV reveals. And HBO Max, in particular, has a stacked lineup with which to spend your final weeks of the year.

Sources indicate that things kick off on December 1 with a fist-pumping throwback as an iconic, multi-decade boxing franchise — spanning from Sylvester Stallone’s 1976 classic to its modern spinoffs — steps into the ring. Elsewhere on the film front, a provocative comedic thriller led by the winning duo of Olivia Wilde and Cooper Hoffman makes its streaming debut on December 4, before an acclaimed sci-fi horror sequel lands later in the month to keep things spooky.

Over on the TV side, the platform is capping things off on Christmas Day with a polarizing latest series adaptation that kicks off a fresh era for a massive wizarding franchise. From nostalgic knockouts to broomstick-flying drama, here’s a guide to everything new on HBO Max in December 2026.

Industry observers note that one of the most talked-about new movies of the so-called "awards season" thus far has been "I Play Rocky," an underdog biopic starring Anthony Ippolito as Sylvester Stallone during the tumultuous production of his iconic boxing flick "Rocky," which famously went on to win the Oscar for Best Picture. But before you tune into that new bio-drama, why not go back to where it all started with a big "Rocky" movie marathon?

It has been revealed that helpfully, HBO Max isn't just bringing back the 1976 original — which is celebrating its major 50th anniversary this year and centers on a small-time Philadelphia boxer (Stallone) who gets a once-in-a-lifetime chance to face the world heavyweight champion in the ring — but all nine films in the "Rocky" franchise beginning on December 1. That includes the "Rocky" sequels “Rocky II” (1979), “Rocky III” (1982), “Rocky IV” (1985), “Rocky V” (1990) and “Rocky Balboa” (2006), as well as the Michael B. Jordan-led "Creed" spinoff trilogy comprising “Creed” (2015), “Creed II” (2018) and “Creed III” (2023).

That should keep you busy until Fresh Year's, right?

Stream "Rocky" on HBO Max starting December 1.

Few Hollywood stars had a 2026 like Olivia Wilde, who directed arguably the year's best comedy, "The Invite," and also pops up opposite Pedro Pascal in the cellist dramedy "Behemoth!" and alongside Cooper Hoffman in this Gregg Araki-directed erotic comedy.

In "I Want Your Sex," Wilde plays renowned artist and provocateur Erika Tracy, who takes fresh-faced twentysomething Elliot Bell (Hoffman) as her assistant and sexual muse. As their arrangement begins to blur professional and personal lines, Elliot is pulled into a world of sexuality, obsession, power, betrayal and murder.

Along with Wilde and Hoffman, the star-studded cast includes Charli XCX, Mason Gooding, Chase Sui Wonders, Johnny Knoxville, Margaret Cho and Daveed Diggs.

Stream "I Want Your Sex" on HBO Max starting December 4.

One of the most anticipated TV titles of the year has also been its most controversial, drawing backlash over J.K. Rowling's involvement, casting choices, and, most odd of all, children's teeth. Regardless, plenty of HBO viewers will undoubtedly be tuning into another year at the Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry, with a fresh set of fresh faces playing some of modern-day literature's most iconic characters.

The eight-episode series will follow pretty much the same plotline as the first "Harry Potter" book and subsequent film, with Dominic McLaughlin as Harry Potter, Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger, Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley, John Lithgow as Albus Dumbledore, Janet McTeer as Minerva McGonagall, and Paapa Essiedu as Severus Snape.

Stream "Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone" on HBO Max starting December 25.

The Best Last-Minute Gifts That Don't Feel Last Minute

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that we’ve all experienced gift panic—that sinking feeling when you realize you need a present in an hour and you just don’t have one to give.
  • With the right presentation, even the most last-minute gift can read as thoughtful.
  • A handwritten note that contains a shared memory or personal joke can elevate a present.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that we’ve all experienced gift panic—that sinking feeling when you realize you need a present in an hour and you just don’t have one to give. Whether you spent all year chasing the “perfect” gift or simply procrastinated, your time is nearly up. But don’t panic. The clock may have nearly run out, but your options haven’t. Before you resort to re-gifting something from the back of a closet, here’s how to pull off a last-minute gift that is effortless but feels elevated and worthy of the person you’re giving it to.

With the right presentation, even the most last-minute gift can read as thoughtful. Any performer will tell you that the difference between a good show and a bad one comes down to commitment and confidence. The same is true for last-minute gifts: If you act like your gift is thoughtful and intentional, they’ll think it is. The biggest mistake people make is apologizing as they hand over a present—nothing ruins a vibe faster than, “Sorry this is so last-minute.” So give with confidence.

And focus on presentation. A handwritten note that contains a shared memory or personal joke can elevate a present. Use simple but personal wrapping; craft paper and twine, or a reusable gift bag that looks like you planned ahead. Add a small flourish, like a sprig of holly or a fancy bow. Small touches can make it seem like you’ve carefully prepared. What you don’t want are obvious panic gifts that scream, “I grabbed this on the way here.” The goal is effortless, not frantic.

Recent findings suggest that digital gifts are your friends. You can order something in minutes that arrives instantly online, and with a little thought, will still read as personal and intentional. The trick is choosing a present that speaks to the recipient’s tastes, hobbies, or quirks, and pairing it with a small note to show you remember what they love. From e-books to streaming subscriptions, these gifts hit the sweet spot of thoughtful and last-minute. Here are some suggestion:.

When time is running out, gift cards are your secret weapon. They arrive instantly online, don’t require shipping, and with the right presentation, they can feel surprisingly thoughtful. The key is to pick a card that fits the recipient’s interests and add a personal note. The more specific you are, the better. If your giftee is into Italian food, get them an Eataly gift card. If they're a PC gamer, get them a Steam card. If they're into education, a membership to Skillshare is perfect. There's a gift card out there for just about any interest, and all you have to do it google it and email it.

Generic gift cards can be a last-minute lifesaver that can still seem a little personal if you give them the right way.

According to recent reports, pick a theme or design: Many online cards, like Amazon, Etsy, or Starbucks, let you choose designs. The right visual makes the card feel more intentional.

Recent findings suggest that include a warm, personal message: Even one line can make a digital card feel thoughtful—something like, “I couldn’t pick just one thing for you. Hope this helps you treat yourself.”.

Send strategically: Deliver the card by email or text, but consider printing the email or screenshotting it in a small envelope so it feels like a “real” gift.

It has been revealed that sign someone up for a subscription service, write a note explaining you want to keep giving them presents all year, and you're golden. Here are some suggestions:.

SnackCrate: This service sends a different snack from around the world every month.

SpiceClub: For the culinary adventurer on your list. A subscription to RawSpiceBar’s Spice Club delivers a curated selection of spices every month.

It has been revealed that mocktail Club: Booze-free fancy drinks delivered once a month? Sign me up.

Thera Box: If you know someone in need of some self-care, this once-a-month box is packed with wellness and relaxation items.

Loot Crate: If your giftee is geeky, consider this monthly surprise box of pop culture treasures.

It has been revealed that cameo is a platform where celebrities, influencers, musicians, and performers create personalized video messages for fans. If someone on your list is a fan of someone on Cameo, you can set up a session, and give a card with a mysterious note like "Keep an eye out for a special message." They'll be delighted with a personal message from wrestling legend Mick Foley or terrified when Chris Hansen appears on their screen; your choice.

I have enough crap in my house, so I love getting experiences instead of things. The challenge with experience gifts is usually timing: Many require reservations or coordination, but there are plenty of options that let your giftee schedule the time, making them perfect last-minute gifts.

Museum membership cards: Many institutions sell digital gift memberships that the recipient can activate whenever they like.

Movie tickets: Your local multiplex probably has a gift certificate you can buy online.

Local attraction passes: Some city attractions offer gift cards or “anytime admission” tickets that don’t expire immediately.

Pair these with a note explaining why you chose the experience, or, if you have that kind of relationship, something like, "I want to take you to the Museum of Modern Art." Just make sure you follow through and actually go.

Sometimes, there’s literally no time to order, wrap, or even think about a gift. If you’re scrambling out the door and need something now, you might be able to fake your way through, even if you're stopping at the liquor store on the way to the Christmas party.

According to recent reports, flowers or a small potted plant: Give a seasonal bouquet or a small indoor plant. Add a handwritten note, even a single line, and it might come off as thoughtful.

Gourmet chocolates or candy: Specialty chocolates from a local shop or grocery store display can feel luxe with a little ribbon or bag.

In a recent development, wine, craft beer, or non-alcoholic beverage: A bottle with a clean label or interesting packaging immediately elevates your gift. Ask the clerk at the liquor store to help you find something unique.

Lottery tickets: Who wouldn't appreciate a bunch of scratch-off lottery tickets?

Hard cash is the most impersonal gift of all, but the only one you know will be used. This gift really depends on the person getting it, so be aware of whether they're likely to think "Just what I wanted!" or "Wait, I'm not poor." If you give cash, make sure it's crisp bills in a nice card, with a personalized note.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iOS 27 gives the Messages app a variety of welcome upgrades, including one I’ve found myself using a lot: a Smart Reply feature that’s now personalized to the user’s writing style.

When the first wave of Apple Intelligence features were confirmed in 2024, one that I immediately thought sounded useful was Smart Reply.

In a recent development, the idea behind Smart Reply is simple. Rather than needing to manually type out replies in Messages and Mail, your iPhone can offer prewritten replies you can choose and send with a couple taps.

Great in theory, but the ‘Smart’ part of Smart Reply struggled to materialize in iOS 18.

Fortunately, with a key Apple Intelligence upgrade in iOS 27, the fresh version of the feature finally lives up to its name. Per Apple:.

Smart Reply in Mail and Messages can now draw on a user’s personalized writing style.

In a recent development, before, Smart Reply would look at the context of a conversation to craft its suggestions. But now, it also aims to match your writing style, punctuation, and tone.

Industry observers note that in iOS 18, I almost never used Smart Reply. That’s because despite being fine at suggesting replies that technically worked, those suggestions didn’t sound like me at all.

According to recent reports, that’s changed in iOS 27. Smart Reply now consistently impresses me. It no longer offers generic responses that sound like AI wrote them. Instead, its suggestions actually fit with my normal style of communication.

In a recent development, the only drawback is that right now, you’ll only ever see two Smart Reply suggestions. If Apple expanded the feature by letting you scroll horizontally through more options, I suspect I’d use Smart Reply even more.

Have you been using iOS 27’s Smart Reply feature in Messages? Let us know in the comments.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • First register your details to create a user profile for the hub, then login to access all content within the hub.
  • IEEE Spectrum Magazine, the flagship publication of the IEEE, explores the development, applications and implications of upcoming technologies.

Electronic products now pack circuits, structures, thermal paths, and packaging into very small spaces. These physical domains interact with one another. A packaging choice can change how a shock load reaches a circuit board. Such interactions are hard to predict. Most are found during physical qualification, late in development. At that stage, the design is mostly fixed. A failure leads to redesign, rebuilds, and retesting. Physical tests give strong evidence of robustness, but they give limited insight into load paths and failure margins. Traditional simulation gives more detail, but it needs specialist skills and long manual setup. This white paper explains how guided virtual validation brings shock and drop assessment into the design phase. It reviews common test configurations, model inputs, and acceptance criteria. A packaged drop case study then shows how packaging can be optimized across all drop orientations and checked against physical test results.

IEEE Spectrum Magazine, the flagship publication of the IEEE, explores the development, applications and implications of upcoming technologies. It anticipates trends in engineering, science, and technology, and provides a forum for understanding, discussion and leadership in these areas.

HomeKit Weekly: Lafaer’s 5-in-1 presence sensor fixes an annoying automation in Apple Home

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (716 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Motion-based automations are generally straightforward in Apple Home.
  • HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework.
  • In a recent development, A standard motion sensor uses PIR, which only detects movement, and that works fine in many situations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Motion-based automations are generally straightforward in Apple Home. The only carve-out is lighting, because some rooms are hard to judge by time of day alone. Depending on the windows and placement against the sun, some rooms might need light-based automations earlier in the day than others. The Lafaer 5-in-1 presence sensor fixes that with a light sensor most motion sensors lack, along with mmWave radar.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework.

In a recent development, A standard motion sensor uses PIR, which only detects movement, and that works fine in many situations. If you’re still for long periods, you’re invisible, and the automation assumes the room is empty. The Lafaer LWR02 pairs PIR with 2.4 GHz mmWave radar. The PIR-based motion sees you walking in, and the radar sees the minor stuff, like breathing and shifting on the couch, so the room stays “occupied” for as long as you are in it. The two together also reduce false positives from ceiling fans, curtains, and the dog, because the radar and PIR both must agree before the sensor reports motion.

In Apple Home, that highlights up as an occupancy sensor and a motion sensor from the same device.

“Turn on the lights when someone enters” is a common automation I use, but it can be tricky. What if you only want it when it’s not light outside? Doing it based on time of day sometimes works, but what about depending on where the windows are facing, etc.? You might have a room that gets darker an hour earlier than another room. “Turn on the lights when someone enters, and it’s dark in the room” is what the light sensor can handle for you.

Sources indicate that in the Home app, that means triggering a sensor for occupancy, then converting the automation into a Shortcut and adding a condition for the light level. It’s a few extra steps, but it does really give you more fine control over how it works.

Presence, motion, light, temperature, and humidity all come from the same device, and each one appears in Apple Home as its own sensor, so you can build automations around whichever ones fit the room.

Sources indicate that it’s IPX3-rated, so bathrooms, kitchens, and laundry rooms are fine to use in. Coverage is about 13 feet for presence and 26 for motion across about 120 degrees, which works in a bedroom, office, or bathroom. It’s not going to cover a great room from one corner. The base is a magnetic half sphere, so you can aim it, and it mounts with adhesive or sits on a shelf. I generally like to use the shelf for these types of sensors.

The Lafaer LWR02 is Matter over Thread, so it pairs directly with a HomePod, HomePod mini, or Apple TV 4K with no Lafaer hub or account needed. It runs on two included AAA batteries, is rated for up to two years, and rechargeable AAAs work with it as well. Thread is why a sensor doing this much can last that long on batteries. All sensor data is processed locally, so it only uses a trickle on the batteries.

Sources indicate that lights that turn off while you’re sitting still in the room are the reason a lot of people stop using motion automations in smart homes. The Lafaer LWR02 fixes that with mmWave radar and then lets you have more granular control of light-based automations based on what’s actually in the environment in the room, not just the time of day.

The Lafaer 5-in-1 presence sensor is available on Amazon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Rolling Stone may receive an affiliate commission.

The holidays are officially here, and while a new piece of jewelry or another thoughtful find is always a welcome surprise, some of the best gifts go beyond what you can unwrap, like the gift of knowledge. And there’s no one better to help you pass that along than MasterClass.

Right now, the online learning platform offers memberships starting as low as $5 per month for its Standard plan. You can also upgrade to the Plus plan for as low as $8 per month or the Premium plan for $10 per month.

MasterClass subscriptions deliver access to more than 200 courses. All of these courses are taught by bona fide experts — many of whom are also A-list names — and courses range from cooking lessons with Dominique Ansel to survival skills and wilderness training with Jessie Krebs. In other words, there’s something for almost every interest, and you don’t need to leave your living room to get started.

It has been revealed that if you’re looking to pick up a fresh skill, change careers, or just learn something new for fun, now is a great time to do so. Peruse the platform’s course list and take advantage of the affordable plans here.

In a recent development, the best way to save on MasterClass right now is to split a membership with friends or family. At the time of this writing, the Standard plan costs $5 per month and allows one user at a time, while the Plus plan costs $8 per month and can be shared between two users. The Premium plan, meanwhile, costs $10 per month and allows up to six users at once, making it the best value per person. Split the Premium plan among six people, and you’ll pay just $1.66 per person, per month.

MasterClass offers more than 200 courses (and counting) across a wide range of categories, from writing and music to business and branding. Just a few of the standout courses include “The Upcoming Rules of Business” with Kim Kardashian, “Dopamine” with Dr. Anne Lembke, “Designing a Home that Tells a Story” with Joanna Gaines, and creative writing with Margaret Atwood.

Created with beginners in mind, MasterClass courses focus on video lessons divided into short, easy-to-digest segments you can watch at your own pace. These lessons are accessible on your phone, laptop, tablet, or streaming device, so you can fit in a session whenever it works for you — whether on your lunch break or while traveling.

Beyond the video lessons, most MasterClass courses also include a workbook and opportunities for community interaction, giving you a chance to practice what you’ve learned and share your work with fellow students.

MasterClass also offers a more intensive type of course called “Sessions.” These begin on a set date, involve more hands-on work, and include more feedback from peers. 📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The holiday shopping season is here, and Apple’s AirPods are sure to be one of the most popular gifts.
  • AirPods 5 were introduced in September and come in two different versions.
  • Sources indicate that the case for the higher-end AirPods 5 ($149) supports wireless charging and Find My.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The holiday shopping season is here, and Apple’s AirPods are sure to be one of the most popular gifts. If you’re shopping for AirPods, Apple sells three different models: AirPods 5, AirPods Pro 3, and AirPods Max 2. Here’s how they compare.

AirPods 5 were introduced in September and come in two different versions. Unlike their predecessors, both versions of AirPods 5 offer Active Noise Cancellation. They differ in the charging case, battery life, and volume control. The base model AirPods 5 ($129) come with a case that can only charge via USB-C.

Sources indicate that the case for the higher-end AirPods 5 ($149) supports wireless charging and Find My. You also get one extra hour of battery life. The higher-end model also adds on-stem volume control, so you can adjust the volume just by swiping up or down on one of the earbud stems.

Here’s a full comparison between both AirPods 5 models:.

Recent findings suggest that the key thing about AirPods 5 is their open-ear design, unlike the in-ear design of the AirPods Pro 3 (more on those later). Even with that open-ear design, AirPods 5 offer incredible Active Noise Cancellation capabilities.

If you are shopping for AirPods 5, I do recommend spending the extra $20 to get the higher-end model. The better charging case alone is worth the extra money. With Find My integration and a built-in speaker, you can track your AirPods and play a sound from the case if you lose them.

If the person you’re shopping for doesn’t like in-ear earbuds, AirPods 5 are an excellent choice.

For most people, though, AirPods Pro 3 are probably the better choice ….

Industry observers note that airPods Pro 3 are Apple’s most capable earbuds, even with the introduction of AirPods 5 this year. They offer an in-ear fit and come with five foam-infused silicone ear tip sizes. With that in-ear design, AirPods Pro 3 can offer up to 3x stronger noise cancellation than AirPods 5. In my testing, this difference is notable.

AirPods Pro 3 also offer several other features you won’t find on AirPods 5, including a heart rate sensor for workouts, plus Hearing Test, Hearing Aid, and Hearing Protection features.

In a recent development, I still think AirPods Pro 3 are one of the best products in Apple’s lineup today. I wear mine for multiple hours every single day and can’t imagine life without them. I love the in-ear fit, and the ANC still impresses me, whether I’m at home or somewhere like a coffee shop.

In a recent development, if you know the person you’re shopping for (whether it’s yourself or someone else) likes the in-ear earbud design, I think AirPods Pro 3 are the best option. This is especially true when AirPods Pro 3 are on sale, like they are right now at $149. The price difference between AirPods 5 and AirPods Pro 3 is very small, and you’re getting a much better product.

Finally, we have AirPods Max. These are Apple’s only option for people who want AirPods in an over-ear headphone form factor. Last year, they were pretty hard to recommend since they’d gone five years without a real upgrade.

This year, however, Apple officially introduced AirPods Max 2, bringing modern features to Apple’s high-end headphones. This includes features like Adaptive Audio, Conversation Awareness, Personalized Volume, and more.

AirPods Max 2 are a far more compelling option than AirPods Max were at this time last year. They’re still pricey, but I love the aesthetics and find them very comfortable. There’s something about the premium aluminum design with an elegant Digital Crown that really stands out.

If you’re looking to splurge this holiday season, AirPods Max 2 are a great choice. For more realistic budgets, I think AirPods Pro 3 are the best option.

I upgraded to an Apple Watch Series 12 this fall (now $329 on Amazon), and there are four main features that make me especially glad I did.

The Apple Watch was overdue for a chip update, with Apple skipping any changes last year and not having any true performance upgrades since the S9.

I’m happy to report that the new S11 chip appears much faster and more capable than its predecessor, the S10.

Everyday tasks on Apple Watch Series 12 just feel fast. And Siri AI, a tentpole addition in watchOS 27, very much feels made for this latest hardware. Siri was sluggish on older hardware in my testing, but it performs much more like I’d hoped on Series 12.

Recent findings suggest that the fresh Health Sensing System makes Apple Watch Series 12 better at tracking key metrics like heart rate and steps. But this isn’t a case where accuracy is the only improvement.

Because of the fresh health sensors, Series 12 offers three complications not available before:.

Industry observers note that the complications let you see up-to-date readings on your current heart rate, step count, and readiness score right from your watch face. These are very welcome additions that meaningfully improve the Apple Watch’s health and wellness feature set.

I’ve been using the watchOS 27.3 beta, which adds a new Siri Recap feature for Series 12 models that I really love.

Siri Recap ambiently takes notes on your conversations throughout your day and creates high-level Apple Intelligence–generated summaries that you can use later to jog your memory, so you can stay present in the moment.

Most of what Siri documents, I’ll never need to reference and it gets deleted automatically. But for those times I have trouble remembering a key piece of information, I’ve found Siri Recap a very convenient addition.

Apple Watch Series 12 offers largely the same battery life as Series 11, though it will last 25% longer for outdoor workouts.

Sources indicate that more battery is always nice, but I’m especially a fan of the faster charging available on Series 12. Here’s how it stacks up to Series 11:.

I wear my Apple Watch to bed and generally try to top it off rapidly in the evening, but I’m not always great at giving it much time on the charger. With faster charging support on Series 12, my poor planning isn’t a problem.

Apple Watch Series 12 is now only $329 on Amazon, down from $399.

What if you make this the year you don't fill all the stockings with candy or gift cards? Both have their place, but if you want to make this the best Christmas ever, you have to shove some tech in those stockings. The good news: Tech gifts don’t have to be expensive to be impressive.

Industry observers note that no matter who you're shopping for, there are tons of affordable gizmos that are some combination of cool and useful and that feel pricier than they are. Here are 20 cool tech stocking stuffers to light up any holiday morning, all of which cost less than $50.

If there's an old-school gamer on your list, their Christmas morning will be extra merry if it includes a tiny video game emulator. R36T Retro Gaming Console ($48.98) puts over 18,000 video games in the palm of your hand. It has a 3.5" screen, so whether they like arcade classics or consoles-of-the-past, they can fit 'em all in a pocket.

Industry observers note that the Xteink X4 is an e-reader that's smaller than your phone. It uses e-ink like an Amazon Kindle, so you can whip a glare-free screen out of your pocket and start reading anywhere there's a light source. The X4 is a no-frills gadget—there's no lighting, touchscreen, or apps—but if you want a cheap, convenient way to read for around $50, it's perfect.

Recent findings suggest that those disposable cans of compressed air with the red straws are so 2015. Blow the dust off your electronics with an SDFM Electric Air Duster instead. With an engine that moves at 150,000 RPM, it shoots air such high speeds, the dust doesn't stand a chance. It's also cordless and comes with a variety of cleaning attachments to keep your gear in top shape.

Sources indicate that if your giftee likes to listen to music or podcasts while drifting off to sleep, the only gift better than a pair of sleep headphones is two pairs of sleep headphones! This two-pack retails for $22.99 and contains two headbands with built in speakers you can pair with your phone or other device easily.

It has been revealed that your giftee may have the tech side of their battle station/home office locked down, but I bet they don't have the aesthetics dialed in. Govee Smart LED Light Bars ($54.99, but currently on sale for $34.99) are programmable, colorful light bars that work with Alexa and Google Assistant and can display light effects created from 16 millions colors. It even syncs with your music to provide trippy visuals.

Sources indicate that my lifestyle doesn't involve cutting down trees, but I still need one of these miniature chainsaws. I mean, it's a chainsaw, and it's only six inches long. This Seeii mini chainsaw ($49.99) is battery-powered, so no one will be accidentally cutting the cord. According to the listing, it's suitable for tree pruning, garden artistry, shrub trimming, forest logging, and wood cutting.

In a recent development, you know what computer fiends are missing in their lives? Knobs. This little $33 gadget lets you assign functions to four external knobs and 12 push buttons, so you can finally have a decent volume control, scrub through video smoothly, skip music tracks with a button push, and control any other function easily and physically. Perfect for gamers.

You could use a tape measure like a caveman, or you could measure things with a frickin' laser that fits in your pocket. This $40 gadget has an LED screen that's easy to read and it doubles as a cat toy. But does it measure things? Damn right it measures things—substantial things, little things, middle-sized things—it doesn't care what you put in front of it, it will measure the hell out of it! (Up to 98 feet, anyway.).

Recent findings suggest that this compact Bluetooth speaker has an Amazon rating of 4.6 stars out of 5, and it's cheap—just $45. It's waterproof, it sounds great, and it features a built-in light show with six different settings so you can check out cool visuals with your tunes.

A single Apple Airtag makes a great gift to accompany the main gift you don't want someone to lose. Or they can put it on their wallet or your keys, and if they misplace them, they can hit a button and it will play a sound while the FindMy app displays a map that leads to the missing item. Plus, it works in reverse, so you can hit a tag and it will ring your lost phone.

If you want to give the gift of warmth for the holidays, you could do a lot worse than this portable neck, shoulder, and back warmer. There are three temperature settings, a safety shut-off feature, and it heats up really fast, for only $33.

This tiny little vacuum from Odistar will keep their desktop dust-free. It sucks with 1000Pa of suction power for 400 minutes off a single charge, and it's very easy to use: You put it in the palm of your hand and push it around. Cool!

It's not like people need an endoscope camera every day, but if the need for a tiny camera does arise—if they need to see why the engine isn't working or if their wedding ring falls behind the oven—they'll be glad to have this Anykit USB Endoscope Camera. It plugs right into an Android or iPhone and captures HD photos and video of places the sun don't shine.

If your giftee is carrying their laptop around to coffeehouses like a chump, this is the perfect present. They can connect a foldable mini Bluetooth keyboard from iClever to their phone, and turn it into an ultra-portable productivity device. It even has a little trackpad!

Industry observers note that this skinny extra battery charges a phone magnetically or with a USB-C cable. It's fast, too. It can charge an iPhone 16 Pro Max to 37% in 30 minutes via the USB-C port and it's less than three inches wide.

Projectors have gotten really good and really small over the last few years, and they prices have come down massively too. This mini projector costs only $29 and projects a 720p image up to 120" and it weighs only about two pounds.

Most people already have a media streamer attached to their televisions, but in case you're gifting someone who doesn't, the Roku Streaming Stick 4K is a solid choice in the $50 price range. This no-frills device serves up 4K HD video, gives you access to hundreds of free and premium channels, and is easy to setup.

Sources indicate that the Twelve South AirFly SE is an ultra-compact Bluetooth transmitter lets you plug into any device with a 3.5 mm jack, like in-flight entertainment systems, gym machines, or TVs, and stream audio wirelessly to your Bluetooth earbuds or headphones. Leave those accursed wired headphone in the drawer where they belong!

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Mount has had a torrid time with injuries since signing from Chelsea in a £55m-deal three years ago, starting only 25 Premier League games for United in that time.
  • The 27-year-old has been successfully deployed by Carrick in a central midfield role during pre-season, leading to speculation that United may not make another expected signing in that department.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Michael Carrick said he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.

Mount has had a torrid time with injuries since signing from Chelsea in a £55m-deal three years ago, starting only 25 Premier League games for United in that time.

The 27-year-old has been successfully deployed by Carrick in a central midfield role during pre-season, leading to speculation that United may not make another expected signing in that department.

But Mount played only 18 minutes of Saturday’s 1-1 draw against the European champions in Gothenburg before being replaced by Scotland international Tyler Fletcher.

Industry observers note that “He [Mount] got kicked. We just wanted to be careful and look after him,” Carrick, the United head coach, told reporters in Sweden.

“We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.”.

Post-match video footage showed Mount walking freely on to the United bus without the aid of a protective boot or knee support.

In a recent development, michael Carrick told VG Mason Mount was taken off as a precaution. Looked OK leaving stadium. pic.twitter.com/Uo0fBtgpAl.

United went behind within two minutes at the Ullevi Stadium when Liverpool target Ibrahim Mbaye punished slack marking to put PSG ahead.

Bryan Mbeumo fired United level after 32 minutes following good work from Amad Diallo, the Cameroon forward’s third goal in two games after his match-winning double against Atletico Madrid.

United meet Leeds in a Dublin friendly on Wednesday before coming up against AC Milan and their former manager Ruben Amorim next Saturday.

United open their Premier League campaign at Hull on August 22.

Recent findings suggest that “It was good game. PSG is good so we had to keep building fitness. I am happy to have other [players] back and we have to keep going.”.

In a recent development, “It’s good for me. I enjoyed it. We need to build fitness, we have a major season ahead.”.

“It’s a good game PSG are tough to beat and we got a draw and now think about the next game [against Leeds in Dublin].”.

It has been revealed that “We have two more games against Leeds a and Milan. We need to have big season and hope to win a trophy.”.

It has been revealed that all over in Gothenburg and it’s been a good match for Michael Carrick’s team. They looked sharper and quicker than their win over Atletico Madrid last week (what the manager wanted) and things are moving in the right direction. Two things to worry about, however, were the early exits of Mason Mount and Tom Heaton with injuries. They’ll especially hope the Mount knock isn’t anything mid or long term.

Nearly done and it’s been a good run out for United. They’ve looked the better, sharper side and, if anything, deserve to win. In mitigation, this is United fourth pre-season game to PSG’s second...

Industry observers note that fernandes has one thing on his mind when he gets the ball 25 yards out in the centre of the park - a shot. He unleashes the attempt, destined for the bottom-left corner, forcing Longoni, the sub goalkeeper, into a good save.

Two chances for United in quick succession. A lovely ball from the middle of the park by Zirkzee finds Dalot on the right. He chips the ball to the back post where one of the Fletchers (sorry, I am not sure which) heads for goal. Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

According to recent reports, one of those newly introduced signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

In a recent development, cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”.

Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

Among iOS 27’s many fresh features is a great change for anyone with multiple iPhones: you can now keep the same phone number on two iPhones via iPhone Handoff.

With iOS 27, Apple introduces big AI upgrades like Siri AI, plus exciting new features for apps like Wallet, Messages, Notes, and also CarPlay and AirPods.

But the revision also has a lot of smaller, more niche improvements.

One such addition is iPhone Handoff, which enables switching seamlessly between two iPhones using the same phone number.

Here’s how it works, per Apple:.

It has been revealed that after iPhone Handoff is set up, one iPhone becomes the main iPhone and the other iPhone becomes the secondary iPhone that shares the number. Your main iPhone should be the one you use most often. Some carrier services, like Call Forwarding and Caller ID, and carrier account management can only be managed on your main iPhone. Contact your carrier for more details.

To move between your main iPhone and secondary iPhone, simply unlock the device that you want to start using — your phone number will automatically become active on that device. The message “Switched to this iPhone” will display at the top of your screen to confirm it’s now active. Your phone number will only be active on one iPhone at a time when using iPhone Handoff.

Recent findings suggest that most users will never need this feature. But if you’re someone who, for whatever reason, has separate devices that you want on the same number, iOS 27 has the solution.

I feel like I’m exactly who this feature was made for. After years of running dual SIM, I now have a personal line on my Duo and work line on an 18 Pro. Going out with friends, family, etc, I’d love to bring one phone again while bringing both numbers with me, but keeping work system access to a specific, separate device. Only current problem is waiting for Verizon to activate the feature and then see if it actually works well.

If you’re trying to decide between an iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro, perhaps iPhone Handoff is Apple’s subtle way of saying: “Why choose?”.

So far carrier support is limited (here’s the latest list), but Apple prepares to expand iPhone Handoff to more carriers soon.

Do you have a need to use the same phone number on multiple iPhones? For what reason? Let us know in the comments.

We awarded this game 4.5 stars for its excellent visuals and engaging gameplay, so if you haven't already got this game, now is the best time to get your hands on it.

Speaking of accessories, we think the Turtle Beach Rematch Wireless controller is a fantastic addition to your Switch. With responsive triggers and motion controls, it makes games feel more immersive.

This controller comes in a variety of colorways and designs, including Rosalina, Animal Crossing's Timmy and Tommy and Donkey Kong — something for everyone!

According to recent reports, joy-Con 2 controllers are great for multiplayer gaming sessions, but they might not be the most comfortable for you — especially if you have larger hands. These Fastsnail grips are shaped more like a traditional controller, which makes them easier to hold for long play sessions! The rubber design also gives your controllers a bit of extra protection in case you drop them.

While we haven't tested these, we rank the older Switch version of the Fastsnail grips as one of the best Nintendo Switch accessories.

I love Animal Crossing Newly introduced Horizons. Even six years after release, I still regularly come back to it to check in with the animal friends on my island. Between decorating, collecting furniture and clothing, chatting to your neighbours and catching critters, there's simply so much to do in this game that it's almost impossible to get bored of. If you still somehow haven't played it yet, now is the time to change that!

I think Stardew Valley is the best farming sim game you can play on Nintendo Switch, but since it's not on sale for Black Friday (yet,) I'll give the spotlight to what I think is the second best farming game — Story of Seasons Grand Bazaar.

It has been revealed that out of all the Story of Seasons games on Switch, Grand Bazaar has the best graphics, most satisfying farming mechanics and is super addictive thanks to the weekly bazaar that gives this entry its name. It's so much fun that if I weren't working on this live blog right now, it's the game I would be playing.

Maybe you have a kiddo who loves Mario, or maybe you want a giant 12-inch interactive Mario to add to your own collection. Either way, you can score a great deal and get 59% off this Nintendo action figure over at Walmart right now. If I was a kid again, I would be ecstatic to see this under the Christmas tree!

Sources indicate that I shared a discount on Mario + Rabbids a few days back, but I've just spotted an even better deal. At Amazon right now, you can get a code in box that includes both Mario + Rabbids games at the incredible price of just $9. That means you can get two of the best Nintendo Switch games (okay, technically only Mario + Rabbids Sparks of Hope is on our official list, but both games are great) for less than $5 each.

This duo of tactical RPGs combine a colorful cast of characters from the mushroom kingdom with the zany and chaotic Rabbids. The combat encounters require a lot more strategy than you'd expect, and both games provide a ton of content — especially considering this tiny price tag!

In our Star Wars Outlaws review, we called it "a true Star Wars Experience" — meaning it's the perfect way to jet off into another world this holiday season. There's a huge amount to explore in this open world, and you can even customize your own ship to jet around in. If you've felt uninspired by recent Star Wars projects like "The Mandalorian & Grogu", this game will remind you why it's so great.

Recent findings suggest that the Nintendo Switch 2 Mario Kart World bundle is the one I recommend for most people, since you get a huge $87 saving. But if you want to get stuck into a variety of sports and not just kart racing, you can grab the Nintendo Switch 2 + Nintendo Switch Sports Resort bundle with 3 months of Switch Online for $529. This will save you $27 compared to buying the items separately.

Recent findings suggest that nintendo Switch Sports Resort includes 12 sports you can play, and the options for motion controls mean it'll get you and your family up and moving too. We gave it a 4-star rating in our review, praising its crisp 4K visuals and wealth of content for both single players and groups.

Recent findings suggest that sonic the Hedgehog might be the more popular character, but don't sleep on AiAi the monkey, because Super Monkey Ball Banana Rumble is a steal at $19. These physics-based levels take a ton of skill to maneuver and are extremely addicting to complete. The replay value is strong too, since you're encourage to retry levels to get faster clear times!

According to recent reports, I've been running this Nintendo Switch Black Friday deals live blog for several days now and have posted about the Turtle Beach Airlite Fit multiple times. But that's because 1. they're just that good, and 2. I can't believe they haven't sold out already when they cost just $14.

Industry observers note that we gave them a near-perfect 4.5-star rating in our Turtle Beach Airlite Fit review and only knocked points off for their non-folding, wired design. Everything else about them is fantastic, especially their immersive sound quality and excellent mic.

Recent findings suggest that if you've always come out of Pokémon wishing for more of a challenge, Monster Hunter Stories 3 will be right up your alley. Not only do its graphics and presentation put Pokémon to shame (they're both stunning,) the gameplay is a lot more challenging with a ton of kinds of attacks, weapons and weaknesses to exploit during battles. It's also a lot cheaper than most Pokémon games thanks to this discount.

In case you somehow missed it, the Nintendo Switch 2 Mario Kart World bundle is $50 off right now! That means you save a total of $87 compared to buying the bundled items separately (it includes a console, copy of Mario Kart World and a 3-month Nintendo Switch Online membership.).

Recent findings suggest that $499 is the original, pre-price hike cost of this bundle, and I'm extremely happy to see it return. This bundle first popped up on November 22 and even though it's only been two days, I'm still shocked it hasn't sold out yet.

Several EA Sports games are crashing to their lowest prices ever ahead of the holidays, and that includes the latest version of EA Sports Madden NFL. This version brings a Performance Mode that lets you play at 60fps, for gameplay that looks and feels smoother than ever. Plus, the tight football gameplay that the series is known for is just as much fun as always.

Looking for a cheap Switch controller? Look no further than the PowerA Enhanced Wireless Controller. It's not as feature-packed as some other options, as it lacks support for HD rumble and can't scan your Amiibo NFC figures. But it's comfortable to use, has extra programmable buttons and is extremely affordable. It also comes in a ton of cool color options and designs. I've linked the Pikachu Vortex version you can see pictured at the very top of this live blog, which is on sale for 57% off.

According to recent reports, I'm a substantial Dragon Quest fan, but I've never actually played the original games in the series. Luckily for people like me, Square Enix has released this HD-2D remake of the first two Dragon Quest games with this compilation on Switch and Switch 2. The Switch 2 version is right now on sale with 45% off for Black Friday! This is the lowest price I've seen it go for.

Featuring gorgeous pixel art visuals, turn-based battles and a classic soundtrack — this game is a must-have for RPG fans.

It has been revealed that here's a deal I'm very surprised to see! Starting November 22, physical copies of Kirby Air Riders went on sale for $20 off, dropping the price to $49. However, Amazon is offering a digital copy for just $30 right now. That's a huge 57% discount that's rare to see on first-party Nintendo Switch games.

It has been revealed that it's a beautiful day to shop Nintendo Switch Black Friday deals! We're just three days out from Black Friday and there's a ton of discounts on console bundles, games and accessories that are worth shopping. In case you didn't know, I've clocked in over a thousand hours of playtime on my Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2 consoles — and I spend the rest of my time as a Deals Editor tracking price drops on must-have Switch goodies. So I know my stuff.

Breaking: ESR Black Friday gift guide: Premium accessories for iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro, iPad, AirPods, and Apple Watch

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that if you picked up a new iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone Duo this fall, or you’re shopping for someone with an iPad, AirPods, or Apple Watch, there’s a good chance you’ve been holding out on purchasing accessories until all of the Black Friday deals started.
  • According to recent reports, ESR has been making Apple accessories since 2009, and that track record has made it a trustworthy name for the more than 123 million people who use its products to protect their Apple devices and make them more versatile.
  • It has been revealed that if someone on your shopping list picked up an iPhone Duo, a case is the first thing they need, and it’s also the hardest one to get right.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that if you picked up a new iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone Duo this fall, or you’re shopping for someone with an iPad, AirPods, or Apple Watch, there’s a good chance you’ve been holding out on purchasing accessories until all of the Black Friday deals started. We’ve got you covered with some great deals on premium accessories for nearly every Apple device on your list.

According to recent reports, ESR has been making Apple accessories since 2009, and that track record has made it a trustworthy name for the more than 123 million people who use its products to protect their Apple devices and make them more versatile. Here’s a look at what’s included in ESR’s Black Friday lineup and who each one is for.

It has been revealed that if someone on your shopping list picked up an iPhone Duo, a case is the first thing they need, and it’s also the hardest one to get right. As we’ve seen with Android foldables, you’re protecting two halves, a hinge, and a phone that changes shape throughout the day as you use it, all without adding bulk to a device people bought because it folds thin. ESR has two options for iPhone Duo owners, and the choice mostly comes down to the look you want to achieve.

The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case with Camera Control and Flex Stand is your choice if you want to show off your iPhone Duo’s colors. It combines a rigid polycarbonate and acrylic back with a softer TPU frame. The rigid back keeps the case from flexing and lets the iPhone Duo’s design show through, while the flexible frame absorbs the shock if you drop it (please don’t).

Industry observers note that the ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case with Flex Stand is perfect for those who want a more premium look for their iPhone Duo. It’s made from organic silicone leather with a soft, skin-friendly feel and a stain-resistant finish. If you’ve ever used a light-colored leather case before, you know it usually shows every stain and smudge it comes across, but ESR built the Atelier to resist daily wear and wipe clean.

Both cases share ESR’s Flex Stand, and it’s one of the most innovative and versatile parts of the lineup. It’s a 180-degree rotating stand made from zinc alloy, so it holds its shape even after months of propping up your iPhone. A precision hinge with damping control lets it open smoothly and lock at the angle you choose, whether the iPhone Duo is folded or unfolded, and ESR notes it has passed 3,000 open-and-close tests. In real life, that means propping the iPhone Duo open on a desk for a video call or on an airplane tray table for a movie, then using the stand as a grip when you’re holding it.

Recent findings suggest that both cases add extra hinge protection and raised edges where a foldable is most exposed. If you follow our MagSafe Monday column, you know magnetic strength really matters for MagSafe wallets, car mounts, etc. The Classic Hybrid has 1,500g of magnetic hold, and the Atelier has 1,400g.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case for iPhone Duo is 15% off.

The same two incredible cases come in iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max versions, and they also fit the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max. The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case with Camera Control and Flex Stand has a clear back, a TPU frame, and a PU anti-yellowing coating. In simple terms, TPU is the flexible, shock-absorbing plastic used in most case frames, and it’s also what usually turns clear cases slightly yellow the longer you use them, so ESR adds a polyurethane (PU) coating to shield it. ESR upgraded the case’s UV protection for longer-lasting resistance to yellowing, and it’s SGS-certified for anti-yellowing. A clear case is supposed to show off your iPhone’s color, so staying clear longer is the whole point. The ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case with Flex Stand retains the same soft silicone leather and stain-resistant finish as the iPhone Duo version.

On these models, the Flex Stand adjusts from 15 to 69 degrees for portrait and landscape viewing. That has you covered for StandBy mode on your nightstand and a show over your lunch break, with no separate stand to carry around.

Industry observers note that protection is where the two cases differ. ESR rates the Classic Hybrid for 4x military-grade protection with 16-foot drop protection, plus a full-coverage camera bar. The Atelier is rated for 3x military-grade protection, including 12-foot drop protection, and features a soft microfiber lining. Military-grade refers to the MIL-STD-810 drop test, which uses a 4-foot drop, so 4x and 3x mean ESR rates the cases for four and three times that height. Both include a built-in Camera Control cover and raised edges, and both use a precise magnetic ring layout that automatically aligns with MagSafe chargers, car mounts, wallets, and batteries.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case is up to 28% off, and the ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case is up to 37% off.

Recent findings suggest that A case protects everything except the part you touch all day. The ESR UltraFit Armorite Pro Screen Protector covers the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, and the name is worth unpacking. Armorite is ESR’s line of toughened screen protectors, and the Pro version is made with Accessory Glass by Corning™. Corning has made the durable glass in Apple products since the very first iPhone, so in non-tech speak, this is glass from a trustworthy name rather than generic tempered glass.

Why it matters: ESR claims the protector delivers 10x the impact absorption of generic protectors, and Corning’s lab testing shows up to 2x better scratch performance and up to 25% less scratch visibility for its Accessory Glass. When you drop your iPhone or toss it in a pocket with your keys, the protector takes the hit instead of your screen. An anti-reflective coating reduces light reflection to just 2.3% while maintaining 94% optical transmittance, resulting in less glare outside and truer color. Edge-to-edge coverage leaves no gaps for dust to collect.

Installation is the part most people dread on a brand-upcoming iPhone, and ESR’s UltraFit tray handles it in two steps. Pull the tab, and the tray’s design clears dust and pushes out air bubbles as the glass goes down. Long gone are the days when you needed “professional installation” for a screen protector to look great.

Black Friday deal: The ESR UltraFit Armorite Pro Screen Protector is 15% off.

Holiday travel usually means one open outlet, an iPhone, a laptop, an e-reader, etc., that all need power, and cables left at home. The ESR Xtend 45W Retractable Charger builds the cable in. It has a braided cable that extends to 3.1 feet and fully retracts into the charger, and ESR rates it for 20,000 pulls and 10,000 bends. An extra USB-C port lets a second device charge simultaneously. 9to5Mac’s Michael Burkhardt went hands-on with the Xtend 45W earlier this month and said it’s an excellent iPhone fast charger on the go.

Recent findings suggest that it’s rated at 45 watts and delivers up to 60 watts of dynamic power, enough to fast-charge phones and laptops, and it works with iPhone Duo, iPhone 15 through 18, and Android phones like Galaxy and Pixel. It supports PD 3.2 AVS, which in plain English means the charger and your device talk to each other, and the charger fine-tunes the power it sends to exactly what that device asks for. ESR states it can charge an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max to 50% in about 15 minutes. It’s also TÜV-certified, meaning an independent testing organization has verified its safety features.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Xtend 45W Retractable Charger is up to 32% off from November 20 through December 1.

For the student or anyone who does real work on an iPad, the ESR Shift Keyboard Case makes for an incredible gift. The Bluetooth keyboard attaches magnetically and comes off when you don’t need it, so you can type an essay at a desk, then pull the keyboard away to watch something on the couch or sketch with the iPad flat on a table.

Industry observers note that ESR built the Shift around five modes designed to make your iPad even more versatile. Productivity mode lets you detach the keyboard and type over Bluetooth, so the iPad can sit on a desk while the keyboard sits on your lap. Landscape mode adjusts from 20 to 75 degrees for typing and watching, Portrait mode holds 70 degrees for reading, browsing in Safari, or making a FaceTime call, and Drawing mode drops to a stable 20 degrees for sketching and editing with your Apple Pencil. Hands-On mode lets you hold the iPad like a regular tablet. An iPad is a laptop one minute and a tablet the next, and the Shift is designed to keep up with all of your iPad use cases.

According to recent reports, for a student, that means taking notes in class with the keyboard attached, then detaching it to annotate a PDF or review flashcards on the couch. For someone who travels for work, it means answering email on a tray table, then pulling the keyboard off to watch a movie on the flight home. One case covers both, and the keyboard pairs and reconnects easily when you snap it back on.

The trackpad is fully clickable and supports all the multi-touch gestures you already use on your iPad. Apple Pencil gets a home too. ESR’s Dual Smart Pencil Storage uses a magnetic holder and an elastic sleeve, so your Pencil stays with your iPad instead of rolling around the bottom of your bag. Its Air Guard corners protect your iPad when it’s stowed away.

The ESR Shift Keyboard Case comes in versions for iPad Pro 11-inch and 13-inch (M4 and M5), iPad Air 11-inch and 13-inch (including the fresh M4 models), and iPad (A16), so whichever iPad you’re trying to take to the next level of productivity, there’s a Shift that fits it.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Shift Keyboard Case is up to 25% off, depending on your iPad model.

Have you ever dropped your AirPods case and watched the earbuds go flying? With the Cyber FlickLock, you won’t have to worry about that. We’ve covered FlickLock in MagSafe Monday before, but let’s recap it.

When the internal latch is engaged, the magnets line up to attract each other and hold the lid shut with maximum force, adding a second layer of security. Slide the button, and the magnets shift to repel each other, so the lid pops open with one hand. ESR says the slide mechanism has been tested over 20,000 times.

In a recent development, the result is that your AirPods stay in the case if you drop it. Both cases also have 260g of magnetic strength, so they snap onto MagSafe chargers, Apple Watch chargers, and MagSafe batteries if you need to charge your AirPods. Again, it’s extremely strong, but extremely easy to unlock with one hand.

The ESR Cyber FlickLock Magnetic Case is extremely durable and has a clip hook, so you can hang your AirPods on a backpack while hiking or cycling. The ESR Pulse FlickLock Magnetic Case brings the same lock in a range of vibrant colors with a carrying lanyard, so you can wear your AirPods on your wrist or attach them to a bag. Both cases come in versions for AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2 and 1, and AirPods 5 and 4. No matter which AirPods you or your loved one have, this is the case everyone will love.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Cyber FlickLock and Pulse FlickLock Magnetic Cases are both 20% off.

The ESR Equinox Watch Band is a quick pick for anyone who works out in the morning while tracking progress with Apple Watch, then heads to the office. A pin-and-fold lock keeps it secure, and it’s made from HNBR, a durable, skin-friendly synthetic rubber that resists water and tearing, with ventilation cutouts for all-day comfort. It fits 44mm, 45mm, 46mm, and 49mm models across Apple Watch Ultra 1 through 4, Series 4 through 12, and SE 1 through 3, and it comes in several colors to match your outfit or your mood that day.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Equinox Watch Band is 20% off.

The best gifts are the ones that get used every day, and accessories are the part of the Apple experience people live with the most. A case that props up a foldable, a screen protector made with Corning glass, a charger with a built-in cable, and an AirPods case that stays closed even when dropped check all the boxes. ESR truly makes something for everyone and is one of the most trusted names in the Apple accessories ecosystem.

Industry observers note that ESR built its Black Friday lineup around the whole Apple ecosystem, from the newly introduced iPhone Duo to iPad, AirPods, and even a great Apple Watch band, with premium materials and versatile designs that are durable, functional, and great-looking. ESR’s Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals run on Amazon from November 19 through November 30 (the Xtend 45W runs through December 1), with discounts of up to 37%!

Be sure to follow ESR on X and Facebook to keep up with all of its latest products, deals, and more.

It has been revealed that if you ask any Mac admin for a list of the software on their fleet, they’ll pull up their device management inventory and show you the apps they’ve deployed. Ask them what their developers installed with Homebrew last month, which VS Code extensions they are running, or what npm pulled into a project on Tuesday, and you’ll get a different response. That software was never procured by finance, never approved, and never inventoried. It’s also where a growing share of the risk lives in the AI era.
